parts.name: Basics
parts.title: Orientation and absolute basics
parts.intro: From counting to scientific notation: the exercises start trivially easy and end with estimates about atoms and the universe.

topics.title: Map of mathematics
topics.search: map of mathematics Domain of Science
topics.goal: How the branches of math connect, so you know where each later part fits.
checks: I can name at least five branches of mathematics.
I can say which branches quantum mechanics leans on most.

ex.q: Name the branch for each problem: (a) counting ways to arrange 5 books, (b) the area under a curve, (c) the chance of rain tomorrow, (d) whether a coffee mug and a donut are "the same shape", (e) solving 3 equations in 3 unknowns.
Before Part 3, write one sentence guessing why quantum mechanics needs linear algebra. Keep it and check yourself later.

topics.answerAll: (a) combinatorics, (b) calculus, (c) probability, (d) topology, (e) linear algebra.

topics.title: Map of physics
topics.search: map of physics Domain of Science
topics.goal: The big regions of physics and where quantum mechanics sits among them.
checks: I can place quantum mechanics, relativity and thermodynamics on the map.
I can explain what "quantum gravity" is trying to unify.

ex.q: Name the field of physics behind each: a rainbow, the clock correction in GPS satellites, a fridge, a transistor, a compass needle, a planet's orbit.
ex.a: optics, relativity, thermodynamics, quantum/solid-state physics, electromagnetism, classical mechanics.

ex.q: Which two theories does quantum gravity try to combine?

topics.title: Map of chemistry
topics.search: map of chemistry Domain of Science
topics.goal: How chemistry grows out of physics and leads into biology.
checks: I can explain how chemistry sits between physics and biology.

ex.q: Name the branch of chemistry for: why iron rusts, how a painkiller acts in the body, why salt dissolves in water, designing a better battery.
Which physics theory explains why atoms form bonds at all?

topics.title: Map of quantum physics
topics.search: map of quantum physics Domain of Science
topics.goal: A first overview of every quantum topic in this roadmap.
checks: I can name three things I use every day that rely on quantum mechanics.
I can name the main sub-areas of quantum physics from the map.

ex.q: Before watching, write what you think "quantum" means in one sentence. After watching, rewrite it.
Match each technology to its quantum effect: laser, MRI scanner, transistor, the Sun shining. Effects: tunneling, stimulated emission, nuclear spin, energy bands in solids.
ex.a: laser: stimulated emission; MRI: nuclear spin; transistor: energy bands; Sun: tunneling.

topics.title: The scientific method
topics.goal: Hypothesis, experiment, falsification; why physics trusts experiments over intuition.
checks: I can explain what makes a claim falsifiable.
I can design a simple experiment that could prove a claim wrong.

ex.q: Which claims are falsifiable? (a) Invisible, undetectable dragons live in my garage. (b) All swans are white. (c) Every electron has a charge of −1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
Someone says heavy objects fall faster. Design a test with two balls and a phone camera. What result would prove them wrong?
ex.a: Drop both from the same height; landing together (air resistance aside) falsifies the claim.

ex.q: Why do physicists insist that other labs repeat an experiment before trusting it?
ex.a: To rule out errors and flukes in one setup.

topics.title: Number sets
topics.search: natural numbers integers rational irrational real numbers
topics.goal: Name each number set, give an example, and know each sits inside the next.
checks: I can say which set (natural, integer, rational, irrational, real) any number belongs to.
I can explain why every integer is also rational.

ex.q: Put each number in the smallest set it belongs to: 7, −3, 0.75, 2/3, √2, π, √16, 0.333…, −0.5.
ex.a: 7 natural; −3 integer; 0.75, 2/3, 0.333… and −0.5 rational; √2 and π irrational; √16 = 4 natural.

ex.q: Write 0.272727… as a fraction in lowest terms.
Is there any number between 0.999… and 1? What does that tell you?
Is √−1 in any of these sets? (You will meet it in entry 1.37.)

topics.title: The four operations
topics.search: addition subtraction multiplication division explained visually
topics.goal: Do all four by hand and see multiplication as repeated addition and as area.
checks: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide whole numbers by hand.
I can explain multiplication as repeated addition and as the area of a rectangle.

ex.q: Draw 23 × 14 as a rectangle split into 20 × 10, 20 × 4, 3 × 10 and 3 × 4, and add the four areas.
Add 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100 in under a minute by pairing the first and last numbers (Gauss's trick).
Light travels about 300,000 km every second. How far does it go in one minute?

topics.title: Long multiplication and long division
topics.goal: Multiply and divide multi-digit numbers by hand.
checks: I can multiply two 4-digit numbers on paper.
I can do long division and continue past the decimal point.

ex.q: 100000 ÷ 7 to three decimal places.
Work out 1/7 by long division until the digits repeat. What is the repeating block? Now compute that block × 2 and × 3. What do you notice?
The exact speed of light is 299,792,458 m/s. How many metres does light travel in 60 seconds?

topics.title: Divisibility, even and odd
topics.search: divisibility rules even and odd numbers
topics.goal: Test divisibility by 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10 at a glance.
checks: I can test divisibility by 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10 without dividing.
I can prove that odd × odd is always odd.

ex.q: Is 123456 divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 9?
Is 98765 divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 9?
Is 111111111 divisible by 9?
Is odd + odd even or odd? Odd × odd? Prove both by writing odd numbers as 2k + 1.
Pick any 3-digit number and write it twice, like 247247. Divide by 7, then 11, then 13. Why does it always work? (Hint: 247247 = 247 × 1001.)

topics.title: Order of operations
topics.goal: Evaluate 3 + 4 × 2² correctly (19) and explain why the order is fixed.
checks: I can evaluate expressions with brackets, powers, × ÷ and + − in the right order.
I can explain why −3² and (−3)² differ.

ex.q: −3² and (−3)²
2^3^2, using the convention that stacked powers are read from the top down.
Add brackets to 1 + 2 × 3 + 4 so it equals 21.

topics.title: Negative numbers
topics.goal: Add, subtract and multiply negatives; why negative × negative is positive.
checks: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide with negative numbers.
I can explain why a negative times a negative is positive.

ex.q: It is −18 °C and the temperature rises by 25 degrees. What is it now?
Use 0 = (−1) × (1 + (−1)) and the distributive law to show (−1) × (−1) = 1.
A proton has charge +1 and an electron −1. What is the total charge of 6 protons and 8 electrons? (This is a carbon ion.)

topics.title: Absolute value
topics.goal: Treat \|x\| as distance from zero; solve \|x − 3\| = 2.
checks: I can read |x| as the distance of x from zero.
I can solve simple equations and inequalities with absolute values.

ex.q: Solve |x − 3| = 2.
Solve |x| < 4.
How far apart are −5 and 8 on the number line?
Two electrons sit at −2 nm and 3 nm on a line. How far apart are they?

topics.title: Fractions
topics.goal: Add, multiply and divide fractions; find a common denominator.
checks: I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators.
I can multiply, divide and simplify fractions.

ex.q: Simplify 84/126.
Compute 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16. What do you think the sum approaches if you keep going forever? (You will prove it in entry 1.30.)
Write 3/4 as the sum of two different fractions that each have 1 on top.
A recipe for 4 people uses 2/3 of a cup of rice. How much for 6 people?

topics.title: Decimals and percentages
topics.goal: Convert freely between fractions, decimals and percentages.
checks: I can convert between fractions, decimals and percentages.
I can explain why +20% then −20% does not return to the start.

ex.q: Write 3/8 as a decimal and a percentage.
Write 0.06 as a percentage and as a fraction in lowest terms.
What is 125% of 80?
A price rises 20% and then falls 20%. What is the overall change?
Write 1/3 and 2/9 as decimals.

topics.title: Rounding
topics.goal: Round to a given place value.
checks: I can round to any decimal place or place value.
I can explain why rounding too early causes errors.

ex.q: Round 3.14159 to 2 and to 4 decimal places.
Round 2,718,281 to the nearest thousand.
Round 0.04567 to the nearest hundredth.
Compute 1.4 × 1.4 × 1.4 exactly. Then redo it rounding to one decimal place after each step. How far off is the rounded answer?

topics.title: Primes, GCD and LCM
topics.search: prime factorization greatest common divisor least common multiple
topics.goal: Factor any number into primes; use this to simplify fractions.
checks: I can write any number below 1000 as a product of primes.
I can find the greatest common divisor and least common multiple.

ex.q: Factor 360 into primes.
Find GCD(84, 126) and use it to simplify 84/126.
Find LCM(12, 18).
Is 91 prime?
Two planets line up with their star now. One orbits every 12 years, the other every 18. When do they next line up?
List every prime below 50 using the sieve of Eratosthenes. How many are there?
Why is 1 not counted as a prime?
ex.a: So that prime factorizations are unique.

topics.title: Ratios and proportions
topics.goal: Solve a proportion; tell direct from inverse proportion (crucial for reading physics formulas).
checks: I can solve a proportion.
I can tell direct proportion from inverse proportion and read "∝" in formulas.

ex.q: Solve 3 : 5 = x : 40.
5 m of wire weighs 40 g. How much do 12 m weigh?
4 workers paint a house in 6 hours. How long for 8 workers?
Gravity follows F ∝ 1/r². What happens to the force if the distance doubles? Triples?
Kinetic energy follows E ∝ v². How many times more energy does a car have at 100 km/h than at 50 km/h?
An atom is about 100,000 times wider than its nucleus. If the nucleus were a 1 cm marble, how wide would the atom be?

topics.title: Rates
topics.goal: Use rate = amount ÷ time, for example speed = distance ÷ time.
checks: I can compute and convert rates such as speed.

ex.q: A train covers 150 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
Convert 90 km/h to m/s.
A tap fills 12 L in 3 minutes. How long to fill a 200 L bath?
Sunlight travels 150,000,000 km to reach Earth at 300,000 km/s. How many minutes does it take?
Hair grows about 1.25 cm per month. How many nanometres per second is that? (1 cm = 10,000,000 nm; take a month as 30 days.)

topics.title: Averages
topics.goal: Compute and compare the three kinds of average.
checks: I can compute mean, median and mode.
I can say when the median is fairer than the mean.

ex.q: Find the mean, median and mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 10.
Five incomes (in thousands): 30, 30, 40, 50, 1000. Find the mean and median. Which describes a typical person better?
What is the average roll of a fair six-sided die? Can you ever roll it? (Quantum "expectation values" behave the same way.)
Your test scores are 70, 80 and 90. What do you need on the fourth test to average 85?

topics.title: Exponents
topics.goal: Use aᵐ·aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ, a⁰ = 1 and a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ without hesitation.
checks: I can use all the exponent rules, including zero and negative powers.
I know when terms with powers can and cannot be combined.

ex.q: 2³ × 2⁴
(3²)³
5⁰ and 2⁻³
x⁵ ÷ x²
Simplify (2a³b)² × 3a⁻²b.
Is 2³ + 2³ equal to 2⁶? If not, what is it as a single power of 2?
Simplify 3x² + 5x² and 3x² + 5x³ (if possible).
A sheet of paper is 0.1 mm thick. If you could fold it in half 42 times, how thick would it be? Compare with the distance to the Moon (384,400 km). Use 2⁴² ≈ 4.4 × 10¹².
A chessboard has 1 grain of rice on the first square, 2 on the next, 4, 8, and so on. How many grains on the 64th square?

topics.title: Roots
topics.search: square roots and nth roots fractional exponents
topics.goal: Read √a as a^(1/2); simplify roots.
checks: I can read √a as a^(1/2) and ∛a as a^(1/3).
I can simplify roots and explain why √(a + b) ≠ √a + √b.

ex.q: Simplify √50.
Test √(9 + 16) against √9 + √16.
Solve x² = 81 (both answers).
A pendulum's period grows like √(length). How much longer must a pendulum be to tick half as often?

topics.title: Squares, cubes and reciprocals
topics.goal: Recognize squares up to 20², cubes up to 10³, and reciprocals 1/x.
checks: I know squares up to 20² and cubes up to 10³.
I can find reciprocals of simple numbers and decimals.

ex.q: Square numbers ending in 5 by a trick: for 35², multiply 3 × 4 = 12 and append 25. Use it for 15², 65² and 85².
6³ and 9³
Show that 1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³ (Ramanujan's taxicab number).

topics.title: Scientific notation
topics.goal: Write and multiply numbers like 6.02 × 10²³ and 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹.
checks: I can write very large and very small numbers in scientific notation.
I can multiply and divide them by handling the powers of ten separately.

ex.q: Write 602,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 in scientific notation.
Write 0.000052 in scientific notation.
An atom is about 10⁻¹⁰ m wide and its nucleus about 10⁻¹⁵ m. What fraction of the atom's volume is nucleus? (Volume grows as width³.)
One electron carries 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. How many electrons make 1 C?
Your body holds about 7 × 10²⁷ atoms. Counting one per second, how many years would counting take? Compare with the age of the universe, 1.38 × 10¹⁰ years. (One year ≈ 3.15 × 10⁷ s.)
ex.a: About 2.2 × 10²⁰ years, roughly 16 billion times the age of the universe.

topics.title: Binary and number bases
topics.goal: Count in binary; know why a bit is 0 or 1 (qubits come later).
checks: I can convert between binary and decimal.
I can say how many values n bits can store.

ex.q: Count from 0 to 8 in binary.
Convert 1011 (binary) to decimal.
Convert 25 to binary.
Add 1101 + 0110 in binary, then check in decimal.
How many different values do 8 bits hold? n bits?
Describing n qubits takes 2ⁿ numbers. Roughly how many numbers for 300 qubits? Compare with the roughly 10⁸⁰ atoms in the observable universe. (Use 2¹⁰ ≈ 10³.)
ex.a: About 10⁹⁰, more than the number of atoms in the universe.

ex.q: Convert the hexadecimal number FF to decimal.

topics.title: Orders of magnitude and Fermi estimates
topics.search: orders of magnitude and estimation Fermi problems
topics.goal: Estimate any quantity to the nearest power of ten.
checks: I can estimate a quantity to the nearest power of ten from rough assumptions.

ex.q: About how many times does a heart beat in an 80-year life? (Assume 70 beats per minute.)
How many seconds are in a year? Compare with π × 10⁷.
Give the order of magnitude of the number of people on Earth and the mass of a car in kg.
A sheet of paper is about 0.1 mm thick and an atom about 0.1 nm wide. How many atoms thick is the paper?

topics.title: Powers of Ten
topics.goal: Feel the scale from 10⁻¹⁶ m (inside a proton) to 10²⁴ m (galaxy clusters).
checks: I can place everyday and cosmic objects on a powers-of-ten scale.

ex.q: Order these by size and give each a power of ten in metres: Earth, a proton, a city, an atom, a cell, the Milky Way, you, the solar system.
ex.a: proton 10⁻¹⁵, atom 10⁻¹⁰, cell 10⁻⁵, you 10⁰, city 10⁴, Earth 10⁷, solar system 10¹³, Milky Way 10²¹.

ex.q: How many powers of ten separate a proton (10⁻¹⁵ m) from the Milky Way (10²¹ m)?
Which surprised you more: the empty space between stars, or the empty space inside atoms? Why?

topics.title: Scale of the universe
topics.search: scale of the universe from quarks to cosmos
topics.goal: Place an atom (10⁻¹⁰ m), a nucleus (10⁻¹⁵ m) and a cell (10⁻⁵ m) on that scale.
checks: I can place an atom, a nucleus, a cell and a wavelength of light on one scale.

ex.q: A hair is about 10⁻⁴ m wide. How many atoms (10⁻¹⁰ m) fit across it?
How many cells (10⁻⁵ m) fit side by side in 1 cm?
If an atom were blown up to the size of a 100 m stadium, how big would the nucleus be?
Visible light has a wavelength of about 5 × 10⁻⁷ m. How many atoms wide is one wavelength? Why can't an ordinary microscope show atoms?
ex.a: About 5,000 atoms; light is far too coarse to resolve atoms.

topics.title: SI units and prefixes
topics.search: SI base units and metric prefixes
topics.goal: Know the 7 base units (m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd) and the prefixes from femto to tera.
checks: I know the 7 base units and the prefixes from femto to tera.
I can write derived units such as the newton and joule in base units.

ex.q: Give the base unit for mass, electric current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.
Convert 3.2 GHz to Hz, 500 nm to m, and 1 fm to nm.
Write the newton and the joule in base units.
Since 2019 the kilogram is defined through Planck's constant h, measured in J·s. Write the units of h in kg, m and s.

topics.title: Unit conversion and dimensional analysis
topics.goal: Convert units by multiplying by 1; check a formula by its units alone.
checks: I can convert units by multiplying by fractions equal to 1.
I can reject a formula whose units do not match.

ex.q: Convert 72 km/h to m/s.
A light-year is the distance light travels in a year. Estimate it in km using 3 × 10⁵ km/s and 3.15 × 10⁷ s.
Check that E = mc² gives joules. Is "distance = speed × time²" possible?
A pendulum's period T can only depend on its length L (m) and g (m/s²). Combine them to get seconds.
Challenge: show that √(ħG/c³) has units of metres. Units: ħ in kg·m²/s, G in m³/(kg·s²), c in m/s. (This is the Planck length, Part 22.)
ex.a: The product ħG/c³ has units m², so its root is in m.

topics.title: Significant figures and uncertainty
topics.goal: Report a measurement with sensible precision and an error bar.
checks: I can count significant figures and round results sensibly.
I can tell whether two measurements with error bars agree.

ex.q: How many significant figures in 0.00450 and 3.0 × 10⁸?
Compute 2.5 × 3.14159 to the right number of significant figures.
A table is 1.82 m ± 0.01 m long. What range of lengths is allowed?
Two labs measure g as 9.79 ± 0.03 and 9.86 ± 0.02 m/s². Do they agree?
ex.a: No; the ranges do not overlap.

ex.q: The electron's magnetic moment has been measured to about 13 significant figures. Why is matching that with theory such a strong test?
ex.a: A tiny mistake in the theory would show up as a mismatch.

topics.title: Reading graphs
topics.goal: Read slope, intercept and area off any graph, including log axes.
checks: I can read slope and area from a graph and say what they mean physically.
I can read a logarithmic axis.

ex.q: A position-time graph is a straight line from (0 s, 0 m) to (4 s, 20 m). What is the speed?
A velocity-time graph is flat at 10 m/s for 3 s. What distance does the area under it give?
On a logarithmic axis, what number lies halfway between 1 and 100?
Sketch y = x, y = x² and y = 2ˣ for x from 0 to 10. Which is largest at x = 10?
Each step on the Richter scale is 10 times the shaking. How much more shaking is a magnitude 7 earthquake than a magnitude 5?

topics.title: The Greek alphabet
topics.search: Greek alphabet in math and physics
topics.goal: Recognize and name ψ, φ, λ, ω, ħ, Δ, Σ, ∂, ∇ and the rest on sight.
checks: I can write and name all 24 Greek letters.
I know what the common ones usually mean in physics.

ex.q: Write the Greek alphabet from memory, lower and upper case.
Name each symbol and its usual physics meaning: λ, ω, ψ, ħ, Δ, Σ, ρ, θ, ν, τ.
ex.a: lambda: wavelength; omega: angular frequency; psi: wavefunction; h-bar: reduced Planck constant; Delta: change or uncertainty; Sigma: sum; rho: density; theta: angle; nu: frequency; tau: lifetime or torque.

ex.q: Read aloud: Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2.
ex.a: "Delta x times delta p is at least h-bar over two."

topics.title: Mathematical notation
topics.search: how to read mathematical notation symbols
topics.goal: Read ∑, ∏, ≈, ∝, ∈, ∀, ⇒, subscripts and superscripts aloud.
checks: I can read sums, products and logic symbols aloud.
I can translate a sentence into symbols and back.

ex.q: Compute the sum of n² for n = 1 to 5.
Compute the product of k for k = 1 to 4.
Translate into words: for all x in ℝ, x² ≥ 0.
ex.a: Every real number has a non-negative square.

ex.q: What do ≈, ∝, ≡, ⇒ and ⇔ mean?
ex.a: approximately; proportional to; defined as or identical to; implies; if and only if.

ex.q: Write in symbols: "the sum of the first n odd numbers equals n squared". Check it for n = 4.
ex.a: Sum of (2k − 1) for k = 1 to n equals n²; 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16.

parts.name: Algebra to Complex
parts.title: Algebra, geometry, trigonometry, functions, complex numbers
parts.intro: This part ends with the question at the heart of quantum mechanics: why adding complex amplitudes can make probabilities cancel.

topics.title: Variables
topics.search: what is a variable introduction to algebra
topics.goal: Treat letters as unknown or changing numbers.
checks: I can substitute numbers into an expression.
I can turn a sentence into an algebraic expression.

ex.q: If x = 4, evaluate 3x + 2 and x² − x.
Write "five more than twice a number n" as an expression.
A taxi charges 3 € plus 2 € per km. Write the cost for d km, then find the cost for 12 km.
Think of a number, double it, add 10, halve it, then subtract the number you started with. Use algebra to prove you always get the same answer.

topics.title: Linear equations
topics.goal: Isolate x by doing the same thing to both sides.
checks: I can solve any linear equation, including ones with brackets and fractions.

ex.q: Diophantus's riddle: his childhood was 1/6 of his life, his youth 1/12 more, he married after another 1/7, his son was born 5 years later, the son lived half as long as his father, and Diophantus died 4 years after his son. How old was he?

topics.title: Rearranging formulas
topics.goal: Solve v = u + at for t and E = mc² for m.
checks: I can make any variable the subject of a physics formula.

ex.q: Solve v = u + at for t.
Solve E = mc² for m and for c.
Solve KE = ½mv² for v.
Solve 1/f = 1/u + 1/v for v.
Solve F = Gm₁m₂/r² for r.
A photon's energy is E = hc/λ. Solve for λ, then find λ for E = 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J using h = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s and c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s. What colour is that light?

topics.title: Inequalities
topics.goal: Solve inequalities; flip the sign when multiplying by a negative.
checks: I can solve inequalities and flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative.

ex.q: The uncertainty principle says Δx · Δp ≥ ħ/2. If an electron is confined to Δx = 10⁻¹⁰ m, what is the smallest possible Δp? Use ħ = 1.05 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s.

topics.title: Lines and slopes
topics.goal: Read slope as a rate of change in y = mx + b.
checks: I can find the slope and equation of a line from two points.
I can explain what the slope means physically.

ex.q: Find the slope of the line through (1, 3) and (4, 12), then its equation.
A line has slope 1/2 and crosses the y-axis at −2. Where does it cross the x-axis?
Fahrenheit is F = 1.8C + 32. What does the slope 1.8 mean? At what temperature do the two scales show the same number?
What is the slope of a line perpendicular to y = 2x + 1?

topics.title: Systems of linear equations
topics.search: systems of linear equations substitution elimination
topics.goal: Solve 2 equations in 2 unknowns (this becomes matrices later).
checks: I can solve two equations in two unknowns by substitution and by elimination.
I can recognize a system with no solution.

ex.q: x + y = 10 and x − y = 4
2x + 3y = 13 and 4x − y = 5
Adult tickets cost 12 € and child tickets 5 €. 20 tickets cost 156 €. How many of each?
Try to solve x + y = 2 and 2x + 2y = 5. What goes wrong, and what does it look like on a graph?
ex.a: No solution; the lines are parallel.

topics.title: Expanding and factoring
topics.goal: Expand (a + b)² and factor x² − 5x + 6.
checks: I can expand brackets and factor quadratics.
I can use the difference of two squares for mental arithmetic.

ex.q: Expand (a + b)² and (x + 3)(x − 3).
Factor x² − 5x + 6.
Factor 2x² + 7x + 3.
Factor x³ − x completely.
Compute 99 × 101 in your head using (100 − 1)(100 + 1).
Compute 1001² − 999² without a calculator.

topics.title: Quadratic equations
topics.search: completing the square and quadratic formula derivation
topics.goal: Derive and use the quadratic formula; read the discriminant.
checks: I can derive the quadratic formula by completing the square.
I can use the discriminant to predict how many real solutions there are.

ex.q: Derive the quadratic formula from ax² + bx + c = 0.
What does the discriminant say about x² + 2x + 5 = 0? (You will solve it in 1.37.)
A ball's height is h = 20t − 5t² metres. When does it land? When is it highest, and how high?
ex.a: Lands at t = 4 s; highest at t = 2 s, 20 m

ex.q: The golden ratio solves x² = x + 1. Find its positive value.

topics.title: Functions
topics.search: what is a function domain range
topics.goal: Use f(x) notation, domain, range, composition and inverses.
checks: I can compose functions and find inverses.
I can find a function's domain and range.

ex.q: With f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x², find f(g(3)) and g(f(3)).
Find the inverse of f(x) = (x − 3)/2.
Find the domains of √(x − 2) and 1/(x − 5).
Is the circle x² + y² = 1 the graph of a function y(x)? Why not?
ex.a: No: most x give two y values

ex.q: What is the range of x² + 1?

topics.title: Graph transformations
topics.goal: Predict the graph of a·f(b(x − c)) + d.
checks: I can predict how shifting, stretching and flipping change a graph.

ex.q: Describe y = (x − 2)² + 3 compared with y = x².
Describe y = −2 sin x and y = sin 2x compared with y = sin x.
ex.a: Flipped and stretched ×2; squeezed to period π

ex.q: Write the equation of y = x² moved 1 left and 4 down. Where does it cross the x-axis?
A wave shape f(x − vt) moves to the right at speed v. Which way does f(x + vt) move?

topics.title: Parametric equations
topics.goal: Describe a path by x(t), y(t), for example a circle by (cos t, sin t).
checks: I can sketch a curve from x(t) and y(t).
I can eliminate t to get y as a function of x.

ex.q: Sketch x = cos t, y = sin t for t from 0 to 2π.
Sketch x = 2 cos t, y = sin t.
A projectile moves as x = 10t, y = 20t − 5t². Eliminate t to find its path y(x).
Describe the 3D curve x = cos t, y = sin t, z = t/(2π). (A charged particle in a magnetic field moves like this.)
Sketch the Lissajous figure x = sin 3t, y = sin 2t.

topics.title: Polynomials
topics.goal: Sketch a polynomial from its roots and leading term.
checks: I can sketch a polynomial from its roots and leading term.

ex.q: Sketch y = (x + 2)(x − 1)(x − 3). Where does it cross the y-axis?
Describe both ends of the graph of y = −x⁴ + 3x.
Write the polynomial with roots 1, 2 and 3 and leading coefficient 1, fully expanded.
Divide x³ − 1 by x − 1.
How many real roots can a cubic have? Can it have none?

topics.title: Rational functions
topics.goal: Recognize 1/x and 1/r² behaviour (as in gravity and Coulomb's law).
checks: I can find vertical and horizontal asymptotes.

ex.q: Find the asymptotes of y = 1/(x − 2).
Find the asymptotes of y = (2x + 1)/(x − 1).
Compare 1/r and 1/r² at r = 0.1, 1 and 10. Which falls off faster far away? Which is bigger up close?
ex.a: 1/r: 10, 1, 0.1; 1/r²: 100, 1, 0.01. 1/r² falls faster far away and is bigger up close.

topics.title: The inverse square law
topics.goal: Why light intensity, gravity and electric force fall off as 1/r².
checks: I can explain 1/r² as the same amount spread over a sphere of area 4πr².

ex.q: A bulb gives intensity I at 1 m. What is the intensity at 3 m?
Mars is about 1.5 times as far from the Sun as Earth. How strong is sunlight there compared with Earth?
Jupiter is 5.2 times as far. Same question.
How much farther from a radiation source must you move to cut the dose by a factor of 100?

topics.title: Exponential growth and decay
topics.goal: Model half-life and doubling with a·bᵗ.
checks: I can model doubling and half-life with N(t) = N₀ × (1/2)^(t/T).

ex.q: Bacteria double every 20 minutes. Starting from one, how many after 4 hours?
Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5,730 years. What fraction remains after 17,190 years?
A drug leaves the body at 10% per hour. How much of a 200 mg dose remains after 3 hours?
At 1% growth per step, about how many steps until a quantity doubles?

topics.title: Logarithms
topics.goal: Use log rules; read log scales such as decibels and pH.
checks: I can use log rules and solve exponential equations.
I can read decibel and pH scales.

ex.q: log₁₀ 1000, log₂ 32, ln e³
Given log 2 ≈ 0.301, find log 8, log 20 and log 0.5 without a calculator.
Solve 2ˣ = 50.
Each tenfold increase in sound intensity adds 10 dB. How many dB louder is a sound 1000 times more intense?
How many times more acidic is pH 3 than pH 6?
Using 1.13, how long until carbon-14 falls to 10% of its starting amount?

topics.title: Euler's number e

checks: I can explain where e comes from and why the slope of eˣ equals eˣ.

ex.q: Compute (1 + 1/n)ⁿ for n = 1, 2, 10 and 100.
1000 € grows continuously at 5% a year for 10 years: 1000 × e^0.5. How much is it?
Check numerically that (e^1.001 − e)/0.001 is close to e.

topics.title: Exponential vs polynomial growth
topics.goal: Why 2ⁿ eventually beats any power of n (the reason quantum computers matter).
checks: I can explain why 2ⁿ eventually beats any fixed power of n.

ex.q: Fill a table of n³ and 2ⁿ for n = 10, 20 and 50.
Find the first n above 2 where 2ⁿ overtakes n¹⁰ (use logarithms).
Storing the full state of 30 qubits takes about 16 GB. How much for 40 qubits?
In two sentences, explain why this growth is why quantum computers might be powerful.
ex.a: Each added qubit doubles the classical description.

topics.title: Angles, triangles and circles

checks: I know angle sums, circle area and circumference.

ex.q: Two angles of a triangle are 47° and 68°. Find the third.
Find the circumference and area of a circle of radius 5.
What do the interior angles of a hexagon add up to?
Eratosthenes saw the Sun 7.2° from vertical in Alexandria while it was directly overhead in Syene, 800 km south. Use this to estimate Earth's circumference.

topics.title: The Pythagorean theorem
topics.goal: Use a² + b² = c² to find distances between points.
checks: I can prove the theorem with a picture.
I can use it in 2D and 3D.

ex.q: Find the hypotenuse for legs 3 and 4, then 5 and 12.
How far apart are (1, 2) and (7, 10)?
What is the diagonal of a 1 × 1 square?
Find the space diagonal of a 2 × 3 × 6 box.
A 16:9 TV has a 55-inch diagonal. How wide is it?
Your eyes are 2 m above the sea. How far away is the horizon? Earth's radius is 6,371 km. (Draw the right triangle with sides R, d and R + h.)

topics.title: Similar triangles

checks: I can use scale factors for lengths, areas and volumes.

A shape is scaled up 3 times. By what factor do its area and volume grow?
A pinhole camera box is 0.2 m deep. How tall is the image of a 10 m tree 50 m away?

checks: I can use the sphere, cylinder and cone formulas.
I can explain why area scales as L² and volume as L³.

ex.q: Earth's radius is 6,371 km. Find its surface area.
A proton has a radius of about 0.84 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. Find its volume.
The proton's mass is 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. What is its density? How much would a teaspoon (5 × 10⁻⁶ m³) of such matter weigh? (This is the density of a neutron star.)
Double an animal's size in every direction. How do its weight and the strength of its legs (cross-section area) change? Why are elephant legs so thick?
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 and height 10.

topics.title: Radians

checks: I can convert between degrees and radians.
I can use s = rθ for arc length.

How many degrees is 1 radian?
A wheel of radius 0.3 m turns through 2 rad. How far does it roll?
Earth turns 2π rad per day. What is that in rad/s?
Compare sin(0.1) with 0.1. What do you notice?
ex.a: sin(0.1) ≈ 0.0998: for small angles sin θ ≈ θ.

topics.title: Right-triangle trigonometry
topics.search: SOH CAH TOA sine cosine tangent
topics.goal: Find sides and angles of right triangles.
checks: I can find any side or angle of a right triangle.

ex.q: A right triangle has hypotenuse 10 and an angle of 30°. Find the other two sides.
A 5 m ladder makes 60° with the ground. How high does it reach?
Find the angle opposite a side of 3 when the adjacent side is 4.
You stand 50 m from a building and look up 40° to its top. How tall is it?

topics.title: The unit circle

checks: I can read sin θ and cos θ as coordinates on the unit circle.
I know the exact values at π/6, π/4 and π/3.

ex.q: Give sin and cos at 0, π/2, π and 3π/2.
Give exact sin and cos at π/6, π/4 and π/3.
Explain sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 with the Pythagorean theorem.
ex.a: The point (cos θ, sin θ) is 1 from the origin

ex.q: In which quadrants is cos θ negative?
A point goes once around the unit circle every second. Write its x-coordinate as a function of time.

topics.title: Sine waves
topics.search: graphs of sine and cosine amplitude period phase
topics.goal: Read A sin(ωt + φ): amplitude, angular frequency, phase. This is every wave.
checks: I can read amplitude, angular frequency, period and phase from A sin(ωt + φ).

Write a wave with amplitude 0.5 and frequency 440 Hz (the note A).

ex.a: Mirror images; they cancel to zero

ex.q: What do you get when you add sin t to itself?
European mains electricity is 50 Hz. What is its period in milliseconds?

topics.title: Trigonometric identities

checks: I can use the Pythagorean identity and the sum formulas.

Find sin 75° exactly from sin(45° + 30°).
Derive cos 2θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ.
ex.a: From cos(θ + θ) and sin² + cos² = 1

ex.q: Show sin a + sin b = 2 sin((a + b)/2) cos((a − b)/2). (You will use it for beats in 9.7.)
Simplify (1 − cos²θ)/sin θ.

topics.title: Inverse trigonometric functions
topics.goal: Use arcsin, arccos, arctan and their ranges.
checks: I can evaluate arcsin, arccos and arctan and know their ranges.

ex.q: arcsin(1/2), arccos(0), arctan(1)
Why does arcsin only return angles between −π/2 and π/2?
ex.a: So it gives a single answer

ex.q: Find every θ between 0 and 2π with sin θ = 1/2.
If sin θ = 0.5 for a refracted ray, what angle is it in degrees?

topics.title: Polar coordinates

checks: I can convert between (x, y) and (r, θ) in every quadrant.

Convert r = 2, θ = π/3 to (x, y).

ex.q: Sketch r = 1 + cos θ.

topics.title: 3D coordinates

Find their midpoint.
Write the equation of a sphere of radius 2 centred at the origin. Is (1, 1, 1) inside it?

topics.goal: Add vectors tip to tail and split them into components.
checks: I can add vectors, scale them, find their length and split them into components.

A plane flies north at 300 km/h in a 40 km/h east wind. What is its ground speed?
Find the unit vector in the direction of (3, 4).
Split a 10 N force at 30° above horizontal into components.
You walk 3 km east, 4 km north, then 3 km west. Find your displacement and the distance you walked.

checks: I can add matrices and multiply a matrix by a vector.

Multiply [[1, 2], [3, 4]] by the vector (1, 1).
Multiply [[0, −1], [1, 0]] by (1, 0) and by (0, 1). What does this matrix do to the plane?
Multiply [[2, 0], [0, 3]] by (1, 1). Describe what it does.

ex.q: Write 2x + y = 5 and x − y = 1 as a matrix times (x, y), then solve it.

checks: I can identify circles, ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas from their equations.

Which conic does a planet follow? A comet moving faster than escape speed?

ex.a: Multiply S by x and subtract

ex.q: Prove the sum from 0.11 Exercise 6 really approaches 1.
Write 0.999… as a geometric series and sum it.
Zeno: Achilles runs 10 times faster than a tortoise with a 100 m head start. Sum the infinite series of catch-up distances.
Show that 1 + e⁻ˣ + e⁻²ˣ + … = 1/(1 − e⁻ˣ). (Planck used exactly this sum in 1900.)

Why does row n of Pascal's triangle add up to 2ⁿ?

Write the even integers in set-builder notation.
How many subsets does {a, b, c} have? Connect your answer to 0.17b.

ex.q: Prove that √2 is irrational.
Prove there are infinitely many primes.

ex.a: True: a false premise makes the implication true.

Multiply 2e^(iπ/6) by 3e^(iπ/3).
Compute (1 + i)²⁰ using polar form.

ex.q: During which times does it move backwards?
A dropped stone has height x = 20 − 5t². Find its velocity and acceleration.
The third derivative of position is called jerk. Find it for x = t⁴.

topics.title: Optimization
topics.goal: Set the derivative to zero; use the second derivative test.
checks: I can find maxima and minima and confirm them with the second derivative.

ex.q: A rectangle has perimeter 40. What shape gives the largest area?
Cut equal squares of side x from the corners of a 12 × 12 sheet and fold up an open box. Which x gives the largest volume?
Find and classify the stationary points of x³ − 3x.
ex.a: Maximum at x = −1, minimum at x = 1.

ex.q: Light goes from A in air (speed v₁) to B in water (speed v₂). Write the total time as a function of where it crosses the surface and minimize it. Show this gives sin θ₁/v₁ = sin θ₂/v₂ (Snell's law from Fermat's principle).

topics.title: Linear approximation
topics.goal: Use f(x + dx) ≈ f(x) + f′(x)dx.
checks: I can use f(x + dx) ≈ f(x) + f′(x) dx and (1 + x)ⁿ ≈ 1 + nx.

ex.q: Estimate √101.
Estimate 1.002¹⁰⁰, then compare with a calculator.
In relativity, γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) ≈ 1 + v²/(2c²). Estimate γ for v = 0.1c.
A pendulum swings to 5°. How large is the error in using sin θ ≈ θ?

topics.title: L'Hôpital's rule
topics.goal: Evaluate 0/0 and ∞/∞ limits.
checks: I can evaluate 0/0 and ∞/∞ limits.

ex.q: The limit of sin x/x as x → 0
The limit of (1 − cos x)/x² as x → 0
The limit of x/eˣ as x → ∞
The limit of x ln x as x → 0 from above
The limit of x¹⁰⁰/2ˣ as x → ∞. Connect it with 1.15b.

topics.title: Riemann sums
topics.goal: See the integral as a limit of sums.
checks: I can approximate an integral with rectangles and take the limit.

ex.q: Estimate the area under x² from 0 to 1 with 4 right-hand rectangles.
With n rectangles, use 1² + 2² + … + n² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 to show the sum tends to 1/3.
A car moves at 3 m/s for 10 s. Show the area under its v-t graph is its distance.

topics.title: The fundamental theorem of calculus
topics.goal: Why integration undoes differentiation.
checks: I can explain why integration undoes differentiation, with a picture.

ex.q: Integrate 3x² from 0 to 2.
Find d/dx of the integral of e^(−t²) from 0 to x. (No formula exists for the integral itself.)
Velocity is v(t) = 4t. How far does the object go from t = 0 to t = 3?

topics.title: Antiderivatives
topics.goal: Integrate basic functions and add the constant C.
checks: I can integrate basic functions and remember the constant.

ex.q: ∫ x⁴ dx
∫ cos x dx, ∫ eˣ dx and ∫ (1/x) dx
∫ e^(3x) dx
A stone falls from 100 m with acceleration −9.8 m/s², starting at rest. Integrate twice to find x(t), then find when it lands.

topics.title: Numerical integration
topics.search: numerical integration trapezoid rule Simpson's rule
topics.goal: Estimate integrals that have no formula.
checks: I can apply the trapezoid rule and Simpson's rule.

ex.q: Apply the trapezoid rule with 4 strips to the integral of x² from 0 to 1.
Apply Simpson's rule with 4 strips to the same integral. Why is it exact?
ex.a: 0.3333: Simpson's rule is exact for cubics and below

ex.q: Apply Simpson's rule with 2 strips to the integral of e^(−x²) from 0 to 1 (true value 0.7468).
Write a 5-line Python loop for the trapezoid rule and test it on sin x from 0 to π.

topics.title: Substitution
topics.goal: Use u-substitution.
checks: I can spot an inner function and its derivative and substitute.

ex.q: ∫ 2x(x² + 1)⁵ dx
∫ x e^(−x²) dx
∫ sin x cos x dx
Integrate sin x from 0 to π.
∫ tan x dx

topics.title: Integration by parts
topics.goal: Use ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du (used constantly in quantum proofs).
checks: I can choose u and dv well and use parts more than once.

ex.q: ∫ x eˣ dx
∫ x sin x dx
ex.a: sin x − x cos x + C

ex.q: ∫ ln x dx
Integrate x e⁻ˣ from 0 to ∞.
Prove by induction that the integral of xⁿ e⁻ˣ from 0 to ∞ equals n!.
∫ eˣ sin x dx (parts twice, then solve for the integral).

topics.title: Partial fractions
topics.goal: Split rational functions to integrate them.
checks: I can split a rational function into simple pieces and integrate them.

ex.q: Split 1/(x² − 1) and integrate it.

topics.title: Trigonometric substitution
topics.goal: Handle √(a² − x²) type integrals.
checks: I can handle √(a² − x²) and 1/(1 + x²) integrals.

ex.q: Integrate √(1 − x²) from 0 to 1. What shape's area is this?
ex.a: π/4, a quarter of the unit disc

ex.q: Integrate 1/(1 + x²) over the whole real line. (This curve is the shape of a spectral line.)

topics.title: Improper integrals
topics.goal: Integrate to infinity; this is how wavefunctions get normalized.
checks: I can integrate to infinity and decide when the answer is finite.
I can normalize a simple wavefunction.

ex.q: Integrate 1/x² from 1 to ∞.
Show that the integral of 1/x from 1 to ∞ is infinite.
Integrate e^(−ax) from 0 to ∞.
Find A so that the integral of A²e^(−2|x|) over all x is 1. You have normalized the wavefunction ψ = Ae^(−|x|).
Gabriel's horn: rotate y = 1/x for x ≥ 1 about the x-axis. Show its volume is π even though its surface area is infinite.

topics.title: The Gaussian integral
topics.goal: Show ∫e^(−x²)dx = √π. It appears everywhere in quantum mechanics.
checks: I can prove that the integral of e^(−x²) over all x is √π.

ex.q: Prove it by squaring the integral and switching to polar coordinates.
Show the integral of e^(−ax²) is √(π/a).
Normalize ψ(x) = A e^(−x²/2), the ground state of the quantum harmonic oscillator.
Differentiate Exercise 2 with respect to a to find the integral of x²e^(−x²).
Explain where the 1/(σ√(2π)) in the normal distribution comes from.
ex.a: It is 1 over the Gaussian integral with a = 1/(2σ²).

topics.title: Even and odd functions
topics.search: even and odd functions integrals symmetry
topics.goal: Odd functions integrate to zero over symmetric limits (parity).
checks: I can tell even from odd functions and use symmetry to skip integrals.

ex.q: Even, odd or neither: x³, cos x, eˣ, x sin x, sin x cos x.
Integrate x³ cos x from −5 to 5 without calculating.
Split eˣ into an even part and an odd part. (You will meet them again in 2.26.)
A probability density |ψ|² is symmetric about 0. What is the average position, and why?

topics.title: Average value of a function
topics.goal: Weighted averages, the seed of expectation values.
checks: I can compute plain and weighted averages with integrals.

ex.q: Find the average of x² on [0, 3].
Find the average of sin²x over one period.
A probability density is p(x) = 2x on [0, 1]. Find the average x.
Mains voltage is quoted as 230 V, which is the root-mean-square value. What is the peak voltage?

topics.title: Hyperbolic functions
topics.goal: Use sinh, cosh, tanh (relativity and tunneling).
checks: I can use sinh, cosh and tanh and their derivatives.

ex.q: Show cosh²x − sinh²x = 1.
Find the derivatives of sinh x and cosh x.
What do tanh x tend to as x → ±∞?
Show cos(ix) = cosh x using Euler's formula.
A hanging chain follows y = a cosh(x/a). Sketch it for a = 1 and a = 3.

topics.title: Convergence of series
topics.goal: Decide whether a series converges.
checks: I can decide whether a series converges using comparison and ratio tests.

ex.q: Show that 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + … grows without limit by grouping terms.
ex.a: 1/3 + 1/4 > 1/2, the next four > 1/2, and so on

ex.q: Does 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 + 1/16 + … converge? (It equals π²/6, proved in 3Blue1Brown's Basel problem video.)
Use the ratio test on the sum of n/2ⁿ.
Stack identical books so each overhangs the one below by the most it can. The overhangs are 1/2, 1/4, 1/6, … of a book length. Can the top book stick out more than 3 book lengths?
ex.a: Yes: the harmonic series grows without limit, so any overhang is possible.

topics.title: Power series
topics.search: power series and radius of convergence
topics.goal: Write functions as infinite polynomials.
checks: I can find a radius of convergence and differentiate or integrate a series term by term.

ex.q: Find the radius of convergence of the sum of xⁿ and of the sum of xⁿ/n!.
Expand 1/(1 + x²) as a series, integrate term by term to get arctan x, and conclude π/4 = 1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − …
ex.a: 1 − x² + x⁴ − …; arctan x = x − x³/3 + x⁵/5 − …; set x = 1

ex.q: Differentiate the sum of xⁿ to find the sum of n xⁿ⁻¹, then evaluate the sum of n/2ⁿ.

topics.title: Taylor series
topics.goal: Approximate any smooth function by polynomials; small-angle approximation.
checks: I can write Taylor series for eˣ, sin x, cos x and ln(1 + x).
I can explain why every smooth potential looks like a parabola near its minimum.

ex.q: Write the series for eˣ, sin x and cos x around 0.
Write the series for ln(1 + x).
Use cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2 at x = 0.1. How big is the error?
Expand √(1 + x) to second order.
Expand mc²/√(1 − v²/c²) in powers of v. Which familiar formula appears in the second term?
Expand any V(x) around a minimum x₀ to second order. Why does this mean almost everything oscillates?

topics.title: Euler's formula from series
topics.search: Taylor series of e^x sin cos and Euler's formula proof
topics.goal: Prove e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ from the series.
checks: I can derive e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ from the series.

ex.q: Put iθ into the eˣ series and collect real and imaginary parts.
Add the first 10 terms of the series for e^(iπ) by hand or in code. How close to −1 do you get?
ex.a: Within about 0.03 of −1 after 10 terms; 15 terms get within 10⁻⁴

ex.q: Find d/dθ of e^(iθ) and show it is always at right angles to e^(iθ). What motion does that describe?
ex.a: i e^(iθ): velocity at 90° to position gives circular motion.

topics.title: Arc length and volumes of revolution
topics.search: arc length and volumes of revolution
topics.goal: Apply integrals to geometry.
checks: I can set up arc-length and volume integrals.

ex.q: Rotate y = √x from 0 to 4 about the x-axis and find the volume.
Find the arc length of y = x^(3/2) from 0 to 4.
Derive the volume of a ball by rotating a semicircle.
ex.a: π∫(R² − x²) dx from −R to R = (4/3)πR³.

topics.title: A full calculus course
topics.goal: A full lecture course to fill any gaps with worked examples.
checks: I can do a mixed set of problems without knowing which technique each needs.

ex.q: Pick the 10 problems you found hardest in this part and redo them without notes.
d/dx [x² e⁻ˣ sin x]
ex.a: e⁻ˣ(2x sin x − x² sin x + x² cos x)

ex.q: Integrate sin³x from 0 to π/2.
∫ x² ln x dx
Final challenge: integrate x²e^(−x²) from 0 to ∞.

parts.name: Linear Algebra
parts.title: Linear algebra
parts.intro: You finish this part by proving that an entangled state cannot be split into two separate particles, using nothing but vectors.

topics.title: Essence of linear algebra
topics.goal: Watch it all; the rows below are its key checkpoints plus what it leaves out.
checks: I have watched the whole series.
I can explain a matrix as a description of where the basis vectors land.

ex.q: Write one sentence summarizing each chapter, from memory.
For [[2, 1], [1, 2]] (rows in order), draw where (1, 0) and (0, 1) land and sketch the transformed grid.
Without computing, which of these squashes the plane onto a line: [[1, 2], [2, 4]] or [[1, 2], [3, 4]]?

topics.title: Vectors
topics.goal: Vectors as arrows and as lists of numbers.
checks: I can treat a vector both as an arrow and as a list of numbers.

ex.q: Draw (2, 1), (−1, 3) and their sum.
A velocity is (3, 4) m/s. What is the speed?
A gas state (temperature, pressure, volume) is a list of numbers. Is it still useful to call it a vector? What does adding two such states mean, if anything?
ex.a: The numbers form a vector, but adding two whole states has little physical meaning; differences between states do.

topics.title: Linear combinations, span and basis
topics.goal: Build any vector from basis vectors.
checks: I can write a vector in a given basis.
I can tell whether a set of vectors spans a space.

ex.q: Do (1, 2) and (2, 4) span the plane?
ex.a: No: they point the same way

ex.q: Write (2, 3, 4) in that basis.

topics.title: Gaussian elimination
topics.goal: Solve a 3×3 system of equations by row reduction.
checks: I can solve a 3 × 3 system by row reduction.
I can recognize systems with no solution or infinitely many.

ex.q: Describe all solutions of x + y = 2 and 2x + 2y = 4.
ex.a: x = 2 − t, y = t for any t

ex.q: Balance C₃H₈ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O by writing one equation per element and row-reducing.

topics.title: Linear independence
topics.goal: Test whether a set of vectors is independent.
checks: I can test whether vectors, or functions, are linearly independent.

ex.q: Are (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6) and (7, 8, 9) independent?
Are the functions 1, x and x² independent?
Are sin²x, cos²x and 1 independent?
What is the largest number of independent vectors in 3D space?

topics.title: Linear transformations and matrices
topics.goal: A matrix is a recipe for where basis vectors land.
checks: I can write the matrix of a rotation, reflection or shear.
I can tell whether a map is linear.

ex.q: Write the matrix that rotates by 90° counterclockwise.
Write the matrix that reflects across the x-axis.
Where does the shear [[1, 1], [0, 1]] send (0, 1)?
Is f(x, y) = (x + 1, y) linear?
Write the matrix that rotates by any angle θ.

topics.title: Matrix multiplication as composition
topics.goal: Multiply matrices and know why order matters (AB ≠ BA).
checks: I can multiply matrices and explain why the order matters.

ex.q: Compute [[1, 2], [3, 4]] × [[0, 1], [1, 0]] and the product in the other order.
Square the 90° rotation matrix. What transformation is it?
Multiply the rotation matrices for α and β. Read off the angle addition formulas from 1.24.
With σx = [[0, 1], [1, 0]] and σz = [[1, 0], [0, −1]], compute σxσz and σzσx. How are they related?
ex.a: σxσz = [[0, −1], [1, 0]] and σzσx = [[0, 1], [−1, 0]]: one is minus the other.

topics.title: The determinant
topics.goal: Determinant as area or volume scaling; det = 0 means squashing.
checks: I can compute 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 determinants and explain them as area or volume scaling.

ex.q: det [[3, 1], [2, 4]]. What does the number mean for the unit square?
What is the determinant of any rotation matrix?
det [[1, 2], [2, 4]]. What does this transformation do?
ex.a: 0: the plane is squashed onto a line

ex.q: Check det(AB) = det(A) det(B) using the matrices of 3.5 Exercise 1.
What does a negative determinant mean geometrically?
ex.a: Orientation is flipped, like a mirror.

topics.title: Inverses, rank and null space
topics.search: inverse matrices column space null space rank
topics.goal: When Ax = b has a solution.
checks: I can invert a 2 × 2 matrix and explain when no inverse exists.

ex.q: Use the inverse to solve [[2, 1], [1, 1]] x = (3, 2).
Find the rank and null space of [[1, 2], [2, 4]].
Explain with a picture why a matrix with determinant 0 cannot be undone.
ex.a: Many inputs land on the same output.

topics.title: The dot product
topics.goal: Dot product as projection.
checks: I can compute dot products, angles and projections.

ex.q: Find the angle between (1, 0) and (1, 1).
A force (3, 4) N moves an object by (2, 0) m. How much work is done?
Are (1, 2, −1) and (2, −1, 0) perpendicular?

topics.title: The cross product
topics.goal: Cross product for torque and angular momentum.
checks: I can compute a cross product and use it for areas, torque and angular momentum.

ex.q: Find the area of the parallelogram spanned by those two vectors.
A 10 N force pushes along y at the end of a 0.5 m wrench lying along x. Find the torque vector.
A particle at (1, 0, 0) has momentum (0, 2, 0). Find its angular momentum L = r × p.

topics.title: Change of basis
topics.goal: The same vector in different coordinates (the heart of quantum "representations").
checks: I can find the coordinates of a vector in a new basis.
I can rewrite a matrix in a new basis.

ex.q: Find the coordinates of (3, 1) in the basis b₁ = (1, 1), b₂ = (−1, 1).
Write the change-of-basis matrix and its inverse.
Write the 90° rotation in the basis b₁, b₂. Are you surprised?
ex.a: Still [[0, −1], [1, 0]], because b₂ is b₁ rotated 90°

ex.q: Photon polarization: horizontal is H = (1, 0); the diagonal states are D = (1, 1)/√2 and A = (1, −1)/√2. Write H in terms of D and A. What does this suggest a horizontally polarized photon "is" in the diagonal basis?
ex.a: H = (D + A)/√2: an equal superposition of diagonal and antidiagonal.

topics.title: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
topics.goal: Solve Av = λv. Measurement results in quantum mechanics are eigenvalues.
checks: I can find eigenvalues from det(A − λI) = 0 and the matching eigenvectors.

ex.q: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of [[2, 0], [0, 3]].
Show that the 90° rotation has no real eigenvectors. What are its eigenvalues?
Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of σx = [[0, 1], [1, 0]].
How many eigenvector directions does the shear [[1, 1], [0, 1]] have?

topics.title: Quick eigenvalue trick
topics.goal: Find 2×2 eigenvalues fast.
checks: I can get 2 × 2 eigenvalues from mean ± √(mean² − det).

topics.title: Diagonalization
topics.goal: Write A = PDP⁻¹ and use it.
checks: I can write A = PDP⁻¹ and use it to compute high powers.

ex.q: Diagonalize [[2, 1], [1, 2]].
Use the result to compute [[2, 1], [1, 2]]¹⁰.
The Fibonacci step is (Fₙ₊₁, Fₙ) = [[1, 1], [1, 0]](Fₙ, Fₙ₋₁). Find the eigenvalues and use them to explain why Fₙ₊₁/Fₙ approaches the golden ratio from 1.8.
ex.a: Eigenvalues (1 ± √5)/2; the larger dominates after many steps.

topics.title: Abstract vector spaces
topics.goal: Functions are vectors too; derivatives are linear operators.
checks: I can treat functions as vectors and derivatives as linear operators.

ex.q: Why do polynomials of degree at most 2 form a vector space? Give a basis.
Write the matrix of d/dx in the basis {1, x, x²}.
Find all eigenfunctions of d/dx.
Show that sin(kx) is an eigenfunction of d²/dx². What is its eigenvalue?

topics.title: Inner products and orthogonality
topics.goal: Inner products, lengths, orthogonal and orthonormal bases.
checks: I can use an integral as an inner product of functions.

ex.q: With ⟨f, g⟩ = integral of f g from 0 to 2π, show that sin x and cos x are orthogonal.
Compute ⟨sin x, sin x⟩ and normalize sin x.
Show sin x and sin 2x are orthogonal.
Check the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for (1, 2) and (3, 4).

topics.title: Projections
topics.goal: Project a vector; projection matrices P² = P.
checks: I can project a vector onto a line and build the projection matrix.

ex.q: Project (2, 3) onto the line along (1, 1).
Write the matrix that projects onto (1, 1)/√2 and check P² = P.
A quantum state is (0.6, 0.8). The chance of finding it in the state (1, 0) is the squared length of its projection. Compute it.

topics.title: Gram-Schmidt
topics.goal: Build an orthonormal basis.
checks: I can turn any basis into an orthonormal one.

ex.q: Orthonormalize (1, 1, 0) and (1, 0, 1).
Apply Gram-Schmidt to 1, x and x² on [−1, 1] with the integral inner product. Which famous polynomials appear? (See 5.22.)
ex.a: 1, x and x² − 1/3: the Legendre polynomials, up to scale.

topics.title: Complex inner products
topics.search: complex vector spaces and complex inner product
topics.goal: Why the inner product conjugates one side.
checks: I can compute complex inner products and explain why one side is conjugated.

ex.q: With ⟨u, v⟩ = sum of conj(uᵢ) vᵢ, compute ⟨u, v⟩ for u = (1, i) and v = (i, 1).
Compute the length of (1, i). What would you get without the conjugate?
ex.a: √2; without the conjugate you would get 1 + i² = 0

ex.q: Normalize (1 + i, 2).
Show that ⟨v, u⟩ is the complex conjugate of ⟨u, v⟩.

topics.title: Hermitian matrices
topics.goal: Prove Hermitian matrices have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors (they are observables).
checks: I can prove Hermitian matrices have real eigenvalues.

ex.q: Is [[2, i], [−i, 3]] Hermitian?
Find its eigenvalues. Are they real?
Prove that the eigenvalues of any Hermitian matrix are real.
Check that σy is Hermitian.

topics.title: Unitary matrices
topics.goal: Unitary matrices preserve length (time evolution and quantum gates).
checks: I can check U†U = I and explain why unitary maps preserve length.

ex.q: Is the Hadamard matrix H = (1/√2)[[1, 1], [1, −1]] unitary?
Apply H to (1, 0). What kind of state do you get?
Show that every eigenvalue of a unitary matrix has absolute value 1.
Show that rotation matrices are unitary.

topics.title: The spectral theorem
topics.goal: Every Hermitian matrix is diagonal in some orthonormal basis.
checks: I can write a Hermitian matrix as a sum of eigenvalues times projectors.

ex.q: Write [[2, 1], [1, 2]] as 3P₁ + 1P₂ with projectors onto its eigenvectors.
Do the same for σz.
Use the decomposition to find a square root of [[2, 1], [1, 2]].

topics.title: The trace
topics.goal: Trace equals the sum of eigenvalues; it is basis-independent.
checks: I know the trace equals the sum of the eigenvalues and is basis-independent.

ex.q: Find the trace of [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and check it equals the sum of its eigenvalues.
Check tr(AB) = tr(BA) with the matrices of 3.5 Exercise 1.
What are the traces of the three Pauli matrices?
What is the trace of a projection matrix?

topics.title: Commutators
topics.goal: Compute [A, B] = AB − BA; non-commuting means no shared eigenbasis.
checks: I can compute [A, B] = AB − BA and explain what a non-zero commutator means.

ex.q: Compute [σx, σz] and write it in terms of σy.
Compute [σx, σy].
Why do any two diagonal matrices commute?
ex.a: Diagonal entries multiply in either order.

ex.q: Prove [A, BC] = [A, B]C + B[A, C].

topics.title: The matrix exponential
topics.goal: Compute e^A; preview of e^(−iHt/ħ).
checks: I can compute e^A for diagonal matrices and via power series.

ex.q: e^A for A = diag(1, 2)
Let J = [[0, −1], [1, 0]]. Show J² = −I, then use the series to show e^(θJ) is the rotation matrix. Compare with Euler's formula.
ex.a: e^(θJ) = cos θ I + sin θ J

ex.q: Compute e^(−iθσz/2).
Is e^(A + B) = e^A e^B when A and B do not commute? Test it on a computer with two random matrices.

topics.title: Outer products and projectors
topics.goal: Build matrices from vectors (|a⟩⟨b| later).
checks: I can build a matrix from two vectors and recognize projectors.

ex.q: Compute the outer product of (1, 0) with itself.
Compute the outer product of (1, 1)/√2 with itself. Compare with 3.16.
What is the rank of any outer product of two non-zero vectors?
Add the outer products of (1, 0) and (0, 1) with themselves. What do you get, and why?
ex.a: The identity, because the basis is complete.

topics.title: The Pauli matrices
topics.goal: Know σx, σy, σz, their eigenvalues and commutators.
checks: I know σx, σy and σz, their squares, products and eigenvalues.

ex.q: Show σx² = σy² = σz² = I.
Show σxσy = iσz.
What are the eigenvalues of each Pauli matrix?
Write [[3, 1 − i], [1 + i, −1]] as aI + bσx + cσy + dσz.

topics.title: Tensor products
topics.goal: Combine two vector spaces; the math of multi-particle states and entanglement.
checks: I can compute tensor products of vectors and matrices.
I can show that some two-particle states cannot be written as a product.

ex.q: Write (a, b) ⊗ (c, d) in general.
Show that (1, 0, 0, 1)/√2 cannot be written as (a, b) ⊗ (c, d). You have just proved this state is entangled.
ex.a: ad = 0 and bc = 0 force ac = 0 or bd = 0, but both must be 1/√2

ex.q: Write σx ⊗ I as a 4 × 4 matrix.
What is the dimension of the space for 10 qubits?

topics.title: Singular value decomposition
topics.goal: Any matrix as rotate, stretch, rotate (later: Schmidt decomposition).
checks: I can describe any matrix as rotate, stretch, rotate.

ex.q: Find the singular values of [[1, 1], [0, 0]].
In Python, load a greyscale photo as a matrix, keep only its 20 largest singular values, and display the result. How much quality is lost?
Arrange (1, 0, 0, 1)/√2 as the 2 × 2 matrix [[1, 0], [0, 1]]/√2 and find its singular values. (Two equal values mean maximal entanglement, as you will see in 16.27.)

topics.title: A full linear algebra course
topics.goal: A full lecture course for computational fluency.
checks: I can do mixed linear algebra problems quickly and correctly.

ex.q: Work through the first three problem sets of MIT 18.06.
Find the eigenvalues of [[4, 1, 0], [1, 4, 1], [0, 1, 4]].
Prove that similar matrices (B = P⁻¹AP) have the same eigenvalues.

parts.name: Vector Calculus
parts.title: Multivariable and vector calculus
parts.intro: The highlight is 4.10 and 4.20: you normalize the real hydrogen ground state and check that it solves the Schrödinger equation.

topics.title: Functions of several variables
topics.search: functions of several variables contour plots
topics.goal: Picture f(x, y) as a surface and as contour lines.
checks: I can picture f(x, y) as a surface and as a contour map.

ex.q: Describe the contour lines of f = x² + y².
Describe the surface and contours of f = x² − y².
On a hiking map, what do contour lines that crowd together mean?
Temperature on a plate is T = 20 + 5x − 3y. In which direction does it rise fastest?

topics.title: Partial derivatives
topics.goal: Differentiate in one variable while holding the others fixed.
checks: I can take partial derivatives and mixed second derivatives.

ex.q: For f = x²y + sin(xy), find ∂f/∂x and ∂f/∂y.
For the ideal gas P = nRT/V, find ∂P/∂T and ∂P/∂V and explain each physically.
ex.a: nR/V (hotter, more pressure); −nRT/V² (bigger volume, less pressure)

ex.q: For f = x³y², check that ∂²f/∂x∂y = ∂²f/∂y∂x.
For ψ = sin(kx − ωt), show that ∂²ψ/∂t² = (ω/k)² ∂²ψ/∂x². What equation is this?
ex.a: The wave equation with speed ω/k.

topics.title: The gradient
topics.goal: The gradient points uphill; force = −∇(potential energy).
checks: I can compute a gradient and explain why force = −∇(potential energy).

ex.q: ∇(x² + y²)
Potential energy near the ground is U = mgz. Find the force.
With r = √(x² + y² + z²), show ∂(1/r)/∂x = −x/r³. Use it to find the electric field from V = k/r.
ex.a: E = k r/r³, pointing outward with strength k/r²

ex.q: A hill has height h = 100 − x² − 2y². At (3, 1), which way is steepest uphill?

topics.title: Directional derivatives
topics.goal: Rate of change in any direction.
checks: I can find the rate of change of f in any direction.

ex.q: For f = x²y at (1, 2), find the rate of change in the direction (3, 4)/5.
In which direction is that rate zero?
What is the largest possible rate there?

topics.title: The multivariable chain rule
topics.goal: Chain rule through several variables.
checks: I can differentiate along a path through several variables.

ex.q: z = x²y with x = cos t and y = sin t. Find dz/dt.
Temperature is T = x + y². A walker moves along (t, 2t). How fast does the temperature they feel change?
Write ∂f/∂r in terms of ∂f/∂x and ∂f/∂y, using x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ.

topics.title: Hessians and multivariable Taylor series
topics.goal: Approximate near a minimum by a quadratic bowl (why oscillators are everywhere).
checks: I can classify a critical point as minimum, maximum or saddle using the Hessian.

ex.q: Classify the origin for x² + 3y², x² − y² and −x² − y².
Find the Hessian of x² + xy + y² at the origin and its eigenvalues (see 3.11). What kind of point is it?
Near a minimum, any potential looks like a bowl described by its Hessian. Explain why molecules vibrate in patterns given by the Hessian's eigenvectors.

topics.title: Lagrange multipliers
topics.goal: Optimize under a constraint (used to derive the Boltzmann distribution).
checks: I can optimize a function under a constraint.

ex.q: Maximize xy subject to x + y = 10.
Find the box with the largest volume for a surface area of 6.
Find the point on x + 2y = 5 closest to the origin.
Maximize −(p₁ ln p₁ + … + pₙ ln pₙ) subject to p₁ + … + pₙ = 1. What does the answer say about maximum entropy? (Add an energy constraint and you get the Boltzmann factor of 10.15.)
ex.a: All pᵢ = 1/n: no extra knowledge means a uniform distribution.

topics.title: Double and triple integrals
topics.goal: Integrate over areas and volumes.
checks: I can set up and evaluate integrals over rectangles and simple regions, in either order.

ex.q: Integrate xy over the rectangle 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 2.
Find the volume under z = x² + y² over the unit square.
A triangular plate 0 ≤ y ≤ x ≤ 1 has density ρ = x. Find its mass.
Redo Exercise 3 with the order of integration swapped.

topics.title: Change of variables and the Jacobian
topics.goal: Why integrals pick up a Jacobian factor.
checks: I can explain where the Jacobian factor comes from and use it.

ex.q: Show that the Jacobian of polar coordinates is r.
Find the area of a disc of radius R in polar coordinates.
Redo the Gaussian integral of 2.23 as a 2D integral in polar coordinates.
Map the unit disc with x = au, y = bv. Use the Jacobian to find the area of an ellipse.

topics.title: Cylindrical and spherical coordinates
topics.search: cylindrical and spherical coordinates volume element
topics.goal: Use r² sin θ dr dθ dφ (the hydrogen atom needs this).
checks: I can integrate with the volume element r² sin θ dr dθ dφ.
I can normalize a 3D wavefunction that depends only on r.

ex.q: Derive the volume of a ball.
Derive the surface area of a sphere.
The hydrogen ground state is ψ = A e^(−r/a). Find A so the total probability is 1. (Use the integral of xⁿ e⁻ˣ from 0 to ∞ = n! from 2.19.)
What is the probability of finding the electron within r < a?
Find the average distance ⟨r⟩ of the electron from the nucleus.

topics.title: Solid angle
topics.goal: A full sphere is 4π steradians; compute the solid angle of a cone.
checks: I know a sphere is 4π steradians and can find the solid angle of a cone.

ex.q: Derive the solid angle 2π(1 − cos θ) of a cone with half-angle θ. Evaluate it for 60°.
The Sun's disc has an angular radius of 0.27°. About what solid angle does it cover?
A source emits equally in all directions. What fraction hits a 1 cm² detector 1 m away?

topics.title: Vector fields
topics.goal: Picture fields as arrows at every point.
checks: I can sketch a vector field and read its behaviour.

ex.q: Sketch F = (−y, x) and F = (x, y). Describe each in one word.
Which of the two looks like the electric field around a positive charge?
If F is the velocity of water, where would a floating leaf go in each field?
ex.a: Circles around the origin; straight outward.

topics.title: Line integrals
topics.goal: Integrate along a path (work done by a force).
checks: I can compute work along a path and test whether the path matters.

ex.q: Find the work done by F = (y, x) from (0, 0) to (1, 1) along the straight line, then via (1, 0). Compare.
ex.a: 1 both ways (the field is the gradient of xy)

ex.q: Find the circulation of F = (−y, x) around the unit circle.
Why does gravity do the same work whether you slide down a ramp or fall straight down?

topics.title: Surface integrals and flux
topics.goal: Measure how much field passes through a surface.
checks: I can compute the flux of a field through a surface.

ex.q: Find the flux of F = (0, 0, 3) through the unit square in the xy-plane.
Find the flux of F = r/r³ (pointing outward, strength 1/r²) through a sphere of radius R. Why doesn't R matter?
ex.a: 4π: field strength falls as 1/R² while area grows as R²

ex.q: Find the flux of F = (x, y, z) through a sphere of radius R.

topics.title: Divergence and curl
topics.goal: Divergence as outflow and curl as rotation (the language of Maxwell's equations).
checks: I can compute divergence and curl and say what each measures.

ex.q: Find the divergence and curl of (x, y, z).
Find the divergence and curl of (−y, x, 0).
The field r/r³ has zero divergence everywhere except the origin. Where is its source?
ex.a: At the origin: a point source

ex.q: Which field pattern describes a whirlpool, a tap and a drain?
ex.a: Whirlpool: curl; tap: positive divergence; drain: negative divergence.

topics.title: Green's theorem
topics.goal: Relate a loop integral to an area integral.
checks: I can turn a loop integral into an area integral and back.

ex.q: Check Green's theorem for F = (−y, x) on the unit disc.
Use ½∮(x dy − y dx) to find the area of an ellipse.
Look up how a planimeter measures area by tracing a boundary. Why does it work?

topics.title: Stokes' theorem
topics.goal: Circulation equals the flux of curl.
checks: I can relate circulation around a loop to the flux of the curl through any surface it bounds.

ex.q: Check Stokes' theorem for F = (−y, x, 0) using the upper half of the unit sphere.
Why is the circulation of any gradient field around a closed loop zero?
ex.a: The curl of a gradient is zero

ex.q: Ampere's law says the circulation of B around a loop equals μ₀ times the current through it. Which theorem turns this into a statement about curl B?
ex.a: Stokes' theorem gives curl B = μ₀J.

topics.title: The divergence theorem
topics.goal: Total outflow equals the integral of divergence.
checks: I can relate total outflow through a closed surface to the divergence inside.

ex.q: Check the theorem for F = (x, y, z) on a ball of radius R. Compare with 4.13 Exercise 3.
If charge is conserved, show that ∂ρ/∂t + ∇ · J = 0. (Quantum probability obeys the same equation in 15.20.)
Use the theorem with 4.13 Exercise 2 to explain Gauss's law for a point charge.

topics.title: Conservative fields
topics.goal: When a field is the gradient of a potential.
checks: I can test whether a field is a gradient and find its potential.

ex.q: Is F = (2xy, x² + 1) conservative? Find a potential if so.
Is F = (y, −x) conservative?
Why does conservation of energy require a conservative force?
ex.a: Only then does work depend on the endpoints alone.

topics.title: The Laplacian
topics.goal: ∇² as "how different from your neighbours"; it is the kinetic term in the Schrödinger equation.
checks: I can compute ∇² and explain it as "different from the neighbours' average".

ex.q: ∇²(x² + y² + z²)
Show ∇²(1/r) = 0 away from the origin.
Show sin(kx) sin(ky) is an eigenfunction of the 2D Laplacian and find the eigenvalue. (This is a particle in a 2D box.)
Show that [f(x + h) + f(x − h) − 2f(x)]/h² approaches f″(x). How does this explain the "neighbours" picture?
The kinetic energy operator is −(ħ²/2m) d²/dx². Apply it to e^(ikx). Which classical formula appears if p = ħk?

topics.title: The Laplacian in spherical coordinates
topics.goal: Know its radial and angular parts.
checks: I can use the radial part ∇²f = (1/r²) d/dr (r² df/dr) for functions of r alone.

ex.q: Compute ∇² e^(−r).
Redo 4.19 Exercise 2 with the radial formula.
Show that ψ = e^(−r/a) solves −(ħ²/2m)∇²ψ − (ke²/r)ψ = Eψ only if a = ħ²/(mke²). Then find E. You have solved the hydrogen ground state (17.1).
ex.a: The 1/r terms cancel when a = ħ²/(mke²); then E = −ħ²/(2ma²) = −ke²/(2a) ≈ −13.6 eV.

topics.title: Vector identities
checks: I can prove the standard identities in components.

ex.q: Prove ∇ · (∇ × A) = 0.
Prove ∇ × (∇f) = 0.
Use ∇ × (∇ × A) = ∇(∇ · A) − ∇²A on Maxwell's equations in empty space to get a wave equation. (You will redo this in 11.18.)

topics.title: Gaussian integrals in n dimensions
topics.goal: Integrate e^(−x·Ax) (preview of path integrals).
checks: I can integrate e^(−x·Ax) using the determinant of A.

ex.q: Integrate e^(−(x² + y²)) over the whole plane.
Integrate e^(−(x² + 4y²)) over the plane.
Guess the general formula for n dimensions in terms of det A.
Apply it to A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]]. (Diagonalize first, as in 3.13.)

topics.title: A full multivariable course
topics.search: Khan Academy multivariable calculus Grant Sanderson
topics.goal: A full visual course to fill gaps.
checks: I can do mixed multivariable problems without being told the method.

ex.q: Find the flux of F = (x², y², z²) out of the unit cube [0, 1]³ using the divergence theorem.
ex.a: The integral of 2(x + y + z) over the cube = 3

ex.q: Find and classify the critical points of f = x³ + y³ − 3xy.
Find the volume of the region inside the sphere x² + y² + z² = 4 and above the cone z = √(x² + y²).

parts.name: ODEs and Fourier
parts.title: Differential equations, Fourier analysis, special functions, complex analysis
parts.intro: In 5.8 you will find that a vibrating string only allows energies in the ratio 1 : 4 : 9, exactly the particle-in-a-box energies of quantum mechanics.

topics.title: Differential equations, a tourist's guide
topics.goal: What a differential equation is; phase space; why most cannot be solved exactly.
checks: I can say what order and linearity mean for a differential equation.
I can read a phase-space picture.

ex.q: Give the order and say linear or not: y″ + 3y′ + 2y = 0; y′ = y²; the pendulum θ″ = −(g/L) sin θ.
ex.a: Second, linear; first, nonlinear; second, nonlinear

ex.q: Sketch the phase space (θ, θ′) of a pendulum without friction, then with friction.
ex.a: Closed loops (and swirls around the top); with friction, inward spirals

ex.q: Take three Euler steps of θ″ = −sin θ by hand from θ = 1, θ′ = 0 with dt = 0.1 (update θ′ from θ, then θ from the old θ′).
Romeo's love R and Juliet's love J obey R′ = J and J′ = −R. Describe what happens over time.
ex.a: They cycle forever: R = cos t, J = −sin t.

topics.title: Separable equations
topics.goal: Solve dN/dt = −λN (radioactive decay).
checks: I can separate variables and integrate both sides.

ex.q: Solve dN/dt = −λN and link λ to the half-life T.
Solve dy/dx = xy.
Coffee at 90 °C cools in a 20 °C room as dT/dt = −0.1(T − 20) per minute. When is it 50 °C?
Solve the logistic equation dy/dt = y(1 − y).

topics.title: Integrating factors
topics.search: first order linear ODE integrating factor
topics.goal: Solve y′ + p(x)y = q(x).
checks: I can solve y′ + p(x)y = q(x).

ex.q: y′ + y = eˣ
A capacitor charges as V′ + V/(RC) = V₀/(RC) with V(0) = 0. Find V(t).
y′ + 2xy = x

topics.title: Constant-coefficient second-order equations
topics.search: second order linear ODE constant coefficients characteristic equation
topics.goal: Complex roots of the characteristic equation produce oscillations.
checks: I can use the characteristic equation, including complex and repeated roots.

ex.q: y″ + 2y′ + 5y = 0 (compare with 1.37 Exercise 3)

topics.title: The harmonic oscillator
topics.goal: Solve x″ = −ω²x by sines, cosines and complex exponentials.
checks: I can solve x″ = −ω²x with any starting conditions.

ex.q: Solve with x(0) = A and x′(0) = 0.
A 0.5 kg mass hangs on a 200 N/m spring. Find ω and the period.
Write the solution as the real part of C e^(iωt).
Show that ½kx² + ½mv² stays constant.

topics.title: Damping and resonance
topics.goal: Damping, resonance and the resonance curve.
checks: I can tell under-, critically and over-damped motion apart.
I can sketch a resonance curve.

ex.q: For x″ + 2γx′ + ω₀²x = 0, find the condition for each damping regime.
ex.a: Underdamped γ < ω₀, critical γ = ω₀, overdamped γ > ω₀

ex.q: Which regime do car shock absorbers aim for, and why?
ex.a: Close to critical: fastest return without bouncing

ex.q: A driven oscillator has amplitude (F/m)/√((ω₀² − ω²)² + 4γ²ω²). Sketch it for small and large γ.
ex.a: Small γ: tall narrow peak near ω₀; large γ: low broad hump

ex.q: The Tacoma Narrows bridge collapse is often blamed on resonance. Look up why that explanation is incomplete.
ex.a: It was aeroelastic flutter, a self-exciting instability.

topics.title: Systems of equations
topics.search: systems of differential equations matrix exponential
topics.goal: Solve x′ = Ax with eigenvectors.
checks: I can solve x′ = Ax with eigenvectors and classify fixed points.

ex.q: Solve x′ = Ax for A = [[0, 1], [−1, 0]]. Compare with 3.24 Exercise 2.
ex.a: A rotation: x = (cos t, −sin t) times constants

ex.q: Two equal pendulums joined by a spring have normal modes along (1, 1) and (1, −1). Describe each motion.
Which eigenvalues give a saddle, a stable node, a spiral and a centre?
ex.a: Real, opposite signs: saddle; both negative: stable node; complex with negative real part: spiral; purely imaginary: centre.

topics.title: Boundary value problems
topics.search: boundary value problems and eigenvalue problems
topics.goal: Boundary conditions allow only certain solutions: this is the math of quantization.
checks: I can explain how boundary conditions allow only discrete solutions.

ex.q: Solve y″ = −λy with y(0) = y(L) = 0. Which λ are allowed?
Show that λ ≤ 0 gives only y = 0.
For L = 1, list the first three λ and their ratios. (These are the particle-in-a-box energies of 15.12.)
Why does a guitar string sound a note plus overtones at 2, 3, 4 times its frequency?
ex.a: The allowed modes have frequencies n times the lowest.

topics.title: The heat equation
topics.search: But what is a partial differential equation 3Blue1Brown
topics.goal: The heat equation as a first PDE.
checks: I can explain ∂T/∂t = α ∂²T/∂x² in words.

ex.q: Where on a temperature curve does the temperature fall, and where does it rise?
ex.a: It falls where the curve bends down (peaks) and rises where it bends up (dips)

ex.q: Check that e^(−αk²t) sin(kx) is a solution.
How much faster does sin(10x) fade than sin x?

topics.title: Separation of variables
topics.search: solving the heat equation separation of variables
topics.goal: Split a PDE into ODEs.
checks: I can turn a PDE into ODEs with a product guess.

ex.q: Put T = X(x)G(t) into the heat equation and separate.
A rod of length π with cold ends starts at T = sin x + 0.5 sin 3x. Write T(x, t).
ex.a: T = e^(−αt) sin x + 0.5 e^(−9αt) sin 3x.

ex.q: Separate the 2D Laplace equation ∂²u/∂x² + ∂²u/∂y² = 0.

topics.title: The wave equation
topics.goal: Derive and solve the 1D wave equation.
checks: I can solve the 1D wave equation with travelling and standing waves.

ex.q: Show that any f(x − ct) solves u_tt = c²u_xx.
Show sin(kx) cos(ωt) solves it when ω = ck.
A bump at rest is released. Describe what happens (d'Alembert's solution).
ex.a: It splits into two half-height bumps moving apart

ex.q: A guitar string is 0.65 m long and waves travel along it at 286 m/s. Find its lowest note.

topics.title: Laplace and Poisson equations
topics.goal: Potentials in empty space and around charges.
checks: I know what ∇²V = 0 and ∇²V = −ρ/ε₀ describe.

ex.q: Show ln r solves the 2D Laplace equation away from the origin.
A solution of Laplace's equation equals the average of its values on any circle around a point. Why does this mean a soap film has no bumps?
ex.a: No point can be higher than all its neighbours

ex.q: Inside a uniformly charged ball, guess V(r) as a quadratic and fix it with Poisson's equation.

topics.title: Fourier series
topics.search: But what is a Fourier series 3Blue1Brown drawing with circles
topics.goal: Build any periodic function from sines and cosines.
checks: I can compute Fourier coefficients and build a periodic function from sines.

ex.q: Derive the series of a square wave: (4/π)(sin x + sin 3x/3 + sin 5x/5 + …).
Evaluate it at x = π/2. Which series for π appears? (Compare 2.28.)
Plot the first 1, 3 and 20 terms. Where does the overshoot (Gibbs phenomenon) appear, and does it shrink?
ex.a: At the jumps; it stays about 9% and only gets narrower

ex.q: Rewrite a Fourier series with e^(inx) terms.
Draw your initials with rotating circles using an online Fourier drawing tool.

topics.title: The Fourier transform
topics.goal: Decompose a signal into frequencies.
checks: I can compute simple Fourier transforms and use an FFT in code.

ex.q: Show that the transform of e^(−x²/2) is again a Gaussian.
Find the transform of a box of width a. How does its width depend on a?
Make a signal of 440 + 554 + 659 Hz in Python and find the three peaks with an FFT.
What is the transform of e^(ik₀x)?

topics.title: The uncertainty principle in Fourier analysis
