Does the photon "decide" its past? Explain.
ex.a: No: only the full set of correlations has meaning.

topics.title: Decoherence
topics.goal: Why the everyday world looks classical.
checks: I can explain why the everyday world looks classical.

ex.q: Why does a dust grain in air lose quantum coherence almost instantly?
ex.a: Billions of collisions record its position each second

ex.q: Does decoherence fully solve the measurement problem? (See 19.1.)
ex.a: No: it explains why we don't see interference, not why one result happens.

topics.title: The Copenhagen interpretation
topics.goal: The textbook interpretation and its rules.
checks: I can state Copenhagen's main ideas and a criticism.

ex.q: List its main claims.
Where is the "cut" between quantum and classical, and why is that a problem?
ex.a: The theory does not say, which is the measurement problem.

topics.title: Feynman's arrows
topics.search: Feynman QED lectures Auckland sum over paths
topics.goal: Feynman's own visual explanation of light as arrows that add.
checks: I can add amplitude arrows to predict where light goes.

ex.q: Feynman explains 4% reflection from glass with arrows from the front and back surfaces. Why does the reflection vary with glass thickness?
ex.a: The two arrows rotate relative to each other as thickness changes

ex.q: Why does light seem to travel in straight lines if it takes every path?
ex.a: Arrows away from the straight path cancel.

ex.q: Explain a diffraction grating by removing the paths whose arrows point the wrong way.

topics.title: The path integral
topics.goal: Particles "try every path"; how classical paths emerge.
checks: I can explain how the classical path emerges from summing all paths.

ex.q: Each path contributes e^(iS/ħ). Why do paths near the stationary-action path (8.34) add up and others cancel?
A baseball has action of order 100 J·s. How many ħ is that, and why does only one path matter?
ex.a: About 10³⁶ ħ: phases swing wildly except along the classical path.

topics.title: Building intuition
topics.goal: A carefully built intro series.
checks: I can explain the core ideas to a friend.

ex.q: Explain to someone with no physics why two paths can cancel.
Explain why measuring changes the outcome, without using the word "disturb".

topics.title: Deep conceptual episodes
topics.search: PBS Space Time quantum mechanics playlist
topics.goal: Deep conceptual episodes on every topic here.
checks: I can summarize a long conceptual video in my own words.

ex.q: Watch three PBS Space Time quantum episodes and write a five-sentence summary of each.

topics.title: A full university course
topics.goal: A full university course with the math.
checks: I can do standard problem-set questions.

ex.q: Find E₁ for an electron in a 0.5 nm box.
Normalize ψ = A sin(πx/L) on [0, L] and find ⟨x⟩.
Find the ground-state energy of an oscillator with ħω = 0.1 eV and the photon wavelength for a 1 → 0 jump.

parts.name: QM Formalism
parts.title: Quantum mechanics, the formalism
parts.intro: Kets are written ∣ψ⟩, with ∣+⟩ = (∣0⟩ + ∣1⟩)/√2 and ∣−⟩ = (∣0⟩ − ∣1⟩)/√2. Highlight: in 16.43 you compute the famous 70% chance that a tritium atom's electron stays put when its nucleus suddenly turns into helium.

topics.title: Dirac notation
topics.goal: Read and write kets ∣ψ⟩, bras ⟨φ∣ and brackets ⟨φ∣ψ⟩.
checks: I can write kets, bras and brackets and compute overlaps.

ex.q: For ∣ψ⟩ = (1, i)/√2, write ⟨ψ∣ and check ⟨ψ∣ψ⟩ = 1.
Find ⟨0∣ψ⟩ and the probability of finding ∣0⟩.
Find ⟨+∣ψ⟩ and the probability of finding ∣+⟩.

topics.title: Operators as matrices
topics.goal: Write an operator as a matrix in a chosen basis.
checks: I can write any operator as a matrix of elements ⟨i∣A∣j⟩.

ex.q: Build the matrix of σx from its elements ⟨i∣σx∣j⟩.
Write σz in the basis {∣+⟩, ∣−⟩}. Which familiar matrix do you get?
In the oscillator energy basis, x only connects neighbouring levels. What does its matrix look like? (See 16.13.)
ex.a: Tridiagonal with √n entries beside an empty diagonal.

topics.title: The completeness relation
topics.search: completeness relation resolution of the identity
topics.goal: Inserting a sum of ∣n⟩⟨n∣ = 1 to change basis.
checks: I can insert a sum of ∣n⟩⟨n∣ = 1 to change basis.

ex.q: Show ⟨φ∣ψ⟩ equals the sum over n of ⟨φ∣n⟩⟨n∣ψ⟩.
Using ∫∣x⟩⟨x∣ dx = 1, explain why ψ(x) = ⟨x∣ψ⟩.
ex.a: Projecting onto ∣x⟩ picks the amplitude at x.

topics.title: The postulates
topics.goal: The rules: states, observables, measurement, evolution.
checks: I can state every postulate.

ex.q: List the postulates in your own words.
Which postulate produces probabilities?
Which one seems strangest to you, and why?

topics.title: Observables are Hermitian
topics.goal: Every measurable quantity is a Hermitian operator.
checks: I can tell whether an operator can be an observable.

ex.q: Why must observables have real eigenvalues?
Is iσx an observable?
Is σx + σz an observable? Find its eigenvalues.

topics.title: The measurement postulate
topics.goal: Outcomes are eigenvalues; probabilities are squared overlaps.
checks: I can compute outcome probabilities, averages and post-measurement states.

ex.q: The state (3∣0⟩ + 4∣1⟩)/5 is measured with σz. Give the probabilities and ⟨σz⟩.
Measure σx on ∣0⟩. Give the probabilities and ⟨σx⟩.
If the result was −1, what is the state afterwards?

topics.title: Position and momentum operators
topics.goal: p̂ = −iħ d/dx and why.
checks: I can apply p = −iħ d/dx and recognize its eigenfunctions.

ex.q: Apply p to e^(ikx).
Is sin(kx) a momentum eigenstate? What momenta does it contain?
Find ⟨p²⟩ for the box ground state and check ⟨p²⟩/2m equals E₁.

topics.title: The canonical commutator
topics.goal: The algebra behind uncertainty.
checks: I can derive and use [x, p] = iħ.

ex.q: Derive [x, p] = iħ by acting on a test function f(x).
Compute [x², p].
Show [p, f(x)] = −iħ f′(x).

topics.title: The general uncertainty principle
topics.goal: Derive ΔA·ΔB ≥ ½∣⟨[A, B]⟩∣.
checks: I can apply ΔAΔB ≥ ½|⟨[A, B]⟩|.

ex.q: For spin, find the bound on ΔSₓΔS_y in the state ∣↑⟩ and check that it is reached.
ex.a: ħ²/4, reached since each spread is ħ/2

ex.q: Can ΔAΔB = 0 for non-commuting A and B? Give an example.
ex.a: Yes, if ⟨[A, B]⟩ = 0 in that state, for example Sₓ and S_y in an Sₓ eigenstate (bound 0).

topics.title: Compatible observables
topics.goal: Commuting observables can be known together.
checks: I can tell which observables can be known together.

ex.q: Do L² and L_z commute? Lₓ and L_z?
For a free particle, H and p commute. What does that let you do?
Which four observables label hydrogen's states?

topics.title: Position and momentum space
topics.goal: They are Fourier transforms of each other.
checks: I can move between ψ(x) and φ(p) with a Fourier transform.

ex.q: A Gaussian has width σ in x. What is its width in p? (Use 5.14.)
Why is the Gaussian the state with ΔxΔp exactly ħ/2?
ex.a: It minimizes the Fourier width product.

topics.title: Time evolution
checks: I can build U = e^(−iHt/ħ) and apply it.

ex.q: Why is U unitary?
A spin has H = (ħω/2)σz. Write U(t) and apply it to ∣+⟩.
ex.a: U = diag(e^(−iωt/2), e^(iωt/2)): the state precesses about z

ex.q: After what time does ∣+⟩ return to itself (up to a phase)?

topics.title: Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures
topics.goal: Three equivalent ways to describe time evolution.
checks: I can describe evolution either by moving states or by moving operators.

ex.q: Write the Heisenberg equation dA/dt = (i/ħ)[H, A].
For a free particle, find x(t) in the Heisenberg picture.

topics.title: Ehrenfest's theorem
topics.goal: Averages obey classical equations.
checks: I can show averages follow classical laws.

ex.q: Show d⟨x⟩/dt = ⟨p⟩/m and d⟨p⟩/dt = −⟨V′(x)⟩.
Why is ⟨V′(x)⟩ generally not V′(⟨x⟩)? For which potential are they equal?
ex.a: Only for potentials at most quadratic, like the oscillator.

topics.title: Ladder operators
topics.goal: Solve the oscillator algebraically with a and a†.
checks: I can solve the oscillator with a and a†.

ex.q: With a = (mωx + ip)/√(2mħω), show [a, a†] = 1.
Show H = ħω(a†a + ½).
Compute a†a†∣0⟩.
Find ⟨n∣x²∣n⟩.

topics.title: Coherent states
topics.goal: The most classical-looking quantum states (laser light).
checks: I can describe coherent states and their photon statistics.

ex.q: A coherent state obeys a∣α⟩ = α∣α⟩. What distribution do its photon counts follow? (See 6.8.)
If the average photon number is 100, what is its spread?
Why is laser light well described by coherent states?
ex.a: Lasers emit classical-like waves with Poisson photon counts.

topics.title: Angular momentum algebra
topics.goal: [Lx, Ly] = iħLz and what it implies.
checks: I can use [Lₓ, L_y] = iħL_z and ladder operators L±.

ex.q: Show [L², L_z] = 0 follows from the basic commutators.
Show [L_z, L₊] = ħL₊. What does L₊ do to m?
Why must l be a whole or half-whole number?
ex.a: The ladder must stop at both ends.

topics.title: Orbital angular momentum
topics.search: orbital angular momentum and spherical harmonics
topics.goal: Eigenstates ∣l, m⟩ and their shapes.
checks: I can use L² = ħ²l(l + 1) and L_z = mħ.

ex.q: For l = 1, find the length of L and the largest L_z. What is the smallest angle L can make with z?
How many m values are there for l = 3?

topics.title: Spin one-half
topics.goal: Spin up and down; spin along any axis.
checks: I can write spin states along any axis.

ex.q: Spin up along the direction (θ, φ) is (cos(θ/2), e^(iφ) sin(θ/2)). Check it for the x-axis.
A spin points up along an axis tilted 60° from z. What is the chance of measuring up along z?

topics.title: The Bloch sphere
topics.goal: Every spin-½ state as a point on a sphere.
checks: I can place states on the Bloch sphere.

ex.q: Where do orthogonal states sit relative to each other?
Where do mixed states (16.25) live?

topics.title: Sequential Stern-Gerlach
topics.goal: Measuring z then x then z again scrambles z.
checks: I can predict beams through a chain of magnets.

ex.q: N atoms in the z-up beam pass an x-magnet; keep x-up and send them through a z-magnet. How many come out up and down?
ex.a: N/4 up and N/4 down (N/2 were lost at the x-magnet)

ex.q: Remove the x-magnet. What comes out?

topics.title: Larmor precession
topics.search: Larmor precession spin in magnetic field
topics.goal: Spin precesses in a magnetic field.
checks: I can compute precession frequencies.

ex.q: Electrons precess at about 28 GHz per tesla. What frequency in Earth's 50 μT field?
Describe the motion of a tilted spin on the Bloch sphere.
ex.a: It circles the field axis at fixed tilt.

topics.title: Rabi oscillations
topics.goal: Driving a two-level system flips it back and forth.
checks: I can predict flip probabilities under a resonant drive.

ex.q: The flip probability is sin²(Ωt/2). How long is a π pulse? A π/2 pulse?
Detuned by Δ, the maximum flip probability is Ω²/(Ω² + Δ²). What is it when Δ = Ω?

topics.title: Adding angular momenta
topics.search: addition of angular momentum Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
topics.goal: Combine two spins into total spin.
checks: I can list the total angular momenta from combining two.

ex.q: Combine two spin-½. Which totals appear and how many states each?
Combine l = 1 with s = ½. Check the state count.
Combine 1 with 1.

topics.title: Singlets and triplets
topics.goal: Two spin-½ particles make spin 0 or 1 (key to helium and bonding).
checks: I can write the triplet and singlet and their swap symmetry.

ex.q: Write the four states.
Which are symmetric under swapping the particles?
Find S₁ · S₂ in the triplet and singlet using S² = S₁² + S₂² + 2S₁ · S₂.

topics.title: Selection rules from symmetry
topics.goal: Selection rules from symmetry.
checks: I can explain why some transitions are forbidden.

ex.q: Why can't hydrogen's 2s state decay straight to 1s by emitting one photon?
ex.a: A photon must carry away one unit of angular momentum

ex.q: Why is 2p → 1s allowed?

topics.title: Density matrices
topics.search: density matrix pure and mixed states
topics.goal: Describe uncertainty about the state itself.
checks: I can tell pure from mixed states.

ex.q: Write ρ for ∣+⟩ and for a 50/50 mixture of ∣0⟩ and ∣1⟩.
Compute tr(ρ²) for each.
Which measurement tells them apart?

topics.title: Partial trace
topics.goal: The state of one part of an entangled system.
checks: I can find the state of one half of a two-particle system.

ex.q: Trace out one qubit of (∣00⟩ + ∣11⟩)/√2.
Do the same for ∣0⟩⊗∣+⟩.
What does the first result say about the half you hold?
ex.a: It is maximally uncertain on its own.

topics.title: Schmidt decomposition
topics.goal: Measure how entangled two parts are.
checks: I can measure entanglement with Schmidt coefficients.

ex.q: Find the entanglement entropy of (∣00⟩ + ∣11⟩)/√2.
What does a product state look like?

topics.title: Generalized measurements
topics.goal: Measurements beyond projections.
checks: I can explain why POVMs go beyond projections.

ex.q: Can you perfectly tell ∣0⟩ from ∣+⟩ in one shot? What can a POVM do instead?
ex.a: No; a POVM can be sometimes certain and otherwise say "don't know"

ex.q: Why can a POVM on a qubit have three outcomes?
ex.a: Its outcomes need not be orthogonal.

topics.title: Open systems
topics.search: Lindblad master equation open quantum systems
topics.goal: How systems lose coherence to their environment.
checks: I can describe T₁ and T₂ decay.

ex.q: Under pure dephasing, what happens to the diagonal and off-diagonal parts of ρ?
What do T₁ and T₂ measure?
ex.a: Energy relaxation and loss of phase coherence.

topics.title: Symmetries and generators
topics.goal: Translations generate momentum; rotations generate angular momentum.
checks: I can link symmetries to conserved quantities in quantum mechanics.

ex.q: Show e^(−ipa/ħ) shifts ψ(x) to ψ(x − a). (Use the Taylor series, 2.29.)
If [H, p] = 0, what is conserved?

topics.title: Parity and time reversal
topics.search: parity and time reversal quantum mechanics
topics.goal: Discrete symmetries and their consequences.
checks: I can use parity to simplify problems.

ex.q: For a box centred at 0, which states are even and which odd?
ex.a: Odd n even, even n odd (for the centred box)

ex.q: Why is ⟨x⟩ = 0 in any parity eigenstate?
What does time reversal do to a wavefunction?

topics.title: Kramers degeneracy
topics.goal: Time reversal forces degeneracy for half-integer spin.
checks: I can state Kramers' theorem and one consequence.

ex.q: State the theorem.
ex.a: With time-reversal symmetry, half-integer-spin levels are at least doubly degenerate

ex.q: Why does it matter for topological insulators (17.58)?

topics.title: The propagator
topics.goal: The amplitude to go from x to x′ in time t.
checks: I can use the propagator to evolve a state.

ex.q: Write the free-particle propagator.
Describe what happens to a state that starts as δ(x).
ex.a: It spreads at once over all space.

topics.title: Deriving the path integral
topics.goal: Derive the path integral from the Schrödinger equation.
checks: I can derive the path integral from time slices.

ex.q: Slice the time into N steps and insert completeness (16.1c) between them.
Show each slice contributes e^(iL dt/ħ).

topics.title: The WKB approximation
topics.goal: Semiclassical solutions and tunneling rates.
checks: I can estimate tunneling and quantization semiclassically.

ex.q: Write the WKB tunneling factor.
Apply ∮ p dx = (n + ½)h to the oscillator. Is the result exact?

topics.title: The variational principle
topics.goal: Estimate ground-state energies.
checks: I can estimate ground-state energies with trial functions.

ex.q: Use e^(−bx²) for the oscillator. What do you find?
A Gaussian trial function for hydrogen gives −(8/3π) × 13.6 eV. Evaluate it. Why is it above −13.6 eV?
ex.a: About −11.5 eV; the variational estimate is always above the true value.

topics.title: Perturbation theory
topics.goal: Correct energies and states for small changes.
checks: I can compute first- and second-order energy shifts.

ex.q: A box gets a uniform extra potential ε. What is the shift?
An oscillator gets an extra λx. Find the first-order shift, then the exact answer by completing the square.
Helium: ignoring electron repulsion gives −108.8 eV; first-order repulsion adds +34 eV. Compare with the measured −79.0 eV.

topics.title: Degenerate perturbation theory
topics.goal: Handle equal-energy states.
checks: I can split degenerate levels by diagonalizing.

ex.q: Two degenerate states are coupled by V. Diagonalize [[0, V], [V, 0]].
Why does hydrogen's n = 2 level show a linear Stark effect?

topics.title: Fermi's golden rule
topics.search: time-dependent perturbation theory Fermi's golden rule
topics.goal: Transition rates (why atoms emit light at the rates they do).
checks: I can use transition rates.

ex.q: Write the golden rule.
Why does it lead to exponential decay?
ex.a: A constant rate means a constant fraction decays each moment.

topics.title: Selection rules
topics.goal: Which jumps are allowed.
checks: I can tell allowed from forbidden transitions.

ex.q: Which are allowed: 3d → 2p, 3d → 1s, 3s → 2p, 2s → 1s?
Why must l change by 1?

topics.title: The adiabatic theorem
topics.goal: Slow changes keep a system in its eigenstate.
checks: I can predict what slow and fast changes do.

ex.q: A box widens slowly from L to 2L. What happens to the ground-state energy?
ex.a: It stays in the ground state; the energy falls to a quarter

ex.q: What happens if it widens suddenly? (See 16.43.)

topics.title: The Berry phase
topics.goal: A phase picked up purely from the path's geometry.
checks: I can compute geometric phases for spin.

ex.q: A spin-½ follows a field around a cone of solid angle Ω. Its Berry phase is −Ω/2. Find it for a loop around the equator.
Which classical effect from 8.26 is a cousin of this?

topics.title: The sudden approximation
topics.goal: What happens when changes are fast.
checks: I can compute overlaps after sudden changes.

ex.q: A box suddenly doubles in width. What is the chance the particle ends in the new ground state?
Tritium beta-decays to helium-3. The 1s overlap between charges 1 and 2 is (2√2/3)³. What is the chance the electron stays in 1s?

topics.title: Scattering cross sections
topics.goal: How collisions are described and measured.
checks: I can explain what a cross section measures.

ex.q: What is the classical cross section of a hard sphere of radius a?
How big is a barn?
How does Rutherford's cross section depend on angle?

topics.title: The Born approximation
topics.goal: Weak-scattering results.
checks: I can relate scattering to the Fourier transform of the potential.

ex.q: Why is the Born amplitude a Fourier transform of V?
How does electron scattering reveal the proton's size?
ex.a: The scattering deviates from a point charge's at large momentum transfer.

topics.title: Partial waves
topics.goal: Scattering by angular momentum channels.
checks: I can explain s-wave scattering at low energy.

ex.q: Why does only l = 0 matter at low energy?
ex.a: Higher l are kept away by the centrifugal barrier

ex.q: A hard sphere's low-energy quantum cross section is 4πa². Compare with Exercise 1 of 16.44.

topics.title: Scattering resonances
topics.goal: Peaks in cross sections and Breit-Wigner shapes.
checks: I can read lifetimes from resonance widths.

ex.q: What shape does a resonance peak have? (Compare 2.21 Exercise 3.)
Look up the Ramsauer-Townsend effect. What is strange about it?
ex.a: Noble-gas atoms become almost transparent to slow electrons.

topics.title: Theoretical Minimum: quantum mechanics
topics.goal: A full lecture course.
checks: I can follow every lecture's main calculation.

ex.q: Redo the lecture's spin-measurement examples without notes.

topics.title: MIT 8.05
topics.search: MIT 8.05 Barton Zwiebach quantum physics II
topics.goal: Full course on the formalism.
checks: I can do the problem sets.

ex.q: Do the first three problem sets.

topics.title: MIT 8.06
topics.goal: Full course on approximation methods and applications.
checks: I can do approximation-method problems.

ex.q: Do the problem sets on perturbation theory and WKB.

topics.title: Griffiths-style lectures
topics.goal: A lecture series that follows Griffiths' textbook.
checks: I can solve textbook problems end to end.

ex.q: A spin-½ starts up along z in a field along x with H = (ħω/2)σₓ. Find the chance of measuring down along z at time t.

parts.name: Quantum Matter
parts.title: Atoms, molecules and quantum matter
parts.intro: This is your helium part. Highlight: in 17.50b you predict the temperature at which helium-4 turns superfluid using only its density, its mass and Bose statistics, and land within 50% of the real 2.17 K.

topics.title: Solving hydrogen
topics.goal: Separate into radial and angular parts; Eₙ = −13.6 eV/n².
checks: I can use Eₙ = −13.6 eV/n².

ex.q: How much energy does it take to ionize hydrogen from n = 2?
Find the wavelength and colour of the n = 4 → 2 line.

topics.title: Hydrogen orbitals in 3D
topics.goal: Picture 1s, 2p, 3d and their nodes.
checks: I can count radial and angular nodes.

ex.q: How many radial and angular nodes does a 3d orbital have?
Why are only s orbitals non-zero at the nucleus?
ex.a: Only l = 0 has no centrifugal barrier.

topics.title: Quantum numbers
topics.search: quantum numbers n l m s explained
topics.goal: What each quantum number counts.
checks: I can list all allowed (n, l, m, s).

ex.q: List every (l, m) for n = 3. How many electrons fit?
ex.a: l = 0 (m = 0), l = 1 (m = −1, 0, 1), l = 2 (m = −2 to 2): 9 orbitals, 18 electrons

ex.q: Why does m run from −l to l?

topics.title: Hydrogen's hidden symmetry
topics.search: hidden symmetry of hydrogen SO(4) degeneracy
topics.goal: Why 2s and 2p have the same energy.
checks: I can explain the n² degeneracy.

ex.q: How many states (ignoring spin) share n = 3?
Which conserved vector from 8.46 is behind this?

topics.title: Fine structure
topics.goal: Small splittings from spin and relativity.
checks: I can estimate fine-structure splittings.

ex.q: Fine structure is about α² × 13.6 eV with α = 1/137. Estimate it.
Sodium's yellow doublet is at 589.0 and 589.6 nm. Find the energy splitting.

topics.title: The Zeeman effect
topics.goal: Level splitting in magnetic fields.
checks: I can predict how levels split in a field.

ex.q: Into how many lines does a 2p → 1s line split in the normal Zeeman effect?
What makes the "anomalous" Zeeman effect anomalous?

topics.title: The Stark effect
topics.goal: Level splitting in electric fields.
checks: I can explain when the Stark effect is linear.

ex.q: Why does hydrogen's ground state have no linear Stark shift?
Why does n = 2 have one? (See 16.38.)

topics.title: The 21 cm line
topics.goal: The spin flip that maps hydrogen across the galaxy.
checks: I can compute the hyperfine transition energy.

ex.q: Find the energy and frequency of a 21.1 cm photon.
Why can radio telescopes map the galaxy's spiral arms with it?
Why was it drawn on the Pioneer plaque?
ex.a: As a universal unit of length and time.

topics.title: The Lamb shift
topics.goal: A tiny shift only quantum electrodynamics explains.
checks: I can say what the Lamb shift is and what explains it.

ex.q: 2s and 2p are split by 1058 MHz. Convert to eV.
Which theory explains it, and what is the physical cause?
ex.a: QED: vacuum fluctuations jiggle the electron.

topics.title: Identical particles
topics.goal: Swapping identical particles leaves physics unchanged.
checks: I can build symmetric and antisymmetric two-particle states.

ex.q: Write symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of ψ_a(x₁)ψ_b(x₂).
Show the antisymmetric one vanishes when both particles are in the same state.

topics.title: Bosons and fermions
topics.goal: Integer spin → bosons; half-integer → fermions.
checks: I can classify particles by spin.

ex.q: Boson or fermion: electron, photon, proton, helium-4 atom, helium-3 atom, deuteron, Higgs boson, neutrino, hydrogen atom.
ex.a: F, B, F, B, F, B, B, F, B.

topics.title: The Pauli exclusion principle
topics.goal: No two fermions can share a state.
checks: I can use Pauli exclusion to fill levels.

ex.q: Put three electrons in a 1D box (15.12). Which levels fill?
ex.a: Two in n = 1 (opposite spins), one in n = 2

ex.q: Why would all matter collapse without the exclusion principle?
ex.a: All electrons would drop into the lowest state.

topics.title: Why helium-4 is a boson
topics.search: why helium-4 is a boson composite particle spin
topics.goal: Count spins: 2 protons + 2 neutrons + 2 electrons give a whole number.
checks: I can decide whether any atom is a boson by counting spin-½ parts.

ex.q: Count the spin-½ constituents of helium-4 and helium-3.
Is rubidium-87 a boson? Lithium-6?
Why does an even number of half-integer spins always add to a whole number?
ex.a: Pairs of halves make whole numbers.

topics.title: The spin-statistics theorem
topics.goal: Why spin decides boson or fermion (it needs relativity).
checks: I can state the theorem.

ex.q: State the theorem.
Why did Pauli's proof need special relativity?
ex.a: It relies on causality and Lorentz invariance.

topics.title: Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics
topics.goal: How bosons crowd together and fermions avoid each other.
checks: I can compute occupation numbers.

ex.q: Write the two occupation formulas.
Evaluate both at E − μ = kT.
What do both become when E − μ ≫ kT?

topics.title: The exchange interaction
topics.goal: A "force" from symmetry alone; why magnets exist.
checks: I can explain exchange as symmetry plus Coulomb repulsion.

ex.q: Why do same-spin electrons stay farther apart, and why does that lower the energy?
ex.a: An antisymmetric spatial part keeps them apart, lowering repulsion

ex.q: Is exchange a new force?
ex.a: No: it is Coulomb repulsion plus symmetry.

topics.title: Helium and multi-electron atoms
topics.goal: Electron repulsion; para- and orthohelium.
checks: I can describe helium's two families of states.

ex.q: What are parahelium and orthohelium?
Helium's two ionization energies are 24.6 and 54.4 eV. Compare their sum with 16.37 Exercise 3.

topics.title: Hund's rules and term symbols
topics.goal: Name an atom's ground state, for example carbon's ³P₀.
checks: I can write ground-state term symbols.

ex.q: Find the ground terms of carbon, nitrogen and oxygen.
State Hund's three rules in order.
ex.a: Maximize S, then L; then J lowest for less than half-full shells, highest otherwise.

topics.title: The periodic table from quantum mechanics
topics.search: periodic table explained by quantum mechanics
topics.goal: Shell filling from quantum numbers and the Pauli principle.
checks: I can explain the row lengths.

ex.q: Why do the rows hold 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32 elements?
ex.a: Shell capacities 2l + 1 combined with the energy ordering

ex.q: Why does 4s fill before 3d?

topics.title: The simplest chemical bond
topics.search: hydrogen molecule ion covalent bond quantum
topics.goal: Why sharing an electron lowers the energy.
checks: I can explain bonding and antibonding in H₂⁺.

ex.q: Which combination of atomic orbitals bonds, and why?
ex.a: The symmetric one, which builds up charge between the nuclei

ex.q: Why does the antibonding state push the nuclei apart?
ex.a: It has a node between them.

topics.title: The Born-Oppenheimer approximation
topics.goal: Separate fast electrons from slow nuclei.
checks: I can justify separating electrons from nuclei.

ex.q: A proton is 1836 times heavier than an electron. For equal kinetic energies, how many times faster is the electron?
What is a potential energy curve of a molecule?
ex.a: Electronic energy as a function of nuclear separation.

topics.title: Molecular rotation and vibration
topics.search: rotational and vibrational spectra of molecules
topics.goal: Quantized rotation and vibration.
checks: I can compute vibrational and rotational line positions.

ex.q: Rotational levels are ħ²J(J + 1)/(2I). How does the spacing between neighbours change with J?
HCl vibrates at 2886 cm⁻¹. Find the energy in eV and the wavelength.

topics.title: Raman scattering
topics.goal: Light scattering with energy exchange.
checks: I can explain Stokes and anti-Stokes lines.

ex.q: What are Stokes and anti-Stokes lines?
ex.a: Light losing or gaining vibrational energy

ex.q: Why are anti-Stokes lines weaker? (Use 10.15.)

topics.title: How lasers work
topics.goal: Bosonic photons copying each other; population inversion.
checks: I can explain population inversion and stimulated emission.

ex.q: Why can't a two-level system lase in steady state?
ex.a: Pumping can at best equalize the populations

ex.q: Why does the photons' bosonic nature matter?
ex.a: Emitted photons join the same mode.

topics.title: The Fermi energy
topics.goal: Electrons in metals fill states up to the Fermi energy.
checks: I can compute E_F = (ħ²/2m)(3π²n)^(2/3).

ex.q: Copper has n = 8.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³. Find E_F in eV.
Find the Fermi temperature E_F/k.
Why do metal electrons barely add to the heat capacity?
ex.a: Only electrons near E_F can be excited.

topics.title: Degeneracy pressure
topics.search: degeneracy pressure white dwarfs neutron stars
topics.goal: The Pauli principle holds up dead stars.
checks: I can explain what holds up white dwarfs.

ex.q: A white dwarf has the Sun's mass (2 × 10³⁰ kg) and Earth's radius. Find its density.
What holds up a neutron star?
ex.a: Neutron degeneracy pressure and nuclear forces.

topics.title: The Chandrasekhar limit
topics.goal: Above about 1.4 solar masses, electron degeneracy fails.
checks: I can explain why white dwarfs have a maximum mass.

ex.q: What is the limit, roughly?
Why does electron pressure fail when electrons become relativistic?
ex.a: Pressure grows more slowly than gravity

ex.q: Why do supernovae from this limit make good distance markers?
ex.a: They explode at nearly the same mass and brightness.

topics.title: Bloch's theorem
topics.goal: Electrons in a periodic potential.
checks: I can state Bloch's theorem.

ex.q: State it in one line.
Why does k only need to run from −π/a to π/a?
ex.a: Adding 2π/a to k gives the same state.

topics.title: The Kronig-Penney model
topics.goal: A solvable periodic potential that produces band gaps.
checks: I can explain where band gaps open.

ex.q: Why do gaps open at k = ±π/a? (Think of Bragg reflection, 9.20.)
Sketch E(k) with two bands and a gap.

topics.title: Bands, conductors and insulators
topics.goal: Gaps between bands decide conductivity.
checks: I can classify materials by band gap.

ex.q: Classify copper (no gap), silicon (1.1 eV) and diamond (5.5 eV).
Why is diamond transparent while silicon looks dark?
ex.a: Diamond's gap exceeds visible photon energies; silicon absorbs visible light.

topics.title: Holes
topics.goal: Missing electrons that act like positive particles.
checks: I can explain holes as positive carriers.

ex.q: Which measurement from 11.12b shows holes are positive?
Give an everyday analogy for a hole.

topics.title: Doping and the p-n junction
topics.search: how semiconductors work doping p-n junction
topics.goal: n- and p-type, diodes.
checks: I can explain n- and p-type material and diodes.

ex.q: Phosphorus or boron in silicon: which makes n-type?
Why does a p-n junction pass current one way only?
ex.a: The depletion region blocks reverse current.

topics.title: Transistors
topics.goal: Switching current with voltage.
checks: I can explain a MOSFET as a voltage-controlled switch.

ex.q: How does the gate voltage switch a MOSFET?
ex.a: Its field opens or closes a conducting channel

ex.q: Why can a chip hold tens of billions of transistors?

topics.title: LEDs and solar cells
topics.search: how LEDs and solar cells work band gap
topics.goal: Band gaps set light colors and absorption.
checks: I can link band gaps to colours.

ex.q: GaN has a 3.4 eV gap. What wavelength does it emit?
A solar cell's gap is 1.1 eV. What happens to photons below that energy, and to the extra energy of photons above it?
ex.a: They pass through; the excess becomes heat.

topics.title: The tunnel diode
topics.goal: A device whose current falls as voltage rises, thanks to tunneling.
checks: I can explain negative resistance from tunneling.

ex.q: Why does a heavily doped, very thin junction let electrons tunnel?
ex.a: The barrier is only nanometres thick

ex.q: Why does the current fall as the voltage rises over part of the curve?

topics.title: Quantum dots
topics.goal: Artificial atoms; color from size.
checks: I can predict colour change with dot size.

ex.q: Using 15.12, what happens to the confinement energy if a dot is half as wide?
Do smaller dots glow redder or bluer?

topics.title: Phonons
topics.goal: Quantized lattice vibrations.
checks: I can describe sound as quantized vibrations.

ex.q: What is the energy of one phonon of angular frequency ω?
Which heat-capacity model from 10.19 uses phonons?

topics.title: Quasiparticles
topics.goal: Collective behaviour that acts like a particle.
checks: I can name and explain several quasiparticles.

ex.q: Name five quasiparticles.
Why are they called "quasi"?

topics.title: Magnons
topics.goal: Quantized waves of magnetism.
checks: I can describe spin waves.

ex.q: What is a magnon?
Bloch's law says magnetization falls as T^(3/2) at low T. What causes the fall?

topics.title: Excitons, polaritons and plasmons
topics.goal: Three more quasiparticles and where they appear.
checks: I can tell these quasiparticles apart.

ex.q: An exciton is a hydrogen-like electron-hole pair. Its binding is 13.6 eV × (μ/mₑ)/ε². Estimate it for μ = 0.1 mₑ and ε = 10.
Why does gold in medieval stained glass look red?
ex.a: Plasmons in gold nanoparticles absorb green light.

topics.title: Magnetism is quantum
topics.search: Bohr-van Leeuwen theorem magnetism is quantum
topics.goal: Classical physics predicts no magnetism at all.
checks: I can state the Bohr-van Leeuwen theorem.

ex.q: Magnetic forces do no work. Use this to explain why classical statistical mechanics predicts no magnetism.
ex.a: The partition function does not depend on B

ex.q: What then makes a fridge magnet work?

topics.title: The Heisenberg model
topics.goal: Spin-spin coupling as the source of magnetic order.
checks: I can write the Heisenberg Hamiltonian.

ex.q: Write H = −J Σ Sᵢ · Sⱼ. Which sign of J favours aligned spins?
Where does J come from?

topics.title: Superconductivity
topics.goal: Electron pairs act as bosons and flow without resistance.
checks: I can explain Cooper pairs and the energy gap.

ex.q: Why is a Cooper pair a boson?
The gap is about 3.5kT_c. Estimate it for niobium (T_c = 9.2 K).

topics.title: The Meissner effect and flux pinning
topics.search: Meissner effect quantum levitation flux pinning
topics.goal: Superconductors expel and pin magnetic fields.
checks: I can tell a superconductor from a perfect conductor.

ex.q: What would a perfect conductor do with a field already inside it when cooled? What does a superconductor do?
ex.a: A perfect conductor traps it; a superconductor expels it

ex.q: Why does a pinned superconductor hover locked in place above a magnet?
ex.a: Flux lines are pinned at defects.

topics.title: Josephson junctions and SQUIDs
topics.goal: Supercurrents tunnel through barriers; ultra-sensitive magnetometers.
checks: I can use f = 2eV/h.

ex.q: Find the Josephson frequency for 1 mV.
What can SQUIDs measure in the human brain?

topics.title: Flux quantization
topics.goal: Magnetic flux comes in units of h/2e.
checks: I can compute the flux quantum.

ex.q: Compute h/(2e).
Why did the 2 prove that charge carriers come in pairs?
ex.a: The charge in h/q came out as 2e.

topics.title: High-temperature superconductors
topics.goal: An unsolved problem in physics.
checks: I can say why cuprates matter and what is unknown.

ex.q: Why was T_c = 92 K for YBCO a big deal?
ex.a: It works with cheap liquid nitrogen (77 K)

ex.q: What remains unexplained?

topics.title: Superfluid helium
topics.goal: Helium-4 below 2.17 K flows with zero viscosity.
checks: I can describe helium II's strange behaviour.

ex.q: Why is 2.17 K called the lambda point?
ex.a: The heat-capacity curve looks like λ

ex.q: What happens to helium's viscosity below it?

topics.title: The 1963 superfluid film
topics.search: Liquid Helium II the Superfluid 1963 Alfred Leitner film
topics.goal: Classic footage: creeping films and the fountain effect.
checks: I can explain the creeping film and fountain effect.

ex.q: Why does superfluid helium climb out of its container?
ex.a: A thin film creeps up the walls without friction

ex.q: Why does heating one side make a fountain?
Describe the two-fluid model.
ex.a: A normal fluid and a zero-viscosity superfluid mixed together.

topics.title: Second sound
topics.goal: Heat travels as a wave.
checks: I can explain heat travelling as a wave.

ex.q: What oscillates in second sound?
ex.a: The ratio of normal to superfluid parts, carrying temperature

ex.q: Why can't an ordinary liquid do this?

topics.title: Quantized vortices
topics.goal: Rotation comes in discrete whirlpools.
checks: I can compute the circulation quantum.

ex.q: Compute h/m for helium-4 (6.65 × 10⁻²⁷ kg).
What forms in a rotating bucket of superfluid?

topics.title: Superfluid helium-3
topics.search: superfluid helium-3 Cooper pairs of atoms
topics.goal: Fermionic helium-3 pairs up at about 2.5 mK.
checks: I can explain why helium-3 needs pairing.

ex.q: Why must fermionic helium-3 atoms pair before going superfluid?
About what temperature is needed?

topics.title: Bose-Einstein condensation
topics.goal: Many bosons in one quantum state.
checks: I can state when condensation happens.

ex.q: When does a gas condense, in terms of de Broglie wavelength and spacing?
ex.a: When the de Broglie wavelength matches the spacing

ex.q: Write the thermal wavelength h/√(2πmkT). What happens to it as T falls?

topics.title: The first BEC
topics.goal: How rubidium was cooled to a BEC.
checks: I can describe the 1995 experiment.

ex.q: Which atom, and roughly what temperature?
What did the famous velocity image show?
ex.a: A sharp peak of atoms at nearly zero velocity.

topics.title: The condensation temperature
topics.goal: Estimate the condensation temperature from density and mass.
checks: I can compute T_c = (2πħ²/(mk))(n/2.612)^(2/3).

ex.q: Liquid helium-4 has n = 2.18 × 10²⁸ m⁻³ and m = 6.65 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Compute T_c.
The real lambda point is 2.17 K. Why is it lower?

topics.title: Laser cooling
topics.goal: Slowing atoms with light.
checks: I can estimate photon recoil.

ex.q: A rubidium atom (1.44 × 10⁻²⁵ kg) absorbs a 780 nm photon. Find its speed change.
About how many photons stop an atom moving at 300 m/s?

topics.title: Reaching millikelvin
topics.search: dilution refrigerator how to reach millikelvin
topics.goal: How labs reach near absolute zero.
checks: I can explain a dilution refrigerator.

ex.q: What happens when a helium-3 and helium-4 mixture is cooled below about 0.9 K?
ex.a: It separates into two phases, and helium-3 crossing between them cools

ex.q: Which technology needs these fridges today?

topics.title: Ultracold Fermi gases
topics.goal: Fermions cooled until Pauli exclusion dominates.
checks: I can explain Pauli blocking in a gas.

ex.q: Why does a cold Fermi gas stay larger than a Bose gas with the same number of atoms?
Name two fermionic atoms used in labs.

topics.title: The Mott insulator
topics.search: optical lattice Mott insulator superfluid transition
topics.goal: Atoms in egg-crate light patterns.
checks: I can describe the superfluid to Mott transition.

ex.q: What happens to a BEC when the optical lattice is made very deep?
Why do the interference peaks vanish?
ex.a: Phase coherence between sites is lost.

topics.title: The BEC-BCS crossover
topics.goal: One continuum from tight molecules to loose Cooper pairs.
checks: I can describe one system that is both a BEC and a BCS superfluid.

ex.q: How does a Feshbach resonance (23.22) let experimenters tune between the two?
ex.a: It tunes the interaction strength through a resonance

ex.q: What is the unitary Fermi gas?
ex.a: The strongest possible interaction, where scattering is limited only by quantum mechanics.

topics.title: The quantum Hall effect
topics.goal: Resistance quantized in units of h/e².
checks: I can use R = h/(νe²).

ex.q: Compute h/e².
What resistance does the ν = 2 plateau have?
Why is it used as a resistance standard?

topics.title: The fractional quantum Hall effect
topics.goal: Quasiparticles with fractional charge.
checks: I can describe fractional charges.

ex.q: At ν = 1/3, what charge do the quasiparticles carry?
Why is this so surprising?

topics.title: Topological insulators
topics.goal: Insulating inside, conducting on the surface.
checks: I can explain protected surface states.

ex.q: What protects the surface states? (See 16.32.)
Name one topological insulator material.

topics.title: Graphene
topics.goal: Electrons that act like massless relativistic particles.
checks: I can describe graphene's massless electrons.

ex.q: Graphene electrons move at about 10⁶ m/s. What fraction of c is that?
Why do they act massless?
ex.a: Their energy is linear in momentum.

topics.title: Magic-angle graphene
topics.goal: Superconductivity from a twist of 1.1°.
checks: I can estimate moiré lengths.

ex.q: The moiré period is about a/θ with a = 0.246 nm. Find it for θ = 1.1°.
What happened at this angle in 2018?

topics.title: Anderson localization
topics.goal: Disorder can trap waves completely.
checks: I can explain how disorder traps waves.

ex.q: How can interference stop a wave from spreading?
ex.a: Paths reflecting in random directions cancel the spreading

ex.q: Name two systems where it has been seen.

topics.title: The Kondo effect
topics.goal: Why some metals' resistance rises as they cool.
checks: I can describe the resistance minimum.

ex.q: What strange behaviour did some metals show on cooling?
ex.a: Resistance rises again at low T

ex.q: What screens the impurity spin?

topics.title: Spintronics
topics.goal: Spin-based electronics in hard drives.
checks: I can explain giant magnetoresistance.

ex.q: Why does resistance depend on whether layers are magnetized the same way?
Which everyday device used it?

topics.title: The scanning tunneling microscope
topics.search: scanning tunneling microscope how it works
topics.goal: Imaging single atoms with tunneling current.
checks: I can explain the STM's sensitivity.

ex.q: Use 15.14 Exercise 4 to explain atomic resolution.
ex.a: The current changes about tenfold per 0.1 nm

ex.q: What does the tip actually measure?

topics.title: Moving single atoms
topics.search: A Boy and His Atom IBM
topics.goal: A movie made by moving single atoms.
checks: I can describe atom manipulation.

ex.q: Watch A Boy and His Atom. What molecules were moved, and on what surface?

topics.title: The nuclear shell model
topics.goal: Nucleons fill shells like electrons do.
checks: I know the magic numbers.

ex.q: List the magic numbers.
Why is lead-208 special?
Why is the alpha particle so stable?

topics.title: Alpha decay as tunneling
topics.goal: Alpha particles escape the nucleus by tunneling.
checks: I can explain the huge range of alpha half-lives.

ex.q: Why do small changes in decay energy change half-lives by factors of billions?
ex.a: Tunneling depends exponentially on the barrier

ex.q: What is the Geiger-Nuttall law?

topics.title: Tunneling powers the Sun
topics.search: quantum tunneling makes the sun shine
topics.goal: Fusion in the sun needs tunneling.
checks: I can show the Sun is too cold for classical fusion.

ex.q: Find the Coulomb barrier for two protons 1 fm apart (ke² = 1.44 MeV·fm).
Find kT at the Sun's core (15 million K).
How many times smaller is kT? What makes fusion happen anyway?

topics.title: The Mössbauer effect
topics.goal: Recoil-free gamma emission.
checks: I can explain recoil-free emission.

ex.q: Why does locking a nucleus in a crystal remove recoil?
ex.a: The whole crystal takes the recoil

ex.q: Pound and Rebka used it in a 22.5 m tower. Find the gravitational shift gh/c².

topics.title: A full solid-state course
topics.search: David Tong condensed matter / solid state physics lectures
topics.goal: A full course to tie the part together.
checks: I can solve mixed solid-state problems.

ex.q: Sodium has n = 2.65 × 10²⁸ m⁻³. Scale from copper (17.24) to find its Fermi energy.

parts.name: Quantum Computing
parts.title: Quantum information and computing
parts.intro: Gates: X flips, Z adds a minus sign to ∣1⟩, H turns ∣0⟩ into ∣+⟩. Highlight: in 18.13 you factor 15 with Shor's algorithm by hand.

topics.title: Qubits
topics.goal: A qubit is a two-level system in superposition.
checks: I can write a qubit state and predict measurement statistics.

ex.q: Write a general qubit state and its normalization condition.
How many real numbers describe a qubit, once normalization and global phase are removed?
You measure (∣0⟩ + ∣1⟩)/√2 a thousand times. About how many 0s?

topics.title: Classical logic and reversibility
topics.search: classical logic gates and reversible computing Toffoli gate
topics.goal: AND, OR, NOT, and why quantum gates must be reversible.
checks: I can explain why quantum gates must be reversible.

ex.q: Write AND's truth table. Why can't you recover the inputs from the output?
ex.a: Three inputs give 0, so 0 hides which

ex.q: The Toffoli gate flips a third bit when the first two are 1. Show it computes AND reversibly.
ex.a: With the target at 0, it becomes a AND b, and the inputs survive.

ex.q: Why does irreversible computing cost energy? (See 10.25.)

topics.title: Quantum gates
topics.goal: Apply single- and two-qubit gates as matrices.
checks: I can apply X, Z, H and CNOT.

ex.q: Compute X∣0⟩, Z∣+⟩ and H∣0⟩.
Show HZH = X.
Apply CNOT (first qubit controls) to ∣10⟩.

topics.title: Quantum circuits
topics.goal: Read and draw circuit diagrams.
checks: I can read a circuit and predict its output.

ex.q: Apply H to ∣0⟩ and measure. What do you get?
Apply H twice and measure. Why is the answer always 0? What does this have to do with interference?

topics.title: Making Bell states
topics.goal: Make entanglement with H then CNOT.
checks: I can build all four Bell states.

ex.q: Apply H to the first qubit of ∣00⟩, then CNOT. What state do you get?
Do the same starting from ∣01⟩, ∣10⟩ and ∣11⟩.
What do measurements of the two qubits always show for the first state?

topics.title: The no-cloning theorem
topics.goal: Unknown quantum states cannot be copied.
checks: I can prove no-cloning with linearity.

ex.q: Suppose U copies ∣0⟩ and ∣1⟩. Show linearity stops it copying ∣+⟩.
ex.a: U applied to the sum gives (∣00⟩ + ∣11⟩)/√2, not ∣+⟩∣+⟩

ex.q: CNOT "copies" ∣0⟩ and ∣1⟩ onto a blank qubit. What does it do to ∣+⟩∣0⟩?

topics.title: Quantum teleportation
topics.goal: Send a state using entanglement plus 2 classical bits.
checks: I can follow teleportation step by step.

ex.q: What resources does teleportation use?
ex.a: One Bell pair and two classical bits

ex.q: Which correction does Bob apply for each of Alice's four results?
Why can't this send information faster than light?

topics.title: Superdense coding
topics.goal: Send 2 bits with 1 qubit.
checks: I can send two bits with one qubit.

ex.q: Which four operations does Alice use to encode two bits?
Why does this need shared entanglement first?
ex.a: The Bell pair carries the extra capacity.

topics.title: BB84 key distribution
topics.goal: Eavesdropping is detectable.
checks: I can explain why eavesdropping shows up.

ex.q: What fraction of bits survive basis comparison?
Eve measures every photon in a random basis and resends. What error rate does she cause in the kept bits?

topics.title: E91
topics.goal: Security from Bell tests.
checks: I can explain entanglement-based security.

ex.q: How does checking a Bell inequality prove nobody listened?
What does "device-independent" mean here?
ex.a: Security holds even with untrusted equipment.

topics.title: The Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm
topics.goal: The first quantum speedup.
checks: I can explain the first quantum speedup.

ex.q: A function on 10 bits is promised to be constant or balanced. How many queries does a classical computer need to be certain in the worst case? The quantum algorithm?

topics.title: Phase kickback
topics.goal: How a control qubit picks up a phase from its target.
checks: I can show how a control qubit picks up a phase.

ex.q: Why does an oracle acting on a target in ∣−⟩ put (−1)^f(x) on the control?
ex.a: The target is an eigenstate, so the phase lands on the control.

topics.title: Bernstein-Vazirani and Simon
topics.goal: Two more oracle problems with quantum speedups.
checks: I can describe two more oracle speedups.

ex.q: Bernstein-Vazirani finds a hidden n-bit string. How many queries classically and quantumly?
Why was Simon's algorithm a stepping stone to Shor's?
ex.a: It found periods with exponential speedup.

topics.title: Grover's algorithm
topics.goal: √N search speedup.
checks: I can estimate Grover's speedup.

ex.q: About how many iterations to search 10⁶ items? Compare with classical.
For N = 4, how many iterations give certainty?
Why is the speedup only quadratic?
ex.a: It is proven optimal for unstructured search.

topics.title: The quantum Fourier transform
topics.goal: The engine of Shor's algorithm.
checks: I can apply the QFT to small cases.

ex.q: What is the QFT on one qubit?
What does it do to the uniform superposition?

topics.title: Shor's algorithm
topics.goal: Factoring fast enough to break RSA.
checks: I can follow Shor's algorithm on a small number.

ex.q: Factor 15 with a = 7: find the period r of 7ˣ mod 15, then compute gcd(7^(r/2) ± 1, 15).
Why does finding a period crack factoring?
ex.a: The period gives a square root of 1 that factors N

ex.q: Why does this threaten RSA encryption?
ex.a: RSA's security rests on factoring being hard.

topics.title: Phase estimation
topics.goal: Read out eigenvalues with a quantum computer.
checks: I can explain how eigenvalues are read out.

ex.q: How many ancilla qubits do you need for 10 bits of precision?
Which algorithm in this part uses phase estimation inside?

topics.title: The variational quantum eigensolver
topics.goal: Hybrid algorithms for chemistry.
checks: I can explain hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.

ex.q: Which part runs on the quantum chip and which on a normal computer?
ex.a: Energy measurement on the chip; parameter updates classically

ex.q: Which principle from 16.36 guarantees the answer is an upper bound?

topics.title: Quantum simulation
topics.goal: Using quantum systems to simulate quantum systems.
checks: I can explain Feynman's motivation.

ex.q: Why did Feynman argue nature should be simulated with quantum computers?
Name two things scientists most want to simulate.
ex.a: Molecules for chemistry and materials such as superconductors.

topics.title: Quantum error correction
topics.goal: Protect qubits without measuring them directly.
checks: I can detect and fix a bit flip without measuring the data.

ex.q: Encode ∣0⟩ → ∣000⟩ and ∣1⟩ → ∣111⟩. Which parities do you check?
The second qubit flips. What do the two parity checks show?
ex.a: Both checks fail, pointing to qubit 2

ex.q: Why does a full code also need to fix phase flips?

topics.title: The surface code
topics.goal: The leading error-correction scheme.
checks: I can estimate surface-code overheads.

ex.q: A distance-d surface code uses about 2d² physical qubits. How many for d = 5?
How does the logical error rate change as d grows?
ex.a: It falls exponentially if below threshold.

topics.title: The threshold theorem
topics.goal: Below an error rate, computation can scale.
checks: I can explain the threshold.

ex.q: Roughly what physical error rate must the surface code beat?
What happens if you add qubits above the threshold?

topics.title: Qubit hardware
topics.search: superconducting trapped ion photonic neutral atom qubits
topics.goal: Compare the hardware platforms.
checks: I can compare platforms.

ex.q: Give one strength and one weakness each for superconducting, trapped-ion, photonic and neutral-atom qubits.
ex.a: Superconducting: fast gates, needs millikelvin; ions: long coherence, slow gates; photons: room temperature, hard to make interact; neutral atoms: large arrays, slower cycles.

topics.title: Quantum advantage
topics.goal: What has actually been demonstrated.
checks: I can describe what has been shown.

ex.q: What task did Google's 2019 experiment perform?
Why did classical computing groups push back?
ex.a: Better classical algorithms cut the gap

ex.q: What did later experiments show about error correction below threshold?
ex.a: Larger codes gave lower logical error.

topics.title: Topological quantum computing
topics.goal: Qubits protected by topology.
checks: I can explain the idea of protection by topology.

ex.q: Why would braiding anyons give built-in protection?
ex.a: Information is stored in global braids, not local states

ex.q: Why is the field's status still debated?
ex.a: Clean evidence for the needed quasiparticles is disputed.

topics.title: Measurement-based computing
topics.search: measurement based quantum computing cluster states
topics.goal: Compute by measuring an entangled state.
checks: I can explain computing by measuring.

ex.q: What resource state is used?
Why does the order of measurements matter?
ex.a: Later measurement angles depend on earlier results.

topics.title: Adiabatic computing and annealing
topics.goal: Computing by slow evolution.
checks: I can link annealing to the adiabatic theorem.

ex.q: How is the answer encoded? (See 16.41.)
ex.a: In the ground state of a final Hamiltonian

ex.q: What limits the speed?

topics.title: Von Neumann entropy
topics.goal: Measure entanglement in bits.
checks: I can compute S = −tr(ρ log₂ ρ).

ex.q: Find S for ½I and for a pure state.
Find the entropy of one half of a Bell pair.

topics.title: Noise channels
topics.goal: Depolarizing, amplitude and phase damping.
checks: I can describe common noise models on the Bloch sphere.

ex.q: Write the bit-flip channel with probability p.
What does depolarizing noise do to the Bloch vector?
Which channel describes T₁ decay?

topics.title: The Holevo bound
topics.goal: A qubit can carry at most 1 classical bit.
checks: I can state how much classical information qubits carry.

ex.q: What is the most classical information n qubits can deliver?
Why doesn't superdense coding break this?
ex.a: It uses a pre-shared entangled qubit.

topics.title: Loophole-free Bell tests
topics.search: loophole-free Bell test 2022 Nobel prize Aspect Clauser Zeilinger
topics.goal: How Bell's theorem was tested experimentally.
checks: I can name the loopholes and how they were closed.

ex.q: Name three loopholes.
Which year saw the first experiments closing the main loopholes together?

topics.title: The CHSH inequality
topics.goal: The quantum limit 2√2 vs classical 2.
checks: I can compute the quantum CHSH value.

ex.q: With correlation E = −cos(θₐ − θ_b), use angles a = 0°, a′ = 90°, b = 45°, b′ = 135°. Compute S = E(a, b) − E(a, b′) + E(a′, b) + E(a′, b′).
Compare with the classical limit 2.

topics.title: Entanglement swapping
topics.goal: Entangle particles that never met.
checks: I can explain how particles that never met become entangled.

ex.q: Describe the setup with two Bell pairs.
Why is this the key to quantum repeaters?
ex.a: It extends entanglement over long distances.

topics.title: The quantum internet
topics.goal: Networks of entanglement.
checks: I can explain why quantum signals can't simply be amplified.

ex.q: Why can't you boost a qubit signal like an internet signal?
What did the Micius satellite demonstrate?

topics.title: Quantum random numbers
topics.goal: True randomness from quantum measurement.
checks: I can explain true randomness from measurement.

ex.q: How can a beam splitter generate random bits?
ex.a: Each photon goes randomly one of two ways

ex.q: How does this differ from a computer's random function?
ex.a: Pseudo-random numbers come from a formula.

topics.title: Quantum complexity
topics.goal: What quantum computers can and cannot do.
checks: I can place BQP among complexity classes.

ex.q: Is factoring in BQP? Is it believed to be in P?
ex.a: Yes; it is not known to be in P and believed not to be

ex.q: Are quantum computers expected to solve NP-complete problems quickly?

topics.title: The ZX-calculus
topics.goal: A diagram language for quantum circuits.
checks: I can read simple ZX diagrams.

ex.q: What are spiders?
ex.a: Nodes representing Z- or X-type maps

ex.q: Show two Hadamards in a row simplify to a plain wire.

topics.title: Your first real circuit
topics.goal: Run a real circuit yourself.
checks: I can build and run a circuit in code.

ex.q: Build the Bell circuit in Qiskit and simulate 1000 shots. What counts do you see?
Run it on real hardware. Why do some 01 and 10 results appear?

parts.name: Interpretations
parts.title: Foundations and interpretations
parts.intro: Interpretations are argued about, not memorized. For each one, be able to say what is real, whether collapse happens, and where it pays a price. Several of these exercises have real numbers in them, because many paradoxes are calculations.

topics.title: The measurement problem
topics.goal: Why "collapse" is the unsolved heart of quantum theory.
checks: I can explain why linear evolution clashes with single outcomes.

ex.q: A detector ends up reading "up" for ∣↑⟩ and "down" for ∣↓⟩. Use linearity to find what happens to (∣↑⟩ + ∣↓⟩)/√2.
Why does that result conflict with what we see?
List the three ways out: add collapse, add hidden variables, or accept all outcomes. Name one interpretation for each.

topics.title: Deriving a Bell inequality
topics.search: Bell inequality derivation step by step
topics.goal: Derive a Bell inequality yourself from local hidden variables.
checks: I can derive the CHSH bound from local hidden variables.

ex.q: Give each of A, A′, B and B′ a preset value of ±1. Show that AB − AB′ + A′B + A′B′ = A(B − B′) + A′(B + B′).
Explain why one of the two brackets is always 0 and the other ±2.
ex.a: B and B′ are each ±1, so they are equal or opposite

ex.q: Conclude that the average is at most 2. Compare this with 2√2 from 18.29.
Which assumption fails if nature breaks the bound?

topics.title: Many worlds
topics.goal: Every outcome happens in a branching wavefunction.
checks: I can explain branching and the Born-rule problem.

ex.q: You measure ten 50/50 qubits in a row. How many branches are there?
How many branches contain exactly five 0s? What fraction of all branches is that?
For √0.9∣0⟩ + √0.1∣1⟩ there are two branches, but the odds are 90/10. Why does this make counting branches fail?
ex.a: Branches would need weights by amplitude squared.

topics.title: Pilot waves
topics.search: pilot wave theory walking droplets Veritasium
topics.goal: Particles guided by a real wave (de Broglie-Bohm).
checks: I can use the guidance equation in simple cases.

ex.q: The guidance equation is v = (ħ/m) Im(ψ′/ψ). Find v for ψ = e^(ikx).
Find v for any real ψ, such as the particle-in-a-box ground state. What is surprising?
How do walking droplets resemble pilot waves, and where does the analogy break?
ex.a: Droplets show orbits and tunnelling-like behavior but lack entanglement and live in 2D.

topics.title: Nonlocality in Bohmian mechanics
topics.goal: Why pilot waves must be nonlocal.
checks: I can explain why pilot waves must be nonlocal.

ex.q: For two entangled particles, what does particle 1's velocity depend on?
Why does this nonlocality still not allow signaling?
ex.a: Initial positions are unknowable and distributed by the Born rule.

topics.title: Objective collapse
topics.search: objective collapse GRW Penrose gravity collapse
topics.goal: Collapse as a real physical process.
checks: I can estimate GRW collapse times.

ex.q: GRW sets a collapse rate of about 10⁻¹⁶ per second per particle. How long does one electron wait on average, in years?
How long does an object of 10²³ particles stay in superposition?
Why does this rescue the cat but leave atoms quantum?
ex.a: Collapse rates grow with particle number

ex.q: Penrose's collapse time is τ ≈ ħ/E_G. What is E_G?
ex.a: The gravitational self-energy of the difference between the mass distributions.

topics.title: QBism
topics.goal: The wavefunction as an agent's beliefs.
checks: I can explain the wavefunction as personal belief.

ex.q: In QBism, what does "collapse" mean?
Give one strength of this view and one criticism.
ex.a: Removes nonlocality worries; criticized as making physics about observers.

topics.title: The ensemble interpretation
topics.goal: ψ as a description of many identically prepared systems, not one.
checks: I can say what ψ describes in this view.

ex.q: What does ψ describe according to the ensemble interpretation?
ex.a: Statistics of many identically prepared systems

ex.q: One photon at a time still builds a two-slit pattern. What does the ensemble view say about each single photon?
Name an experiment on a single system that strains this view.
ex.a: Quantum jumps in one trapped ion.

topics.title: Relational quantum mechanics
topics.goal: Properties exist only relative to other systems.
checks: I can explain properties as relations between systems.

ex.q: How does relational quantum mechanics resolve Wigner's friend (19.12)?
ex.a: Both descriptions are correct, relative to different systems

ex.q: What is the main objection to it?
ex.a: Critics say it gives up shared objective facts.

topics.title: Consistent histories
topics.goal: Assign probabilities to whole histories.
checks: I can explain what makes a set of histories consistent.

ex.q: Why can't you assign probabilities to "went through slit 1" when the interference pattern is visible?
ex.a: The paths interfere, so the probabilities don't add

ex.q: What changes when a which-path detector is added?

topics.title: The transactional interpretation
topics.goal: Waves going forward and backward in time.
checks: I can describe offer and confirmation waves.

ex.q: An offer wave ψ travels forward in time and a confirmation wave ψ* travels back. What does their product give?
Why is this interpretation called time-symmetric?
ex.a: It uses waves running both ways in time.

topics.title: Superdeterminism
topics.goal: Bell's loophole: measurement settings are not free.
checks: I can explain the free-choice loophole.

ex.q: Which Bell-test assumption does superdeterminism deny?
Cosmic Bell tests choose settings using light from distant quasars. How far back in time does that push any shared cause?
Why do many scientists consider this loophole unscientific, and how does Hossenfelder reply?
ex.a: Critics say it could explain any result; she says it's a testable theory of correlations.

topics.title: Quantum Darwinism
topics.goal: How objective classical facts emerge.
checks: I can explain how objective facts emerge.

ex.q: Why can many observers agree on where a chair is without disturbing it?
ex.a: Records copy into many environmental fragments

ex.q: How does this build on decoherence (16.29)?
ex.a: Decoherence selects the stable states that get copied.

topics.title: Wigner's friend
topics.goal: Two observers, two descriptions.
checks: I can describe the two conflicting descriptions.

ex.q: The friend measures a qubit inside a sealed lab. Write the state Wigner assigns to the lab.
What would Wigner need to measure to prove the lab is in superposition?
ex.a: An interference measurement on the whole lab.

topics.title: Frauchiger-Renner
topics.goal: Extended Wigner's friend: quantum theory can't consistently describe its own users.
checks: I can state what the paradox proves.

ex.q: Name the three assumptions that cannot all hold.
ex.a: Universal quantum theory; one outcome per measurement; consistent reasoning between agents

ex.q: Which assumption does many-worlds drop? Which does QBism drop?
ex.a: One outcome (many worlds); universal objective use (QBism).

topics.title: Kochen-Specker contextuality
topics.goal: Outcomes can't be pre-assigned independent of context.
checks: I can prove contextuality with the Peres-Mermin square.

ex.q: Fill a 3×3 grid with ±1 so every row multiplies to +1, the first two columns to +1, and the third column to −1. Try it.
Prove it can't be done: multiply all nine numbers by rows, then by columns.
ex.a: By rows the product is +1, by columns −1

ex.q: Quantum two-qubit observables satisfy these rules. What does that mean for preset values?
ex.a: Values can't be preset independent of context.

topics.title: The GHZ paradox
topics.goal: Bell's theorem without inequalities.
checks: I can show Bell's theorem without inequalities.

ex.q: XXX gives +1 on this state. Preset values xᵢ, yᵢ = ±1 must give x₁y₂y₃ = y₁x₂y₃ = y₁y₂x₃ = −1. Multiply the three and find a contradiction.
ex.a: The y's square to 1, leaving x₁x₂x₃ = −1, but QM says +1

ex.q: Why does a single run settle this, with no statistics?
ex.a: Hidden variables predict −1 with certainty, QM predicts +1 with certainty.

topics.title: Hardy's paradox
topics.goal: Nonlocality from a single impossible event.
checks: I can explain nonlocality from one event.

ex.q: The best Hardy probability is (5√5 − 11)/2. Compute it.
Why does even one occurrence rule out local hidden variables?
ex.a: Local models assign it probability zero.

topics.title: The PBR theorem
topics.search: PBR theorem reality of the wavefunction
topics.goal: The wavefunction is likely a real thing, not just knowledge.
checks: I can state what PBR rules out.

ex.q: What does "ψ-epistemic" mean?
ex.a: ψ represents only knowledge of an underlying state

ex.q: What extra assumption does PBR need?

topics.title: Leggett-Garg inequalities
topics.goal: Testing quantumness in time instead of space.
checks: I can compute a Leggett-Garg violation.

ex.q: With K = C₁₂ + C₂₃ − C₁₃ ≤ 1 and C = cos(ωτ) for equally spaced times, find K at ωτ = π/3.
What is "macrorealism"?
ex.a: Definite values that can be measured without disturbance.

topics.title: The quantum Zeno effect
topics.goal: Watching a system often enough freezes it.
checks: I can compute Zeno survival with polarizers.

ex.q: To rotate polarization by 90° in N equal steps through polarizers, the transmission is cos^(2N)(90°/N). Compute it for N = 1, 2, 10 and 100.
What happens as N → ∞? Link this to Malus's law.
Why do frequent measurements freeze decay?

topics.title: The bomb tester
topics.goal: Detect a bomb without touching it.
checks: I can compute interaction-free measurement odds.

ex.q: A live bomb blocks one arm of a balanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Find the probabilities of explosion, a dark-port click and a bright-port click.
You retry after every inconclusive result. What fraction of live bombs do you find safely?
How does the quantum Zeno effect push this toward 100%?
ex.a: Many weak steps make the bomb almost never absorb.

topics.title: Weak values
topics.goal: Gentle measurements and their odd averages.
checks: I can compute a weak value.

ex.q: The weak value is A_w = ⟨φ∣A∣ψ⟩/⟨φ∣ψ⟩. For ψ = ∣+⟩ and φ = cosθ∣0⟩ + sinθ∣1⟩, show the weak value of σ_z is (cosθ − sinθ)/(cosθ + sinθ).
Evaluate it at θ = 0 and at θ = −40°.
Is a value far outside the range ±1 a contradiction? Explain.
ex.a: No; it is a conditional average, not an eigenvalue.

topics.title: The quantum Cheshire cat
topics.goal: A particle separated from its property.
checks: I can describe the claim and its controversy.

ex.q: In the neutron experiment, where was the neutron and where was its spin?
ex.a: Weak values put the neutron in one arm and the spin in the other

ex.q: Why do critics say this is only a way of talking about weak values?
ex.a: They are averages with no individual-particle meaning.

topics.title: The quantum pigeonhole paradox
topics.goal: Three particles, two boxes, no two share a box.
checks: I can describe the setup.

ex.q: How many pairs can three particles form? What does classical pigeonhole logic say about them?
ex.a: Three pairs; at least one pair must share a box

ex.q: Which choice of pre- and post-selection produces the paradox?
ex.a: Pre-select each particle in ∣+⟩ and post-select each in ∣+i⟩.

topics.title: The Hong-Ou-Mandel effect
topics.goal: Two identical photons always leave together.
checks: I can show two identical photons always leave a beam splitter together.

ex.q: A 50/50 beam splitter has t = 1/√2 and r = i/√2. Add the amplitudes for both photons transmitted and both reflected.
What is the coincidence rate for distinguishable photons?
Why is the HOM dip used to test whether photons are identical?
ex.a: The dip vanishes for distinguishable photons.

topics.title: The Aharonov-Bohm effect
topics.goal: Potentials affect particles where fields are zero.
checks: I can compute the phase from enclosed flux.

ex.q: The phase is eΦ/ħ. What flux shifts an electron's phase by 2π?
What flux shifts it by π? Give a number in webers.
Why does this suggest potentials are more basic than fields?
ex.a: The electrons only pass through regions where the field is zero.

topics.title: Quantum suicide
topics.search: quantum suicide and immortality thought experiment
topics.goal: A many-worlds thought experiment and its flaws.
checks: I can analyze the thought experiment critically.

ex.q: A 50/50 quantum trigger fires 20 times. What is the chance of surviving in an ordinary single world?
What would the experimenter conclude under many worlds?
Give two reasons the argument doesn't prove immortality.
ex.a: Most branches have grieving friends; death is rarely all-or-nothing.

topics.title: The free will theorem
topics.goal: If we have free will, so do particles.
checks: I can state the theorem.

ex.q: Name the three axioms.
What does "free" mean in the theorem?

topics.title: The Tsirelson bound and PR boxes
topics.goal: Why nature allows exactly this much nonlocality.
checks: I can compare classical, quantum and PR-box correlations.

ex.q: A PR box gives outputs with a ⊕ b = x · y. Show it reaches CHSH = 4.
ex.a: Each term contributes ±1 in the right direction

ex.q: Show Bob's output alone is random, so the box can't signal.
ex.a: Both outputs are 50/50 for every input

ex.q: Put 2, 2√2 and 4 in order. Why is it a puzzle that nature stops at 2√2?

topics.title: Reconstructing quantum theory
topics.goal: Deriving quantum theory from simple principles.
checks: I can name the axiom that separates quantum from classical.

ex.q: Can you move continuously and reversibly from bit 0 to bit 1 in classical probability theory? Can you for a qubit?
Which of Hardy's axioms captures this?

topics.title: Orch OR
topics.search: Penrose Hameroff Orch OR consciousness criticism
topics.goal: The quantum mind proposal and the case against it.
checks: I can weigh the proposal against the evidence.

ex.q: Tegmark estimated decoherence in microtubules at 10⁻¹³ s or less. Neurons fire on timescales of about 10⁻³ s. Find the ratio.
What would supporters have to show?
ex.a: Coherence that survives on neural timescales.

topics.title: Putting interpretations side by side
topics.search: Sean Carroll Biggest Ideas in the Universe quantum
topics.goal: A lecture series on foundations.
checks: I can compare interpretations on the same criteria.

ex.q: For Copenhagen, many worlds, Bohm and GRW, say: deterministic? Real collapse? One world? Local?
ex.a: Copenhagen: no, yes, yes, unclear. Many worlds: yes, no, no, local. Bohm: yes, no, yes, nonlocal. GRW: no, yes, yes, nonlocal.

ex.q: Pick the one you find most convincing and write its weakest point.

parts.name: Quantum Field Theory
parts.title: Relativistic QM and quantum field theory
parts.intro: You'll need these constants: ħc ≈ 197.3 MeV·fm, m_e c² = 0.511 MeV, α ≈ 1/137 and μ_B ≈ 9.27 × 10⁻²⁴ J/T. Many of the exercises are estimates that come out to real, measured numbers: the range of the nuclear force, the Casimir pressure, the critical field for tearing pairs out of the vacuum.

topics.title: Why QM and relativity clash
topics.search: why quantum mechanics and special relativity clash
topics.goal: Particle number can't stay fixed at high energies.
checks: I can explain why particle number can't stay fixed.

ex.q: Compute the electron's Compton wavelength h/(mc).
Squeeze an electron into a region smaller than its reduced Compton wavelength ħ/(mc). Use the uncertainty principle to estimate its energy spread. What becomes possible?
ex.a: About mc², enough to create pairs

ex.q: What is the minimum photon energy that can create an electron-positron pair?

topics.title: The Klein-Gordon equation
topics.goal: The first relativistic wave equation and its problems.
checks: I can derive it and state its problems.

ex.q: Substitute E → iħ∂ₜ and p → −iħ∇ into E² = p²c² + m²c⁴. Write the equation you get.
Insert e^(i(kx − ωt)) and find the dispersion relation.
Name the two problems that made physicists abandon it as a single-particle equation.
ex.a: Negative energies and a density that can go negative.

topics.title: The Dirac equation
topics.goal: The relativistic equation for the electron.
checks: I can explain why Dirac needed matrices.

ex.q: Dirac wanted E = cα·p + βmc² to square to E² = p²c² + m²c⁴. Which conditions must αᵢ and β satisfy?
ex.a: αᵢ² = β² = 1, and all pairs anticommute

ex.q: Why can't they be ordinary numbers?
What is the smallest matrix size that works?

topics.title: Spinors and gamma matrices
topics.goal: The 4-component objects of the Dirac equation.
checks: I can work with anticommuting matrices.

ex.q: Compute σₓσ_y and σ_yσₓ for the Pauli matrices. Show they anticommute.
State the rule {γ^μ, γ^ν} = 2η^μν in words.
ex.a: The gammas square to the metric and anticommute

ex.q: What do the four components of a Dirac spinor represent?
ex.a: Spin up and down, for particle and antiparticle.

topics.title: The Dirac sea and antimatter
topics.goal: How negative energies led to positrons.
checks: I can tell the story of the positron's prediction.

ex.q: How does a "hole" in a filled sea of negative-energy states behave?
ex.a: As a positive particle with positive energy

ex.q: Who found the positron, in what year, and how?
Why is the sea picture abandoned in modern QFT?
ex.a: It fails for bosons; fields replace it.

topics.title: g = 2 from the Dirac equation
topics.goal: Spin's magnetic strength predicted, not assumed.
checks: I can use g to compute spin-flip energies.

ex.q: With g = 2, what is the electron's spin magnetic moment in units of μ_B?
The spin-flip energy is gμ_B B. Compute it for B = 1 T, then convert it to a photon frequency.
Which technique in Part 23 uses this frequency?

topics.title: The Klein paradox
topics.goal: Barriers that become transparent at high voltage.
checks: I can explain transparent barriers.

ex.q: About how high must a potential step be before the paradox appears?
How does pair creation resolve it?
Which material shows an analogous effect? (See 17.29.)

topics.title: Zitterbewegung
topics.goal: The electron's predicted "trembling motion".
checks: I can estimate the trembling motion.

ex.q: The angular frequency is 2mc²/ħ. Compute it for an electron.
The amplitude is about ħ/(2mc). Compute it.
How was zitterbewegung simulated in 2010?

topics.title: Visualizing quantum fields
topics.goal: Fields filling space; particles as their excitations.
checks: I can describe particles as ripples in fields.

ex.q: Why are all electrons in the universe exactly identical?
ex.a: They are excitations of one field

ex.q: What is a photon in the field picture?
ex.a: A quantum of the electromagnetic field.

topics.title: Why fields come first
topics.search: what is a quantum field PBS Space Time
topics.goal: Why fields come first and particles second.
checks: I can say why physics needs fields rather than particles.

ex.q: Give two phenomena a fixed-particle theory can't describe.
Where does the Pauli principle (15.x) come from in a field theory?

topics.title: Expert talk: the field picture
topics.search: Quantum Fields The Real Building Blocks of the Universe David Tong Royal Institution
topics.goal: An expert talk on the field picture.
checks: I can summarize the talk in three sentences.

ex.q: Which fields of the Standard Model can you name?
ex.a: Quarks, leptons, gluons, W, Z, photon, Higgs

ex.q: What is the biggest open problem the talk mentions?
ex.a: For example, quantum gravity or dark matter.

topics.title: Classical field theory
topics.goal: Fields obeying least action.
checks: I can derive field equations from a Lagrangian density.

ex.q: A string has ℒ = ½μ(∂ₜφ)² − ½T(∂ₓφ)². Derive the wave equation and the wave speed.
Do the same for ℒ = ½(∂φ)² − ½m²φ² in natural units. Which equation do you get?

topics.title: Creation and annihilation operators
topics.goal: Count particles with operators.
checks: I can use a and a† on number states.

ex.q: Compute a†a†∣0⟩.
Verify [a, a†] = 1 by acting on ∣n⟩.
Fermion operators satisfy (b†)² = 0. What law of nature is that?

topics.title: Quantizing a free field
topics.goal: Each mode of a field is a harmonic oscillator.
checks: I can see a field as many oscillators.

ex.q: What is the frequency of the mode with wavenumber k for a field of mass m?
Each mode carries zero-point energy ½ħω. Why does that make the vacuum energy infinite?
How does normal ordering deal with this, and why does gravity make the problem real?
ex.a: It drops the constant; gravity feels it, which is the cosmological constant problem.

topics.title: Virtual particles
topics.goal: What virtual particles do and do not mean.
checks: I can estimate a force's range from its carrier's mass.

ex.q: A force carried by a particle of mass m has range R ≈ ħ/(mc) = ħc/(mc²). Compute it for the pion (140 MeV).
Compute it for the W boson (80.4 GeV).
Why is the electromagnetic force long-range?
In what sense are virtual particles not real particles?
ex.a: They are terms in a calculation and can't be detected.

topics.title: The quantum vacuum
topics.goal: Empty space is not empty.
checks: I can compute the Casimir pressure.

ex.q: The Casimir pressure is π²ħc/(240d⁴). Compute it for plates 1 μm apart.
Compute it at 10 nm and compare with atmospheric pressure.
Name another measurable effect of vacuum fluctuations.

topics.title: Feynman diagrams
topics.goal: Read diagrams as terms in a calculation.
checks: I can draw diagrams and count powers of α.

ex.q: Draw the lowest-order diagrams for e⁻e⁻ → e⁻e⁻. Why are there two?
ex.a: The two electrons are identical, so swapped outgoing particles count separately

ex.q: Each vertex brings a factor e ∝ √α. How does the amplitude scale for a two-vertex diagram? How does the probability scale?
Adding a loop adds two vertices. By what factor does that suppress the amplitude?

topics.title: The S-matrix and Feynman rules
topics.goal: Turn a Feynman diagram into a number you can compare with experiment.
checks: I can turn a cross-section into an event count.

ex.q: Event rate = luminosity × cross-section. With 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ and 50 pb (1 pb = 10⁻³⁶ cm²), find the rate per second and per day.
Which formula from Part 16 is the S-matrix's simplest relative?
In a Feynman rule, what does an internal line contribute?

topics.title: Quantum electrodynamics
topics.goal: Light and electrons; the most precise theory known.
checks: I can compute the fine-structure constant.

ex.q: Compute α = e²/(4πε₀ħc) from the constants.
Why does a small α make QED calculations work so well?
ex.a: Each extra order is about 100 times smaller.

topics.title: Annihilation and Compton scattering
topics.search: electron positron annihilation and Compton scattering in QED
topics.goal: Two classic QED processes worked through.
checks: I can apply conservation laws to QED processes.
