ex.q: An electron and a positron annihilate at rest. Why two photons, not one? What energy and direction does each have?
ex.a: Momentum must stay zero; 511 keV each, back to back

ex.q: Compute the Compton shift for a photon scattered straight back.
What is the minimum collision energy for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻? (The muon is 105.7 MeV.)

topics.title: The electron's g − 2
topics.search: electron anomalous magnetic moment g-2 prediction
topics.goal: Theory and experiment agree to about 1 part in 10¹².
checks: I can compute Schwinger's first correction.

ex.q: The first correction is a = α/(2π). Compute it.
The measured value is a ≈ 0.00115965. How close is the first term?
What is the status of the muon g − 2 comparison?
ex.a: The 2025 lattice-based theory agrees with Fermilab's final measurement.

topics.title: Gauge theory
topics.goal: Local symmetry demands force fields.
checks: I can explain why local symmetry needs a field.

ex.q: Under ψ → e^(iθ(x))ψ, what extra term does ∂ψ pick up?
How does adding a field A cancel it?
ex.a: The field shifts to absorb the extra term.

topics.title: U(1) gives electromagnetism
topics.goal: Electromagnetism from a phase symmetry.
checks: I can derive the photon's properties from symmetry.

ex.q: How must A transform to restore the symmetry?
Show that the field strength F is unchanged.
Why does gauge symmetry force the photon to be massless?
ex.a: A mass term in A² isn't invariant.

topics.title: Yang-Mills theory
topics.goal: The template for the strong and weak forces.
checks: I can count gauge bosons.

ex.q: SU(N) has N² − 1 generators. How many gauge bosons does SU(2) give? SU(3)?
Why do gluons interact with each other while photons don't?
What is the Millennium Prize problem about Yang-Mills?

topics.title: Renormalization
topics.goal: Taming infinities, and what they tell us.
checks: I can explain bare and measured charges.

ex.q: How do virtual pairs screen an electron's charge?
ex.a: Pairs align and shield the charge

ex.q: How does this relate to 1 + 2 + 3 + … = −1/12 (5.31)?
Why did Dirac and Feynman both feel uneasy about renormalization, and how did Wilson change the view?
ex.a: Wilson treated it as physics changing with scale.

topics.title: Running couplings
topics.goal: Force strengths change with energy.
checks: I can run the strong coupling with energy.

ex.q: At one loop, α_s(Q) = α_s(μ)/(1 + bα_s(μ)ln(Q²/μ²)), with b = (33 − 2n_f)/(12π). Start from α_s = 0.118 at 91.2 GeV with n_f = 5 and find α_s at 1 TeV.
How many quark flavours would it take to destroy asymptotic freedom?
α is about 1/137 at low energy. About what is it at 91 GeV?

topics.title: Effective field theory
topics.goal: Physics at one scale ignores details of smaller ones.
checks: I can read a new energy scale from a coupling.

ex.q: Fermi's constant is G_F ≈ 1.166 × 10⁻⁵ GeV⁻². Compute (√2G_F)^(−½). Which scale is that?
ex.a: About 246 GeV, the Higgs vacuum value

ex.q: Why did Fermi's theory work at low energy but fail at high energy?
Give a non-particle example of effective theory.

topics.title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
topics.goal: Symmetric laws, asymmetric ground states.
checks: I can find the vacuum of a Mexican-hat potential.

ex.q: For V = −μ²φ² + λφ⁴, find where V is lowest.
Give two everyday examples of symmetric laws with an asymmetric state.
ex.a: A magnet, or a pencil falling from its tip.

topics.title: Goldstone bosons
topics.goal: Massless modes from broken symmetry.
checks: I can count Goldstone modes.

ex.q: A complex field breaks U(1). How many Goldstone bosons appear?
Why are pions so much lighter than protons?
Name a Goldstone mode in a solid or magnet.

topics.title: The Higgs mechanism
topics.goal: How the W and Z get mass.
checks: I can count degrees of freedom in the Higgs mechanism.

ex.q: A massless vector boson has 2 polarizations; a massive one has 3. Where does the extra one come from?
The Higgs doublet has 4 real fields. How many are eaten, and how many become the Higgs boson?
Is most of your mass from the Higgs? Explain.
ex.a: No, only about 1%; most mass comes from QCD energy.

topics.title: Quantum chromodynamics
topics.goal: The theory of quarks and gluons.
checks: I can use colour counting.

ex.q: The Δ⁺⁺ is uuu with all spins aligned. Why did it demand a new quantum number?
ex.a: The quarks would otherwise be identical fermions

ex.q: The R ratio is R = N_c × the sum of Q² over reachable quarks. Compute R with u, d, s, then with c, then with b, using N_c = 3.
How did measuring R confirm three colours?
ex.a: R matched experiment only with 3 colours.

topics.title: Asymptotic freedom and confinement
topics.goal: Quarks are free up close and trapped far apart.
checks: I can estimate the force between quarks.

ex.q: The QCD string tension is about 1 GeV/fm. Convert it to newtons. What mass would weigh that much on Earth?
ex.a: About 1.6 × 10⁵ N, the weight of about 16 tonnes

ex.q: What happens when you pull a quark 2 fm away?
ex.a: The string breaks into new hadrons

ex.q: What are jets?
ex.a: Sprays of hadrons from quarks or gluons.

topics.title: The CPT theorem
topics.goal: Every QFT is symmetric under combined C, P and T.
checks: I can apply C, P and T to particles.

ex.q: Apply P, C and CP to a left-handed neutrino. Which results exist in nature?
ex.a: Right-handed ν (no), left-handed anti-ν (no), right-handed anti-ν (yes)

ex.q: Which property must particles and antiparticles share by CPT?
How is antihydrogen used to test CPT?
ex.a: Comparing its spectral lines with hydrogen's.

topics.title: The path integral in QFT
topics.search: path integral in quantum field theory
topics.goal: Sum over all field configurations.
checks: I can link the path integral to statistical mechanics.

ex.q: Write Z with e^(iS/ħ). What does the Wick rotation t → −iτ turn it into?
ex.a: Statistical mechanics in one more dimension

ex.q: Why does that help lattice QCD?
ex.a: It makes the weights real and positive.

topics.title: Anomalies
topics.goal: Classical symmetries broken by quantization.
checks: I can do an anomaly-cancellation check.

ex.q: Add the electric charges of one generation: e, ν, and three colours each of u and d.
Which decay does the chiral anomaly explain?
Why must gauge anomalies cancel?

topics.title: Instantons
topics.goal: Tunneling in field theory.
checks: I can estimate a tunneling suppression in field theory.

ex.q: Weak-force instantons are suppressed by e^(−4π/α_w). With α_w ≈ 1/30, write this as a power of 10.
What does this mean for proton decay through this route?
How does this connect with WKB tunneling (16.x)?
ex.a: Both are tunneling through a barrier.

topics.title: Conformal field theory
topics.goal: Scale-invariant theories.
checks: I can describe scale invariance.

ex.q: A correlation falls as 1/r^(2Δ). By what factor does it change when every distance is doubled?
Where do CFTs appear in the real world?

topics.title: Lattice QCD
topics.goal: Solving QCD on supercomputers.
checks: I can estimate the size of a lattice simulation.

ex.q: A lattice with spacing 0.1 fm spans 4 fm in all four directions. How many sites does it have?
Each site has 4 links, and each link holds an SU(3) matrix with 8 real parameters. How many numbers is that?
Which famous mass has lattice QCD computed?

topics.title: The Schwinger effect
topics.search: Schwinger effect pair production from vacuum
topics.goal: Strong fields rip particles out of empty space.
checks: I can compute the critical field.

ex.q: Compute E_c = m²c³/(eħ).
Show it is the field that does work mc² across the reduced Compton wavelength.
Why has the effect not been observed directly?

topics.title: The Unruh effect
topics.goal: Accelerating observers see a warm vacuum.
checks: I can compute Unruh temperatures.

ex.q: T = ħa/(2πck_B). Compute T for a = 9.8 m/s².
Which acceleration gives 1 K?
How does this relate to Hawking radiation (22.x)?
ex.a: They are linked by the equivalence principle.

topics.title: Graduate QFT lectures
topics.search: Sidney Coleman quantum field theory lectures Harvard
topics.goal: Classic graduate lectures.
checks: I can follow a graduate-level derivation.

ex.q: After the first lectures, write in your own words why QFT is the only way to combine QM and relativity with locality.

topics.title: A gentler lecture series
topics.search: Leonard Susskind Theoretical Minimum special relativity and classical field theory
topics.goal: A gentler lecture series for the same ground.
checks: I can write a Lorentz-invariant action.

ex.q: Why must the action be a Lorentz scalar?
ex.a: So all observers agree on the laws

ex.q: Which combination of ∂_tφ and ∇φ is Lorentz invariant?

parts.name: Particles and Nuclei
parts.title: Particle and nuclear physics
parts.intro: Constants you'll need: 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c², m_p = 938.3 MeV, m_n = 939.6 MeV, ħc = 197.3 MeV·fm, and B[T] = p[GeV]/(0.2998 × r[m]). These exercises use real experiments: you'll count the Sun's neutrinos passing through your thumb, steer LHC protons, and work out how a single cosmic ray compares with a thrown baseball.

topics.title: The Standard Model
topics.search: Standard Model of particle physics explained
topics.goal: The 17 particles and their roles.
checks: I can draw the 17 particles from memory.

ex.q: Count the quarks, leptons, gauge bosons and the Higgs. Do they add up to 17?
Compute the charges of uud and udd. Which particles are these?
Which particles feel the strong force?

topics.title: Three generations
topics.goal: Matter particles and their families.
checks: I can name the generations and compare their masses.

ex.q: Compute the muon-to-electron mass ratio (105.7 MeV and 0.511 MeV).
A cosmic-ray muon lives 2.2 μs at rest and travels with γ = 20. How far does it go on average? (See 12.x.)
Why is all ordinary matter made of the first generation?

topics.title: The four forces
topics.goal: Gravity, electromagnetism, strong, weak.
checks: I can compare force strengths.

ex.q: Compute the ratio of electric to gravitational force between two protons. Does it depend on distance?
If gravity is so weak, why does it rule planets and galaxies?
Rank the four forces by range.
ex.a: Gravity and EM infinite; strong and weak short.

topics.title: Force carriers
topics.search: force carrier bosons photon gluon W Z
topics.goal: Which boson carries which force.
checks: I can match each force to its carriers.

ex.q: Which carriers have electric charge? Which carry colour?
The W is 80.4 GeV and the Z is 91.2 GeV. Use 20.15 to explain why the weak force is short-range.
ex.a: Heavy carriers mean a short range

ex.q: Why isn't the graviton in the Standard Model?

topics.title: Hadrons
topics.goal: Particles made of quarks.
checks: I can find hadron charges from quark content.

ex.q: Find the charges of π⁺ (u anti-d), K⁻ (s anti-u), Λ (uds), Ω⁻ (sss) and Σ⁺ (uus).
Can a meson have charge +2? Can a baryon?
Why are no free quarks seen? (See 20.30.)

topics.title: The eightfold way
topics.goal: How symmetry predicted quarks.
checks: I can predict a mass from a symmetry pattern.

ex.q: The decuplet masses are Δ at 1232 MeV, Σ* at 1385 MeV and Ξ* at 1533 MeV. Find the spacing and predict the Ω⁻ mass.
The measured Ω⁻ mass is 1672 MeV. How close was the prediction?
Why is each step heavier?
ex.a: Each step swaps in a heavier s quark.

topics.title: Where the proton's mass comes from
topics.search: where does the proton's mass come from
topics.goal: About 99% comes from QCD energy, not the Higgs.
checks: I can show the Higgs gives the proton only about 1% of its mass.

ex.q: Take u ≈ 2.2 MeV and d ≈ 4.7 MeV. What fraction of the proton's 938 MeV do its quark masses supply?
Where does the rest come from?
Link this to E = mc² (12.x).

topics.title: The strong force
topics.goal: The strongest force and its range.
checks: I can explain colour neutrality.

ex.q: Why must a baryon contain one red, one green and one blue quark?
How many gluon types are there? (See 20.22.)
How does the residual strong force between nucleons resemble the van der Waals force (13.x)?
ex.a: Both are leftover forces between neutral objects.

topics.title: Yukawa and pions
topics.goal: How nucleons bind.
checks: I can predict a particle's mass from a force's range.

ex.q: The nuclear force reaches about 1.4 fm. Predict the carrier's mass as Yukawa did.
The Yukawa potential falls as e^(−r/R)/r. By what extra factor is it weaker than a Coulomb-like 1/r force at r = 3R?
What was first mistaken for Yukawa's particle?

topics.title: Isospin
topics.goal: Protons and neutrons as two states of one particle.
checks: I can combine isospins as I combined spins.

ex.q: Compute m_n − m_p. Why is isospin only an approximate symmetry?
ex.a: About 1.29 MeV; EM and the quark masses break it

ex.q: Combine two nucleons, each with I = ½. Which total isospins appear, and with which charge states?
The deuteron has I = 0. Why is there no bound diproton or dineutron?
ex.a: The I = 1 state is too weakly bound

ex.q: What is the pion triplet's isospin?

topics.title: Binding energy
topics.goal: Why fusion and fission both release energy.
checks: I can compute mass defects.

ex.q: Atomic masses: ¹H = 1.007825 u, n = 1.008665 u, ⁴He = 4.002602 u. Find helium-4's binding energy and its binding energy per nucleon.
ex.a: About 28.3 MeV; about 7.07 MeV per nucleon

ex.q: Why does iron-56 sit at the top of the curve?
ex.a: It has the highest binding per nucleon

ex.q: Each U-235 fission releases about 200 MeV. How much energy does 1 kg release, in joules and in kilotons of TNT (1 kt = 4.184 × 10¹² J)?

topics.title: Beta decay
topics.goal: How a neutron turns into a proton.
checks: I can write beta decay at the quark level.

ex.q: Write the neutron's decay. Compute its Q value.
Draw it as d → u + W⁻, then W⁻ → ?
Why did the continuous electron spectrum lead Pauli to the neutrino?

topics.title: Conservation laws in reactions
topics.search: conservation laws particle reactions lepton number baryon number
topics.goal: Decide whether a reaction is allowed by checking what must be conserved.
checks: I can judge whether a reaction can happen.

ex.q: Decide allowed or forbidden, and name the rule: a) p → e⁺ + π⁰; b) n → p + e⁻ + ν_e; c) π⁺ → μ⁺ + ν_μ; d) μ⁻ → e⁻ + γ; e) γ → e⁺ + e⁻ in empty space.
ex.a: a) forbidden, baryon number; b) forbidden, lepton number; c) allowed; d) forbidden, lepton flavour; e) forbidden, energy and momentum

ex.q: A proton beam hits a fixed proton target to make p + p → p + p + π⁰ (m_π = 135 MeV). Use the invariant mass (12.x) to find the minimum beam kinetic energy.

topics.title: Neutrinos
topics.goal: Ghostly particles that barely interact.
checks: I can estimate the solar neutrino flux.

ex.q: The Sun emits 3.83 × 10²⁶ W. Each fusion chain releases 26.7 MeV and 2 neutrinos. How many neutrinos does the Sun make per second?
Find the flux at Earth (1 AU = 1.496 × 10¹¹ m) per cm² per second.
Why don't you feel them?

topics.title: Neutrino oscillations
topics.goal: Neutrinos change flavor, so they have mass.
checks: I can use the oscillation formula.

ex.q: The oscillation probability is sin²(2θ) sin²(1.27Δm²L/E), with Δm² in eV², L in km and E in GeV. For Δm² = 2.5 × 10⁻³ eV² and E = 1 GeV, find the first L of maximum oscillation.
T2K sends 0.6 GeV neutrinos 295 km. Compute the phase. Why was that distance chosen?
Why does oscillation prove neutrinos have mass?

topics.title: Sterile neutrinos
topics.goal: A possible fourth neutrino.
checks: I can describe the evidence and its current status.

ex.q: Why would a sterile neutrino be so hard to detect?
ex.a: It feels no force but gravity

ex.q: Which experiments hinted at one, and what have recent results found?
ex.a: LSND and MiniBooNE; MicroBooNE disfavours the simplest version.

topics.title: Parity violation
topics.goal: The weak force tells left from right.
checks: I can explain the Wu experiment.

ex.q: Under a mirror, does spin flip? Does momentum?
Electrons from cobalt-60 come out mostly opposite the nuclear spin. Why does that break mirror symmetry?
ex.a: The mirror image would show the opposite preference

ex.q: Which neutrino handedness exists?

topics.title: CP violation and the matter excess
topics.goal: Why there is more matter than antimatter.
checks: I can state the Sakharov conditions.

ex.q: Name the three conditions.
ex.a: Baryon-number violation; C and CP violation; departure from equilibrium

ex.q: The baryon-to-photon ratio is about 6 × 10⁻¹⁰. Restate it in words.
ex.a: About 1 extra quark per billion pairs

ex.q: Where was CP violation first seen? Is the Standard Model's amount enough?
ex.a: Kaons in 1964; no, far too small.

topics.title: Antimatter
topics.goal: Making and trapping antimatter.
checks: I can estimate annihilation energies.

ex.q: 1 g of antimatter annihilates with 1 g of matter. Find the energy in joules and kilotons of TNT.
What did ALPHA-g find about how antihydrogen falls?
Why are antimatter engines impractical?
ex.a: Production costs vastly exceed the energy returned.

topics.title: Positronium
topics.goal: An atom of an electron and a positron.
checks: I can apply hydrogen physics with a reduced mass.

ex.q: The reduced mass is m_e/2. Find positronium's binding energy and Bohr radius.
Para-positronium decays into 2 photons in 125 ps; ortho-positronium into 3 in 142 ns. Why can't ortho decay into 2?
Where is positronium used in medicine?

topics.title: The Higgs discovery
topics.goal: How the Higgs was found.
checks: I can explain 5σ.

ex.q: What probability does 5σ correspond to?
Which two decay channels were key?
ex.a: Two photons; ZZ to four leptons

ex.q: What is the Higgs mass?

topics.title: Accelerators
topics.goal: Accelerating and colliding particles.
checks: I can compute speeds and fields at the LHC.

ex.q: A 6.8 TeV proton has γ = ? Use 1 − v/c ≈ 1/(2γ²) to find how much slower than light it moves, in m/s.
How many laps of the 26.7 km ring does it make per second?
The bending radius is about 2804 m. What dipole field is needed?

topics.title: Detectors
topics.search: particle detectors cloud chamber bubble chamber
topics.goal: How particles are seen; build your own cloud chamber.
checks: I can read cloud-chamber tracks.

ex.q: Find the radius of a 1 MeV/c electron in 0.1 T.
Describe the tracks of an alpha particle, an electron and a muon.
ex.a: Alpha: short, thick; electron: thin, wiggly; muon: long, straight.

ex.q: Build a cloud chamber with isopropyl alcohol and dry ice, and log the tracks you see in 10 minutes.

topics.title: Muon g − 2
topics.goal: A possible crack in the Standard Model.
checks: I can explain why muons are a sensitive probe.

ex.q: Sensitivity to heavy new particles scales as mass squared. How much more sensitive is the muon than the electron?
What is the current status of the muon g − 2 comparison?
ex.a: The 2025 lattice-based theory agrees with the final measurement.

topics.title: The proton radius puzzle
topics.goal: A puzzle from measuring the proton with muons.
checks: I can explain why muonic hydrogen probes the proton.

ex.q: Compute the reduced mass of muonic hydrogen. How many times the electron's mass is it?
The chance of the lepton being inside the proton scales as 1/a³. By what factor does it grow?
The radii were 0.841 fm versus 0.875 fm. What is the percentage gap, and how was it resolved?
ex.a: About 4%; newer hydrogen measurements favour the smaller radius.

topics.title: The neutron lifetime puzzle
topics.goal: Two methods give different answers.
checks: I can compare the two methods.

ex.q: Bottle experiments give about 878 s; beam experiments about 888 s. What is the percent difference?
What fraction of free neutrons survive 15 minutes?
Give one possible explanation of the discrepancy.
ex.a: Unknown systematics, or an exotic decay channel.

topics.title: Exotic hadrons
topics.goal: Particles beyond simple quark models.
checks: I can find the content and charge of exotic hadrons.

ex.q: LHCb's pentaquark is uud c anti-c. Find its charge.
Why don't glueballs need quarks? Has one been confirmed?
ex.a: They would be made of gluons alone; no.

topics.title: Quark-gluon plasma
topics.goal: The state of matter just after the Big Bang.
checks: I can convert MeV temperatures to kelvin.

ex.q: The transition happens at about 155 MeV. Convert to kelvin (k_B = 8.617 × 10⁻⁵ eV/K).
Compare with the Sun's core at 1.5 × 10⁷ K.
Why is it called a near-perfect liquid?

topics.title: Cosmic rays
topics.goal: The most energetic particle ever detected.
checks: I can compare a cosmic ray with everyday energies.

ex.q: The Oh-My-God particle had 3.2 × 10²⁰ eV. Convert to joules.
How fast would a 145 g baseball need to move for the same energy?
Its collision energy with a resting proton is √(2Em_pc²). Compute it and compare with the LHC's 13.6 TeV.
ex.a: About 780 TeV, about 57 times the LHC

ex.q: What is the GZK limit?
ex.a: About 5 × 10¹⁹ eV, where the CMB stops protons.

topics.title: Dark matter
topics.goal: What dark matter might be made of.
checks: I can estimate the local dark-matter density.

ex.q: The local density is about 0.3 GeV/cm³. How many 100 GeV WIMPs are in a litre?
Flat rotation curves need a constant orbital speed v = √(GM/r). How must M grow with r?
How do WIMPs and axions differ?
ex.a: WIMPs are heavy and weakly interacting; axions are extremely light.

topics.title: Supersymmetry
topics.goal: A proposed symmetry between bosons and fermions.
checks: I can name superpartners and the motivations for them.

ex.q: Name the partners of the electron, quarks, photon and gluon.
Give three motivations for supersymmetry.
What has the LHC found so far?

topics.title: Grand unification
topics.goal: Unifying the three forces.
checks: I can estimate proton-decay rates.

ex.q: Super-K holds about 22.5 kt of water in its inner volume. How many protons is that? (Water is 18 g/mol, 10 protons per molecule.)
If the proton lifetime is 10³⁴ years, how many decays per year?
Why did the simplest SU(5) theory fail?
ex.a: Its proton-decay prediction was ruled out.

topics.title: Magnetic monopoles
topics.goal: Isolated magnetic poles and Dirac's charge quantization argument.
checks: I can state Dirac's argument.

ex.q: If one monopole exists anywhere, what must be true of electric charge?
The Dirac magnetic charge is g = e/(2α). How many times e is that?
What were the Valentine's Day monopole and the monopoles in spin ice?
ex.a: An unrepeated 1982 detector event; emergent magnetic charges in a material.

topics.title: A deep-dive channel
topics.goal: A channel that explains particle physics in depth.
checks: I can explain the Standard Model to a friend.

ex.q: Draw the Standard Model chart from memory, with charges and rough masses. Check it.
Pick one open problem from this part and explain it in two minutes.

parts.name: Quantum Gravity
parts.title: Quantum gravity and cosmology
parts.intro: Nobody knows the final answer here, so the exercises lean on what can be calculated: Planck units, black-hole temperatures and entropies, and the famous mismatch of about 120 orders of magnitude in the cosmological constant. Constants: G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹, ħ = 1.055 × 10⁻³⁴, c = 2.998 × 10⁸, k_B = 1.381 × 10⁻²³ (SI units), M_☉ = 1.989 × 10³⁰ kg.

topics.title: Why quantum gravity is hard
topics.search: why is quantum gravity so hard
topics.goal: Why the usual methods fail for gravity.
checks: I can explain why gravity resists the usual methods.

ex.q: The gravitational coupling between two protons is Gm_p²/(ħc). Compute it and compare with α ≈ 1/137.
ex.a: About 5.9 × 10⁻³⁹, about 10³⁶ times weaker than α

ex.q: Why does gravity's coupling grow with energy, unlike QED's? (See 20.23.)
ex.a: G has units; its dimensionless strength goes as E²

ex.q: Why can't we simply run an experiment at the Planck energy?
ex.a: The energy is about 10¹⁵ times beyond the LHC.

topics.title: Planck units
topics.goal: Scales where quantum gravity matters (about 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m).
checks: I can build the Planck units from G, ħ and c.

ex.q: Compute the Planck length √(ħG/c³) and the Planck time.
Compute the Planck mass √(ħc/G). Compare it with a grain of sand.
ex.a: About 22 μg, roughly a sand grain

ex.q: Express the Planck energy in GeV. How many times the LHC's 13.6 TeV is it?
ex.a: About 1.22 × 10¹⁹ GeV, about 10¹⁵ times the LHC

ex.q: How many Planck lengths fit across a proton (0.84 fm)?

topics.title: Hawking radiation
topics.goal: Black holes glow and slowly evaporate.
checks: I can compute Hawking temperatures and lifetimes.

ex.q: Use T = ħc³/(8πGMk_B) to find T for a one-solar-mass black hole.
Compare it with the CMB at 2.725 K. Is the black hole shrinking or growing today?
ex.a: Colder than the CMB, so it grows

ex.q: What mass of black hole would be exactly as warm as the CMB? Compare it with the Moon (7.3 × 10²² kg).
The lifetime is 5120πG²M³/(ħc⁴). Compute it for one solar mass, in years.
Lifetime goes as M³. Roughly what mass evaporates in the universe's age of 13.8 billion years?

topics.title: QFT in curved spacetime
topics.search: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
topics.goal: The framework behind Hawking and Unruh radiation.
checks: I can link Hawking radiation to the Unruh effect.

ex.q: A black hole's surface gravity is κ = c⁴/(4GM). Put a = κ into the Unruh formula (20.38) and show you recover Hawking's T.
Why don't different observers agree on what counts as "empty" in curved spacetime?
ex.a: Different observers split the field into particles differently.

topics.title: Black-hole entropy
topics.goal: A black hole's entropy grows with its area, not its volume.
checks: I can compute Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.

ex.q: Find the Schwarzschild radius of the Sun's mass.
Compute S/k_B = A/(4ℓ_P²) for that black hole.
The Sun itself has an entropy of about 10⁵⁸ k_B. How many times larger is the black hole's?
What happens to S if the mass doubles?

topics.title: The information paradox
topics.goal: Does information survive evaporation?
checks: I can state the paradox in terms of states.

ex.q: If Hawking radiation is exactly thermal, a pure state turns into a mixed one. Why does that violate unitarity? (See 16.x and 18.25.)
ex.a: Unitary evolution keeps pure states pure

ex.q: Why doesn't burning a book cause the same paradox?
ex.a: The information stays encoded in the smoke and ash.

topics.title: The firewall paradox
topics.goal: A clash between equivalence and unitarity.
checks: I can explain the role of monogamy.

ex.q: Why can't a qubit be maximally entangled with two partners at once?
Which three assumptions clash in the AMPS argument?
ex.a: Unitarity, smooth horizons and valid local physics.

topics.title: The Page curve
topics.search: Page curve and islands black hole
topics.goal: Recent progress on the information paradox.
checks: I can sketch the Page curve.

ex.q: Sketch the radiation's entanglement entropy over time for Hawking's answer and for a unitary answer.
The Page time comes when the black hole's entropy (∝ M²) has halved. What mass is left? What fraction of the lifetime (∝ M³) has passed?
What did the island calculations of 2019 show?
ex.a: Entropy follows the unitary Page curve.

topics.title: The holographic principle
topics.goal: A volume's information fits on its boundary.
checks: I can compute a holographic bound.

ex.q: How many bits can a 1 cm² surface hold, at most? (Use A/(4ℓ_P² ln 2).)
Why can't the information in a region grow with its volume without limit?
ex.a: Too much information collapses into a black hole.

topics.title: AdS/CFT
topics.goal: Gravity in a space equals a quantum theory on its boundary.
checks: I can describe the duality.

ex.q: How many dimensions does the bulk have, compared with the boundary?
Why is a strong-weak duality so useful?
ex.a: Hard calculations become easy on the other side

ex.q: What does AdS/CFT predict for the quark-gluon plasma's η/s? (See 21.26.)

topics.title: ER = EPR
topics.goal: Entanglement and wormholes may be the same thing.
checks: I can explain the conjecture.

ex.q: When were the Einstein-Rosen bridge paper and the EPR paper published?
Why can't these wormholes carry messages faster than light?
ex.a: They're non-traversable without extra effects, and travel through them stays causal.

topics.title: Spacetime from entanglement
topics.goal: Geometry as a pattern of entanglement.
checks: I can explain the Ryu-Takayanagi idea.

ex.q: What happens to the connecting spacetime when you reduce the entanglement between two boundary regions?
What does entanglement entropy equal in Ryu-Takayanagi?
ex.a: The area of a minimal surface divided by 4Għ.

topics.title: String theory
topics.goal: Particles as vibrating strings.
checks: I can say what strings explain.

ex.q: How many dimensions do bosonic and superstring theories need?
Which string vibration is the graviton?
What is the main criticism of string theory?
ex.a: It has no confirmed testable predictions.

topics.title: Extra dimensions
topics.goal: Hidden dimensions curled up small.
checks: I can estimate Kaluza-Klein masses.

ex.q: Extra dimensions curled to radius R give masses m = nħ/(Rc). Find R for a 1 TeV Kaluza-Klein particle.
In 4 space dimensions, gravity falls as 1/r³. By what factor does it drop when distance doubles?
How many dimensions does a Calabi-Yau space have, and why?

topics.title: M-theory and branes
topics.goal: Unifying the string theories.
checks: I can list what M-theory unified.

ex.q: Name the five superstring theories.
ex.a: Type I, IIA, IIB, heterotic SO(32), heterotic E8 × E8

ex.q: How many dimensions does M-theory have? Who proposed it, and when?
What is a D-brane?
ex.a: A surface where open strings end.

topics.title: Loop quantum gravity
topics.goal: Quantized space made of spin networks.
checks: I can describe quantized area.

ex.q: What are the nodes and links of a spin network?
ex.a: Nodes are volume quanta; links are area quanta

ex.q: Areas come in steps of order the Planck area. Why would this remove the singularities of 12.x?
ex.a: A minimum area stops infinite collapse

ex.q: Does LQG unify gravity with the other forces?

topics.title: Causal sets and triangulations
topics.goal: Spacetime built from discrete pieces.
checks: I can describe discrete spacetime approaches.

ex.q: Sorkin predicted Λ ∼ 1/√N, with N ≈ 10²⁴⁰ Planck volumes. What value of Λ is that, in Planck units?
What happens to spacetime's dimension at tiny scales in CDT?

topics.title: Asymptotic safety
topics.goal: Gravity that stays finite at high energy.
checks: I can explain a UV fixed point.

ex.q: What is an ultraviolet fixed point?
ex.a: Couplings stop growing at high energy

ex.q: What did Shaposhnikov and Wetterich predict in 2009?

topics.title: Twistors
topics.goal: Spacetime rebuilt from light rays.
checks: I can state Penrose's idea.

ex.q: In twistor space, what does a light ray become?
Lorentz boosts act on the celestial sphere as Möbius transformations. What does that mean for the night sky seen by a moving observer?
ex.a: Circles on the sky stay circles; only their arrangement shifts.

topics.title: The amplituhedron
topics.goal: A geometric shortcut for particle scattering.
checks: I can explain the shortcut.

ex.q: Two gluons scattering into four take 220 Feynman diagrams. What did Parke and Taylor find?
Which properties of physics does the amplituhedron make emergent rather than built in?

topics.title: The Wheeler-DeWitt equation
topics.goal: An equation of the universe with no time in it.
checks: I can state the problem of time.

ex.q: Write the equation HΨ = 0. Why is there no time in it?
How does the Page-Wootters mechanism recover time?
ex.a: A subsystem's entanglement with a clock.

topics.title: Testing whether gravity is quantum
topics.goal: Tabletop tests of whether gravity is quantum.
checks: I can estimate the entangling phase.

ex.q: Two masses of 10⁻¹⁴ kg sit 200 μm apart for 2.5 s. Compute Δφ = Gm²t/(ħd).
Why would observing entanglement prove gravity is quantum? (Hint: local operations and classical communication can't create entanglement.)
ex.a: A classical field can't create entanglement

ex.q: What makes the experiment so hard?
ex.a: Isolating such masses from all other noise.

topics.title: Inflation
topics.goal: Quantum jitters seeded today's galaxies.
checks: I can explain the horizon problem and seeding.

ex.q: Inflation needs about 60 e-folds. What growth factor is that?
The CMB is uniform to about 1 part in 10⁵. Why is that a puzzle without inflation?
ex.a: The regions were never in contact

ex.q: How did quantum fluctuations become galaxies?
ex.a: Inflation stretched them into density variations.

topics.title: The cosmological constant problem
topics.goal: Prediction and observation differ by about 120 powers of ten.
checks: I can compute the 120-orders mismatch.

ex.q: The naive vacuum energy is the Planck energy per Planck volume. Compute it in J/m³.
Find the critical density 3H²/(8πG) with H₀ = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹, convert to J/m³, and take 69% as dark energy.
Compute the ratio.

topics.title: False vacuum decay
topics.goal: Our vacuum might not be the most stable one.
checks: I can explain metastability.

ex.q: Which two masses decide whether our vacuum is stable?
ex.a: The Higgs (125 GeV) and the top quark (173 GeV)

ex.q: Why would we get no warning if a bubble formed?
ex.a: The bubble expands at nearly c

ex.q: Should you worry? Explain using the estimated lifetime.
ex.a: No; the lifetime far exceeds the universe's age.

topics.title: Eternal inflation
topics.goal: Inflation that never ends everywhere.
checks: I can show why inflation never fully ends.

ex.q: Each step, the inflating volume grows 20 times and half of it decays into bubble universes. How does the inflating volume change per step?
What is the measure problem?

topics.title: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
topics.goal: How the first elements formed in about 3 minutes.
checks: I can predict the helium fraction.

ex.q: At freeze-out, n/p = e^(−Δm/kT) with Δm = 1.293 MeV and kT ≈ 0.72 MeV. Compute it.
After neutron decay, n/p falls to about 1/7. Show the helium mass fraction is Y = 2(n/p)/(1 + n/p) ≈ 0.25.
What is the lithium problem?
ex.a: Predicted lithium-7 is about 3 times too high.

topics.title: Boltzmann brains
topics.goal: A paradox for cosmological theories.
checks: I can state the paradox.

ex.q: The chance of a fluctuation goes as e^(−ΔS/k_B). Why are small fluctuations, such as a lone brain, vastly more likely than a whole universe?
ex.a: A smaller entropy drop is exponentially more likely

ex.q: Why does that count against a theory?
ex.a: It predicts that we're most likely fluctuating brains.

topics.title: A skeptic's overview
topics.goal: A skeptic's overview of the field.
checks: I can compare approaches by their testability.

ex.q: For string theory, LQG, asymptotic safety and causal sets, name one possible experimental test each.
Write your own one-paragraph verdict on the state of the field.

parts.name: Strange Phenomena
parts.title: Strange phenomena and quantum technology
parts.intro: This is the obscure-topics part, where helium and buckyballs live. Almost every entry has a real number to compute: the size of a giant atom, the height of the first quantum bounce of a neutron, the magnetic field needed to make empty space birefringent.

topics.title: The Casimir effect
topics.goal: Two metal plates in a vacuum attract (needs Part 20).
checks: I can compute Casimir forces on real plates.

ex.q: Use π²ħc/(240d⁴) (20.16) to find the pressure at 100 nm and the force on a 1 cm² plate.
By what factor does the force grow when the gap halves?
Can the Casimir force be repulsive? When?
ex.a: Yes, in fluids with suitable dielectric properties.

topics.title: The dynamical Casimir effect
topics.goal: Moving mirrors create photons from nothing.
checks: I can explain photons from a moving mirror.

ex.q: The 2011 experiment modulated a SQUID at 10 GHz. Photons appeared in pairs around what frequency?
Why can't a real metal mirror be shaken fast enough?
ex.a: It must move near light speed.

topics.title: Vacuum birefringence
topics.goal: Empty space bends light in strong magnetic fields.
checks: I can compute the critical magnetic field.

ex.q: Compute B_c = m²c²/(eħ). How does it relate to E_c from 20.37?
Magnetars reach 10¹⁰ to 10¹¹ T. Why are they the natural laboratory?
What did the 2016 polarization study of a neutron star find?

topics.title: How long tunneling takes
topics.search: how long does quantum tunneling take experiment
topics.goal: Measuring tunneling time with atoms.
checks: I can compute tunneling probabilities.

ex.q: An electron faces a barrier 1 eV above its energy and 1 nm wide. Compute κ = √(2m(V − E))/ħ and T ≈ e^(−2κL).
What happens to T when the barrier is twice as wide?
What did Steinberg's Larmor-clock experiment measure for rubidium atoms?

topics.title: The Hartman effect
topics.goal: Tunneling time that stops growing with barrier width.
checks: I can explain why it doesn't break relativity.

ex.q: If the delay stops growing with width L, what happens to L/τ for wide barriers?
Why can't this send a signal faster than light?
ex.a: The pulse is reshaped and tiny; the front never beats c.

topics.title: Time crystals
topics.goal: Matter that repeats in time instead of space.
checks: I can describe period doubling.

ex.q: A discrete time crystal is driven at 20 kHz. At what frequency does it respond?
Why is this not a perpetual-motion machine?
Why can't a ground-state time crystal exist?
ex.a: A no-go theorem rules out ground-state time crystals.

topics.title: Supersolids
topics.goal: A solid that also flows like a superfluid.
checks: I can describe supersolids and their history.

ex.q: Which atoms made the 2019 supersolids?
What happened to the 2004 claim for solid helium?

topics.title: Efimov states
topics.goal: Endless three-body bound states that two bodies can't form.
checks: I can use the Efimov scaling factor.

ex.q: Each Efimov state is 22.7 times larger than the last. The first is 100 nm across. How large is the third?
Binding energies shrink by 22.7² per step. What is the energy ratio between the first and third states?
When and in which atoms were Efimov states first seen?

topics.title: Rydberg atoms
topics.goal: Atoms swollen to near-visible sizes.
checks: I can compute Rydberg-atom sizes.

ex.q: The radius is n²a₀ with a₀ = 0.0529 nm. Compute it for n = 100.
Which n gives an atom 1 μm across? Does the number look familiar?
Compute the binding energy at n = 100.
How does the Rydberg blockade make quantum gates?
ex.a: One excited atom blocks its neighbour's excitation.

topics.title: Ammonia inversion and the maser
topics.goal: A molecule tunneling between two shapes, used in the first maser.
checks: I can treat ammonia as a two-state system.

ex.q: The inversion line is at 23.87 GHz. Find its wavelength and energy in eV.
How long does the molecule take to flip from one shape to the other?
Heavier ND₃ inverts at 1.6 GHz. Why is it slower?
Who built the first maser, and when?

topics.title: Wigner crystals
topics.goal: Electrons freezing into a lattice.
checks: I can explain why low density favours a crystal.

ex.q: Kinetic energy scales as 1/r² and Coulomb energy as 1/r. Which wins at large spacing?
When was a Wigner crystal first imaged directly?

topics.title: Majorana fermions
topics.goal: Particles that are their own antiparticles.
checks: I can build an ordinary fermion from two Majoranas.

ex.q: Write c = (γ₁ + iγ₂)/2. What property does each γ have?
ex.a: Each γ is its own antiparticle

ex.q: Which experiment could show that neutrinos are Majorana particles?
What is the status of Majorana-based qubits?

topics.title: Non-abelian anyons
topics.goal: Particles whose swaps store memory.
checks: I can count fusion states.

ex.q: What do bosons, fermions, abelian anyons and non-abelian anyons pick up when two are swapped?
Fibonacci anyons obey τ × τ = 1 + τ. Count the ways 2, 3, 4 and 5 τ's can fuse to the vacuum. Which sequence appears?
How many states do 10 τ's have?
Which number governs the growth?

topics.title: Magnetic skyrmions
topics.goal: Knots of magnetization.
checks: I can explain topological protection.

ex.q: Why can't a skyrmion unwind smoothly?
What did Skyrme originally invent the idea for?
Why are skyrmions attractive for data storage?

topics.title: Quantum chaos and scars
topics.goal: What chaos means for quantum systems.
checks: I can tell chaotic from regular spectra.

ex.q: Which level-spacing statistics do regular and chaotic systems show?
What is a quantum scar?
ex.a: Extra probability along unstable classical orbits.

topics.title: Floquet systems
topics.goal: New phases from shaking a system.
checks: I can apply Floquet's theorem.

ex.q: What is Floquet's theorem the time version of?
Drive at 1 GHz. How wide is the quasienergy zone, in μeV?
How does the Kapitza pendulum show that shaking can create new stable states?

topics.title: The Hofstadter butterfly
topics.goal: A fractal energy spectrum from a magnetic field.
checks: I can estimate the field needed.

ex.q: One flux quantum (h/e) per cell needs B = (h/e)/a². Compute B for a = 0.25 nm.
Compute B for a 14 nm moiré superlattice.
A flux ratio of p/q splits the band into how many bands?

topics.title: Quantum spin liquids
topics.goal: Magnets that never order, even at absolute zero.
checks: I can explain frustration.

ex.q: Three Ising spins sit on a triangle with antiferromagnetic coupling. How many of the 8 states are ground states?
Pauling's ice entropy is R ln(3/2) per mole. Compute it.
Name a candidate spin-liquid material.

topics.title: Many-body localization
topics.goal: Systems that refuse to reach thermal equilibrium.
checks: I can describe a system that doesn't thermalize.

ex.q: What do MBL systems remember that thermal systems forget?
How does entanglement scale in MBL eigenstates and in thermal ones?

topics.title: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis
topics.goal: How isolated quantum systems still thermalize.
checks: I can explain thermalization under unitary evolution.

ex.q: How many states do 50 spins have?
How can a pure state look thermal to local measurements? (See 18.25.)
ex.a: Entanglement hides the information from local measurements.

topics.title: The Bosenova
topics.goal: A BEC that implodes and explodes.
checks: I can estimate the collapse threshold.

ex.q: The critical number is N_c ≈ 0.574 × a_ho/∣a∣. Find N_c for a_ho = 1 μm and a = −1 nm.
How were the interactions made attractive? (See 23.22.)

topics.title: The atom laser
topics.goal: A coherent beam of atoms from a BEC.
checks: I can compute the de Broglie wavelength of falling atoms.

ex.q: Rubidium-87 atoms fall 1 cm from rest. Find their speed and de Broglie wavelength.
Who built the first atom laser, and when?

topics.title: Feshbach resonances
topics.goal: Tuning how strongly atoms interact.
checks: I can use the resonance formula.

ex.q: a(B) = a_bg(1 − Δ/(B − B₀)) with a_bg = 100a₀ and Δ = 1 G. Find a at B − B₀ = 2 G, 1 G and 0.5 G.
What happens as B → B₀?
Which crossover does this let experiments explore? (See 17.x.)

topics.title: Quantum reflection
topics.goal: Atoms bouncing off an attractive potential.
checks: I can explain reflection from an attractive potential.

ex.q: Would a classical ball rolling into a valley ever bounce back?
Why does reflection grow as atoms slow down?
ex.a: Their wavelength grows, so the potential looks abrupt.

topics.title: Buckyball interference
topics.search: buckyball double slit interference Zeilinger C60
topics.goal: 60-atom molecules show wave interference.
checks: I can compute molecular de Broglie wavelengths.

ex.q: C₆₀ (720 u) flew at 220 m/s. Compute its wavelength.
Compare it with the molecule's 1 nm size.
Find the diffraction angle from a 100 nm grating.
Why did heating the molecules destroy the pattern? (See 16.29.)
What is the current mass record?

topics.title: Macroscopic superpositions
topics.goal: A visible object in a quantum state.
checks: I can compute thermal occupation.

ex.q: The occupation is n = 1/(e^(hf/kT) − 1). Compute it for 6 GHz at 25 mK.
Compute it for 1 MHz at 25 mK. What extra step is needed?
What was put in a cat state in 2023?

topics.title: Cat states in circuits
topics.goal: Cat states made in the lab.
checks: I can quantify a cat's size.

ex.q: The overlap of coherent states ∣α⟩ and ∣−α⟩ is e^(−4α²) for real α. Compute it for α² = 4 photons.
How many photons did the 2013 Yale cat contain?
Why do cat qubits resist bit flips?
ex.a: Flips need jumps across phase space.

topics.title: The 4π rotation
topics.goal: Experimental proof that 360° flips the sign of a spinor.
checks: I can predict spinor interference.

ex.q: Show e^(−iθσ/2) = −1 at θ = 2π.
Interference goes as 1 + cos(θ/2). Where are its minima and maxima?
Neutrons precess at γ = 1.83 × 10⁸ rad/(s·T). How long does a 2π turn take in 1 mT, and how far does a 2000 m/s neutron travel meanwhile?

topics.title: Neutrons in Earth's gravity
topics.search: quantum states of neutrons in Earth's gravity
topics.goal: Neutrons bouncing in quantized gravity levels.
checks: I can compute quantum bounce levels.

ex.q: The levels are Eₙ = (ħ²mg²/2)^(1/3)aₙ, with a₁ = 2.338. Compute E₁ in peV.
Find the classical height E₁/(mg).
Where and when was this seen?

topics.title: Photon antibunching
topics.goal: Light that arrives one photon at a time.
checks: I can compare g⁽²⁾(0) for different kinds of light.

ex.q: Give g⁽²⁾(0) for an ideal single-photon source, a laser and thermal light.
A Fock state has g⁽²⁾(0) = 1 − 1/n. Compute it for n = 1 and n = 2.
Why does g⁽²⁾(0) < 1 prove light comes in photons?

topics.title: Electron spin resonance
topics.goal: Flipping electron spins with microwaves.
checks: I can find resonance fields.

ex.q: ESR runs at about 28.0 GHz/T (20.6). Which field matches a 9.5 GHz spectrometer?
Protons resonate at 42.58 MHz/T. What is the electron-to-proton ratio?
What frequency does MRI use at 1.5 T?

topics.title: The Hanbury Brown-Twiss effect
topics.goal: Correlations that measure star sizes and reveal bosons.
checks: I can explain bunching and antibunching of particles.

ex.q: Sirius is about 6 milliarcseconds wide. Which baseline resolves it at 420 nm?
In a 2007 experiment, helium-4 bunched and helium-3 antibunched. Why? (See the helium video in Part 17.)

topics.title: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion
topics.goal: How entangled photons are made.
checks: I can apply energy conservation to SPDC.

ex.q: A 405 nm pump splits evenly. What wavelength is each photon?
If one photon is at 780 nm, where is the other?
Why is SPDC so inefficient?

topics.title: Ghost imaging
topics.goal: Imaging with photons that never touched the object.
checks: I can explain where the image comes from.

ex.q: The bucket detector has no spatial resolution. Where does the image come from?
ex.a: Coincidences with a camera on the partner photons

ex.q: What is special about imaging with undetected photons?
ex.a: The detected photons never touched the object.

topics.title: The Purcell effect
topics.goal: Changing how fast atoms emit by changing their surroundings.
checks: I can compute a Purcell factor.

ex.q: F = (3/4π²)(λ/n)³(Q/V). Compute F for Q = 10⁴, V = λ³ and n = 1.
A 10 ns lifetime becomes what?
How can emission be suppressed instead?

topics.title: Superradiance
topics.goal: Atoms emitting together, far faster.
checks: I can scale superradiant bursts.

ex.q: For N = 1000 atoms, how do peak intensity and pulse length compare with a single atom?
Show that the total energy is still N photons.
What is subradiance?

topics.title: Cherenkov radiation
topics.goal: Particles faster than light in water.
checks: I can compute thresholds and angles.

ex.q: Water has n = 1.33. What is the threshold β? What electron kinetic energy is that?
Find the cone angle for β → 1.
Why is the glow blue?
Which detector in 21.30 uses it?

topics.title: Sonoluminescence
topics.goal: Collapsing bubbles that flash light (still debated).
checks: I can estimate collapse temperatures.

ex.q: An argon bubble (γ = 5/3) at 300 K shrinks to a tenth of its radius adiabatically. Use TV^(γ−1) = constant to find the final temperature.
Which animal makes flashes with collapsing bubbles?
Which part of the mechanism is still debated?
ex.a: Exactly how the light is produced.

topics.title: The Kapitza-Dirac effect
topics.goal: Electrons diffracted by a standing light wave.
checks: I can compute electron diffraction from light.

ex.q: A standing 532 nm wave forms a grating with what period?
380 eV electrons have λ = 1.226/√V nm. Compute λ and the diffraction angle.
When was this effect predicted, and when was it observed?

topics.title: Atomic clocks
topics.goal: Timekeeping from atomic transitions.
checks: I can compute clock sensitivities.

ex.q: Which frequency defines the second?
The gravitational shift is gh/c². Compute it for 1 cm.
A clock good to 10⁻¹⁸ drifts 1 s in how many years?
How large is GPS's relativistic correction per day?

topics.title: The kilogram redefinition
topics.search: kilogram redefinition Kibble balance Planck constant Veritasium
topics.goal: The SI now rests on h and quantum effects.
checks: I can compute the quantum electrical constants.

ex.q: Compute K_J = 2e/h with e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and h = 6.62607015 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s.
Compute R_K = h/e².
Write the Kibble balance relation mgv = UI. Why does it tie mass to h?
ex.a: U and I come from Josephson and quantum Hall standards

ex.q: When did the new SI take effect, and what was wrong with the old prototype?
ex.a: 2019; the prototype drifted by tens of micrograms.

topics.title: Optical tweezers
topics.goal: Holding particles with light.
checks: I can estimate optical forces.

ex.q: 10 mW of light is absorbed. Find the force P/c in piconewtons.
Compare it with a kinesin motor's 6 pN and with the weight of a 1 μm bead (density 1050 kg/m³).
ex.a: Larger than the motor; the bead weighs about 5 fN

ex.q: Who won the 2018 Nobel Prize for this?

topics.title: Squeezed light
topics.goal: Beating the quantum noise limit.
checks: I can convert squeezing into detector reach.

ex.q: Is 3 dB a factor of 2 in power or in amplitude?
Noise amplitude drops by √2. By what factor does LIGO's reach grow? Its observable volume?
A strain of 10⁻²¹ over 4 km is what length change? Compare it with a proton.
ex.a: About 4 × 10⁻¹⁸ m, a few thousandths of a proton.

topics.title: NV centres
topics.goal: Defects in diamond as quantum sensors.
checks: I can convert NV frequency shifts into fields.

ex.q: The splitting is 2.87 GHz at zero field and shifts by 28 MHz/mT. Which field causes a 2.8 MHz shift?
How big is the shift from Earth's 50 μT?
Why is room-temperature operation such an advantage?

topics.title: The electron EDM
topics.goal: Testing for new physics through electron shape.
checks: I can explain why an EDM breaks time symmetry.

ex.q: Under T, spin flips but an EDM along it doesn't. Why does that violate T, and hence CP? (See 20.31.)
ex.a: The relation between d and spin reverses

ex.q: The 2023 limit is 4.1 × 10⁻³⁰ e·cm; the Standard Model predicts far less than 10⁻³⁵. Why would any detection be big news?
Why are molecules such as HfF⁺ used?

topics.title: A photon BEC
topics.goal: Condensing light itself.
checks: I can explain what lets light condense.

ex.q: Why don't photons in a blackbody condense?
Which two things did the dye-filled microcavity supply?
ex.a: A conserved photon number and an effective mass.

topics.title: A magnon BEC
topics.goal: A condensate of spin waves at room temperature.
checks: I can describe condensing quasiparticles.

ex.q: Are magnons bosons or fermions? How do you know?
What made a room-temperature magnon BEC possible in 2006?

parts.name: Quantum Biology
parts.title: Biology and quantum biology
parts.intro: The last part starts from what a cell is and ends with the open quantum-biology questions. Biology runs at body temperature, about 310 K, so k_BT ≈ 0.027 eV, and you'll keep comparing quantum energies against it. Useful tools: E (eV) = 1240/λ (nm), and F = 96,485 C/mol.

topics.title: The cell
topics.goal: Membrane, nucleus, organelles.
checks: I can name the main organelles and give typical sizes.

ex.q: How many 10 μm cells fit side by side across 1 mm?
An E. coli cell holds about 1 μm³ (10⁻¹⁵ L). What concentration is one molecule inside it, in nanomolar?
Match each to its job: mitochondrion, ribosome, nucleus, membrane.
ex.a: Energy; protein synthesis; DNA storage; boundary.

topics.title: Proteins and folding
topics.goal: Amino acid chains folding into working shapes.
checks: I can explain the Levinthal paradox.

ex.q: How many standard amino acids are there?
A 100-residue chain has 3 shapes per residue. How many conformations is that? At 10¹³ tries per second, how long would a random search take?
Real proteins fold in milliseconds. What resolves the paradox?
What did AlphaFold achieve?
ex.a: Accurate structure prediction; the 2024 Nobel Prize.

topics.title: Enzymes
topics.goal: Enzymes lower activation energy.
checks: I can use the Arrhenius factor.

ex.q: An enzyme lowers the activation energy by 20 kJ/mol at 310 K. By what factor does the rate rise? Use e^(ΔEₐ/RT).
With Eₐ = 50 kJ/mol, by what factor does the rate rise from 300 K to 310 K?
How does tunneling (24.14) add a way around the barrier?

topics.title: DNA
topics.goal: Base pairs held by hydrogen bonds.
checks: I can do DNA arithmetic.

ex.q: Write the strand that pairs with ATGCGT.
How many hydrogen bonds do A-T and G-C pairs have?
The human genome has about 3.1 × 10⁹ base pairs at 0.34 nm each. How long is one copy stretched out?
At 2 bits per base, how many megabytes is one copy?

topics.title: Mutations
topics.goal: How DNA changes.
checks: I can classify mutations.

ex.q: How many codons exist? Why can some mutations be silent?
ex.a: 64; many codons code for the same amino acid

ex.q: A diploid genome has about 6.2 × 10⁹ bp, and the error rate after proofreading is about 10⁻¹⁰ per bp. How many errors occur per division?
Name three kinds of point mutation.

topics.title: Photosynthesis
topics.goal: Capturing light energy in chlorophyll.
checks: I can compute photosynthetic efficiency.

ex.q: Why are leaves green?
ex.a: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue and reflects green

ex.q: Find the energy of a 680 nm photon in eV and in kJ per mole of photons.
Making one glucose (2870 kJ/mol) takes about 48 photons. What is the maximum efficiency at 680 nm?

topics.title: The electron transport chain
topics.goal: Electrons moved step by step to make ATP.
checks: I can compute the free energy of electron transport.

ex.q: Electrons drop 1.14 V from NADH to O₂. Use ΔG = −nFΔE with n = 2.
Electron tunneling slows about tenfold for every 1.7 Å of extra distance. How much slower is a hop 10 Å longer?
Which rotary motor makes ATP?

topics.title: ATP
topics.search: ATP energy currency of the cell
topics.goal: How cells store and spend energy.
checks: I can estimate ATP turnover.

ex.q: ATP releases about 50 kJ/mol in the cell. Convert to eV per molecule and compare with k_BT.
You burn 2000 kcal (8368 kJ) a day. If it all passes through ATP, how many moles is that? How many kilograms (507 g/mol)?
ex.a: About 167 mol, about 85 kg, roughly your body weight

ex.q: Why does the cell recycle ATP instead of storing it?
ex.a: It is unstable and heavy to store.

topics.title: Neurons
topics.goal: Electrical signals in the brain.
checks: I can use the Nernst equation.

ex.q: E = (RT/zF)ln(c_out/c_in). At 310 K, compute E for K⁺ (5 mM outside, 140 mM inside).
Compute E for Na⁺ (145 mM outside, 12 mM inside).
A signal travels 1.8 m at 60 m/s. How long does it take?

topics.title: How the eye detects light
topics.search: how the eye detects light rhodopsin
topics.goal: A single molecule changing shape when it absorbs light.
checks: I can describe rhodopsin's photoreaction.

ex.q: What happens to retinal when it absorbs light, and how fast?
ex.a: It switches from 11-cis to all-trans in about 200 fs

ex.q: Find the photon energy at rhodopsin's 500 nm peak.
Why does such a fast reaction need a quantum description?
ex.a: It passes through a conical intersection.

topics.title: UV and DNA damage
topics.search: UV light DNA damage photon energy
topics.goal: Why UV photons break bonds and visible photons do not.
checks: I can compare photon energies with bond energies.

ex.q: Compute the photon energy at 254, 300 and 550 nm.
A C–C bond is about 3.6 eV. Which photons can break it?
Why can't a bright red lamp give you sunburn? (See 14.x.)
ex.a: Each red photon carries too little energy

ex.q: What lesion does UV cause in DNA?

topics.title: How birds navigate
topics.search: how birds navigate magnetic field migration
topics.goal: The biological puzzle behind the quantum compass.
checks: I can explain why the compass is a puzzle.

ex.q: Compute μ_BB for Earth's 50 μT and compare it with k_BT at 310 K.
ex.a: About 4.6 × 10⁻²⁸ J against 4.3 × 10⁻²¹ J, a ratio of about 10⁻⁷

ex.q: What does that ratio say about any equilibrium explanation?
Weak radio noise disrupted robins in a 2014 study. Why does that point to spin physics?
ex.a: Megahertz noise matches spin precession frequencies.

topics.title: The quantum-biology overview
topics.goal: Overview of where quantum effects may matter in life.
checks: I can sort claims by strength of evidence.

ex.q: List every claimed quantum effect in the talk. Rate each as established, likely, or speculative.

topics.title: Coherence in photosynthesis
topics.search: quantum coherence in photosynthesis FMO complex
topics.goal: Energy transfer claims and the later debate about them.
checks: I can describe the FMO debate.

ex.q: A random walk spreads as √t and a quantum walk as t. After 100 steps, roughly how far does each get?
What did the 2007 experiment claim, and what did later work conclude?
ex.a: Long-lived coherence; later work found mostly vibrational or short-lived coherence.

topics.title: The radical-pair compass
topics.search: radical pair mechanism cryptochrome quantum compass
topics.goal: Entangled electron spins in a bird's eye.
checks: I can link the compass to entangled spins.

ex.q: Write the singlet state of two electrons. Which Bell state is it? (See 18.4.)
Electrons precess at 28 GHz/T. Find the frequency and period in a 50 μT field.
How long must the pair stay coherent?
Which protein is the leading candidate?

topics.title: Proton tunneling in enzymes
topics.goal: Enzymes may use tunneling to speed reactions.
checks: I can estimate isotope effects.

ex.q: A proton tunnels with probability 10⁻⁶. The exponent scales as √m. Estimate the deuteron's probability and the ratio.
Why do electrons tunnel so much more easily than protons?
Classical isotope effects stay below about 7. What does a measured 80 suggest?

topics.title: Tunneling and DNA mutations
topics.goal: Protons hopping between base pairs.
checks: I can state Löwdin's idea.

ex.q: How could double proton transfer in a G-C pair cause a mutation?
Suppose 10⁻⁹ of pairs sit in a tautomeric form at replication. How many is that per 6.2 × 10⁹ bp genome?
What did 2022 simulations suggest about these tautomers?
ex.a: They form but usually revert quickly.

topics.title: The vibration theory of smell
topics.search: vibration theory of smell Luca Turin
topics.goal: A controversial quantum theory of smell.
checks: I can compute vibrational energies.

ex.q: A C–H stretch is about 2900 cm⁻¹. Convert to eV (1 cm⁻¹ = 1.24 × 10⁻⁴ eV).
Deuterium roughly doubles the reduced mass. Estimate the C–D frequency.
What did fruit-fly and human experiments find?
ex.a: Flies distinguish them; human results are mixed.

topics.title: Seeing single photons
topics.search: can humans see a single photon
topics.goal: Rod cells respond to individual photons.
checks: I can apply Poisson statistics to vision.

ex.q: A flash delivers a mean of 1 absorbed photon. Find P(0) and P(at least 1).
Repeat for a mean of 6.
What did the 2016 single-photon study find?

topics.title: Is the brain quantum?
topics.search: is the brain quantum decoherence Tegmark
topics.goal: Why most physicists doubt quantum effects in thought.
checks: I can argue the decoherence case.

ex.q: Compute the thermal de Broglie wavelength h/√(2πmk_BT) for a water molecule at 310 K.
Compare it with the 0.3 nm spacing between molecules. What does that mean?
ex.a: Much smaller, so molecules behave classically

ex.q: Recall Tegmark's numbers from 19.30.

topics.title: Posner molecules
topics.search: Posner molecules Matthew Fisher quantum cognition
topics.goal: A speculative proposal for quantum memory in the brain.
checks: I can state Fisher's proposal.

ex.q: A Posner molecule is Ca₉(PO₄)₆. How many phosphorus-31 spins does it hold?
Why would nuclear spins keep coherence far longer than electron spins?
ex.a: Weak magnetic moments couple weakly to noise

ex.q: What lithium-isotope result inspired the idea?
ex.a: Rats responded differently to lithium-6 and lithium-7.

topics.title: MRI
topics.goal: Spin physics used in medicine.
checks: I can compute MRI frequencies and polarization.

ex.q: Find the proton frequency at 3 T, using 42.58 MHz/T.
The excess spin fraction is about hf/(2k_BT). Compute it at 3 T and 310 K.
How many net aligned protons does 1 mL of water hold?

topics.title: PET scans
topics.goal: Positrons used to image the body.
checks: I can apply half-life and annihilation physics.

ex.q: F-18 has a half-life of 110 minutes. What fraction remains after 4 hours?
What does annihilation emit? (See 20.18b.)
ex.a: Two 511 keV photons back to back

ex.q: A time-of-flight scanner resolves 300 ps. What position resolution along the line is that?

topics.title: Green fluorescent protein
topics.search: green fluorescent protein how it glows
topics.goal: Quantum light emission used throughout biology.
checks: I can compute Stokes shifts.

ex.q: GFP absorbs at 395 nm and 475 nm and emits at 509 nm. How much energy is lost in each case?
Why is emitted light always lower in energy?
Who shared the 2008 Nobel Prize for GFP?
